author: Austin_Federa
quoted_text:
THE DIAMOND COMPUTER 

SAXON Q: Quantum Computing in a Diamond, at Room Temperature

Most quantum computers still live behind a lab door and a dilution refrigerator. SAXON Q, a Leipzig spin-out from Universität Leipzig, sells a different machine: a diamond-chip processor that runs at ordinary room temperature, plugs into a wall outlet, and is meant to sit in a server rack or a wheeled cabinet.

Founded in 2021 as SaxonQ GmbH and now branded SAXON Q, the company grew out of work at Leipzig University’s Felix Bloch Institute by Marius Grundmann and ion-implantation specialist Jan Meijer, with Bernd Burchard on intellectual property. Their bet is that a solid-state defect in diamond can stay usable without millikelvin cooling.

How the qubit works

The hardware uses nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamond. Implant a nitrogen atom in place of one carbon atom and leave a neighboring site empty. The electron trapped at that defect becomes a spin that lasers and microwaves can initialize, drive, and read out. The stiff carbon lattice keeps the defect working at about 293 K—no vacuum chamber, no cryostat.

The NV electron is also an interface to nearby nuclear spins: the defect’s own nitrogen-14 nucleus and carbon-13 nuclei in the lattice. Those nuclei hold quantum states far longer than the electron. In a September 2026 experiment with Fraunhofer IWU, the calculation qubits were three of those nuclear spins; the electron was only the optical port.

Control uses deterministic nitrogen implantation at roughly 3-nanometer precision, thermal annealing so vacancies pair with nitrogen, and transparent nanowiring for electrical readout. SAXON Q argues those steps can ride ordinary semiconductor process flows.

The manufacturing fix

NV centers have been studied for decades. The bottleneck was yield. Conventional implantation typically turns only 1 to 10 percent of implanted nitrogen atoms into working, negatively charged qubits—too sparse to tile a chip.

SAXON Q’s patented answer is sulfur co-implantation. Sulfur acts as a donor that helps keep NV centers in the charged state they need, and the company says conversion yield rises above 85 percent. It claims more than 220 patents and pending applications.

Reported single-qubit fidelities are 99.92 percent in product materials, with later internal figures of 99.98 percent peak and about 99.90 percent average on the Grover run. Two-qubit numbers are thinner: that experiment quoted three-qubit subspace gate fidelities averaging 95.7 percent. Independent full-stack benchmarks on the 128-qubit class machines are still scarce.

What “128 qubits” means

The SXQ128 is 128 physical NV qubits across 16 cores, with eight fully entangled qubits per core. The planned SXQ512 is 32 cores of 16 entangled qubits each. Coherent computation is still a per-core problem. A multi-core operating system is supposed to coordinate work across cores, and the boxes are modular so customers can add chips later. That is closer to a cluster of small high-quality processors than one fully connected 128-qubit register.

Products

- SXQ4 — four-qubit mobile systems delivered 2023–2025 to DLR in Ulm and Fraunhofer IWU in Dresden; reachable on-site and by cloud API.
- SXQ128 — 128 physical qubits; orders opened in 2026 with a stated three-month delivery window.
- SXQ512 — 512 physical qubits; deliveries slated for Q2 2027.
- SXQ10k — roadmap after 2030: an embeddable chip targeting 10,000-plus qubits.

1 of 2

quoted_text:
Salesforce acquires Listen Labs for ~$2b. But who gets the 💰? My usual breakdown below 👇

The company was founded in Sep-23 and had raised less than $100m. Investors will share ~$850m of profits on $96m invested, a ~10x blended.

From a huge pivot to a unicorn valuation term sheet they refused, this is truly a wild story ✍️. In the end an incredible outcome for all involved.

So let's dive in!

1) The boldest move: walking away from $1.5b 🎲

Listen Labs had a signed $125m Series C term sheet from Menlo at a $1.5b valuation... and walked away from it to sell to Salesforce at ~$2b.

This takes a huge amount of courage: few founders turn down a signed unicorn-plus round. @itsalfredw and @florian_jue did it 2.5 years after founding.

Huge congratulations are in order for the discipline and execution of the founders here.

2) Founders and team: a life-changing outcome in under 3 years 🥳

By my best estimates, founders and team still own over half the company.

At $2b, that's ~$1.1b for them to share. Specifically, assuming a 15% option pool, that is ~$300m for the team and ~$750m for the two co-founders.

And, as was the case with Hugging Face, this is all from a pivot. They originally built an AI customer-interview tool to understand why their viral app BeFake was growing, then realised the tool was the business!

3) Sequoia's Bryan Schreier did it again 👑

What few people know is that Bryan was an early backer of Qualtrics... the category Listen Labs is disrupting.

Now he led both the seed and the Series A here. By my estimates, those two rounds will return ~$670m combined, or ~25x on ~$27m invested, in under three years.

Pattern recognition and industry knowledge have their perks, it would seem!

4) Ribbit: 4x in 8 months ⚡

Ribbit led the $69m Series B in Jan-26 at ~$500m. At $2b, that's ~4x in 8 months. Unbelievable IRR and a great return on a meaningful cheque.

5) Neo does it again, congrats @apartovi 🎯

Listen Labs went through the Neo accelerator early on, which came with a $600k SAFE. On my estimates, that cheque is worth ~$25m+ today.

This comes just three months after Cursor's acquisition (a cool >1,000x for Neo). What a hit rate!

This one is very straightforward: it is a massive win for everyone. And so congratulations to all involved: Sequoia, Ribbit, Conviction, Pear, Neo and the team!

text:
跑会的这个话题真的是每次大会都会说一次，我的观点始终保持一致，如果没有具体的业务，如果不是抱着过来玩的心态，如果没有小伙伴再一起，跑会大可不必。

这一轮的跑会应该是从四月香港开始的吧，然后就是七月的日本，八月的香港，九月的台北，十月的韩国和新加坡，十一月的曼谷，结束。

从人数来说，两次香港虽然人并不很多，但如果准备是社交的话真的是足够了，而且从内地到香港不论是时间还是费用相比都是很低的，甚至有些小伙伴都是白天在香港，晚上住深圳，费用会更低。

日本和韩国，相对来说对于想要进军日韩市场的项目方肯定是不会错过的，但日韩的市场过于保守了，想要在这两个国家取得成绩需要交非常高的学费，我亲眼见过很多一腔热血的项目方被一些当地的“大哥”骗得团团转。

而对于 KOL 来说，日韩除非是项目方报销，否则获得得信息资源和所谓得人脉资源并不会高于香港，尤其是日韩主力语言并不是英语，而且很多小伙伴英语也不够好，这种情况下跑会更多的就是纯玩了。

台北很好，真的很棒，主要是语言通畅的情况下可以和当地的小伙伴沟通，可以学到很多当地有用的知识，认识更多当地的小伙伴，只是台北的签证不是很容易，但这些跑会中，我是觉得台北是仅次于香港可以有有效社交的地方。

新加坡是最大的 Token 2049 活动，又有 F1 ，本身成本就很高的地区更是雪上加霜，怎么说呢，来新加坡是一种对肉体上极大的消耗，你会感觉到跑不完的会，见不完的人和项目方，但跑个三五天下来，可能真正的收获还是零。

确实新加坡的“大哥”很多，做市商更多，但和普通的小伙伴真的没有一毛钱的关系，很多所谓的做市商找你都是为了让你提供项目，如果你真有这份能力不来新加坡也没问题，如果没有那就更别说了。

新加坡的项目方也确实不少，新的老的都有，确实也会有一些合作的机会，但说实话，如果你还在为了经费而考虑是不是来新加坡的话，这些项目方大概率和你没有什么缘分，毕竟项目方需要的也是“大哥”。

更别说新加坡的牌局了，去年我聊过一次，就被小伙伴说多事了，新加坡的德州局水很深，没事的话不如去巨哼或者金煌，还能有点收获，非常非常不建议来坡的小伙伴和不熟悉的人打牌。具体的就不提了。

对于新加坡来说，你遇到的人会比香港多很多，机会也会多一些，但这前提完全在于你来的目的是什么，如果你的目的就是“撞大运”我觉得还是挺难的，很有可能是你还在嫌田鸡粥都要 100 新币的时候，大佬们还在巨哼玩第三场呢。

可能你觉得我很现实，但现实就是这样，大佬在巨哼包场，小兄弟们在越南场包场，小伙伴们在饭店包场，交易员在德州包场，而你还拿着邀请函盘算下一个地方应该去哪里的话，相信我，即便你和大哥坐在一桌，也不会有太多的收获。

真正是定点邀请的小伙伴都已经有足够清晰的路线，该去哪里，什么时候去，怎么去都已经非常明确了，而如果你还在犹豫，只能说你还需要努力，这种努力是跑会很难提升的。

这也是我为什么每次大型会议都想要办一个无差别活动的原因，如果你就是想见人，想和网友面基，想认识更多的小伙伴，和交易所以及项目方的小伙伴多接触一下，那么来我的活动肯定能有些收获，但如果只是这样，跑一次并不值得，当然就像我前边说的，你就是来当旅游的，那完全没问题。

最后十一月的曼谷，成本还是挺低的，如果说新加坡的主场是 OKX 的话，曼谷的主场就是 Binance（以前是在迪拜）

text:
Quantum-safety is a huge concern, and for this reason, we should start talking about the fact that it will be determined by a combination of 2 factors:
1. Quantum exposure
2. Crypto agility

What are these 2 things?

1. Quantum exposure: this is the degree to which a quantum computer will threaten your cryptography. 
For example, elliptic curve cryptography is quantum-vulnerable, while hash-based cryptography (e.g. ZK-STARKs) is quantum-resistant. 
So the more your protocol relies on quantum-vulnerable cryptography, the higher your quantum exposure.

2. Crypto agility: this is the ability to upgrade your cryptography while staying operational. 
Some protocols will need at least a soft fork (hello Bitcoin) to reach quantum-safety, some will require users to navigate their way through clunky UX, and in some cases, users will only need a quick approval for an upgrade. 
So seamless upgradability means high crypto agility. In cases where chains have lower crypto agility, it means the road to quantum-safety is longer and more difficult.

So quantum safety will rely on the combination of these 2 factors together. 
You CANNOT separate them.

More details and ecosystems review in the tweet below👇

text:
Synthetic Consciousness: A Personal Ontology

I keep using a few terms and throw them at people here on X. I thought for today's challenge I can list a few of them, and explain them in relation to each other and what the important differences are. Btw, nothing here is final – it's all still being defined and written up in the papers/essays/book from yesterday's post => so some of it will change.

Stop dying vs solve death:
- Process world-line -- the 4D trajectory of the physical processes going on in your brain, from birth onwards, taken as one continuous thing.

- Death -- as I use it: the process world-line ending irreversibly.

- Stop dying -- keep the process world-line from ending, with the brain you have now. Near-term, pretty medical, buys you time => but you're still stuck with one biological brain that keeps ageing, i.e. a single point of failure.

- Solve death -- going after that single point of failure itself. Premise: death is a contingent failure of the substrate. Move: swap the substrate out bit by bit for something repairable/fault-tolerant, with the process never switched off. Way slower, way harder tbh. Also "solved" doesn't mean immortal => the limits go from biological to physical ones, and the universe has plenty of those (heat death, eventually), so immortality is really its own question.

- Functional whole brain isolation (FWBI) -- the CPR-and-defibrillator part, basically. People die now, so a collapsing brain needs time bought long before anyone settles the identity debate => a whole brain kept alive and working outside the body, no death in between. Categorically different from transplantation, and a different ballpark from reperfusing a brain post mortem. It's @eightsixscience's empirical core.

- Extracorporeal cerebral preservation (ECP) -- the longer arc around isolation: gradual biohybrid replacement, then isolation, then further integration, ending up with what I call extracorporeal neuroprosthetics (isolated brains, at first only partly synthetic). Death is an Engineering Challenge (our essay from 2025) still calls it "ectopic cognitive preservation".

- Progressive extracorporeal cerebral preservation (pECP) -- the part of that arc that's actually near-term, and pretty much the stop-dying paper: keeping a brain preserved on extracorporeal support while it's still alive and working (built straight on top of isolation).

Uploading:
- Classical mind uploading (CMU) -- mind uploading's first naturalisation, into computer science, with whole brain emulation (WBE) as its main instantiation. Recipe: scan/model/run as software. Load-bearing assumption: whatever carries the person survives being abstracted into a computation, i.e. substrate independence (untested). The Great Filter essay from a few days ago is about classical mind uploading specifically.

- Re-naturalisation -- round two, and the central thesis of the manuscript I'm writing right now. Same aims (preservation/resilience/augmentation), just pursued step by step, preservation first. Parent disciplines this time are materials science and experimental medicine (computer science was round one; whether that counted as a naturalisation or more of a formalisation is a history question I'll leave for the paper :-)).

- Hybrid mind uploading (HMU) -- the discipline that comes out of the re-naturalisation, and the most pragmatic way to solve death as far as I can tell. Programmes can live inside it.

- Brain at hand -- starting point for hybrid mind uploading: the living brain someone already has, i.e. the one physical object the field actually has access to. Most of the literature I've been collecting skips it and goes straight to scan => model => run. Software still has a part to play, e.g. computationally reducible shortcuts for getting de novo hardware integrated, but as a bystander (a tool, basically) => it no longer carries the central thesis, or the philosophical leap about what the brain/consciousness/reality even is.

- Biomimetic neuromorphics -- not my field to claim btw, it already exists. Where I'd put it: whole brain emulation's slot, but in hybrid mind uploading. When emulation papers say "hardware", they (mostly, but not always) mean running the model faster, neuromorphic chips included => still the free-standing simulation posture, the model sits in the centre and the hardware just runs it. Here the brain's physics gets rebuilt in a substrate that couples into the host brain at hand (keep-the-patient-alive medicine, basically).

Replacement:
- Weak multiple realisability -- what I call it when a different piece of brain takes over a function. I mostly lean on two things here: the serial lesion effect (take the same tissue out in stages instead of in one go and function is often spared) and Barrett's (2013) gradual reorganisation principle, which builds on it (he's got cases with vast but gradually acquired damage and no measurable psychological deficit!). What it doesn't give you: a different substrate taking over (still open, and the bit I actually care about tbh).

- Alien neuron -- the concept I'd now put at the centre of hybrid mind uploading. An engineered structure whose form comes from its materials + from how it has to integrate into an existing brain (which is why it may look nothing like what it replaces). Design principle: optimising for temporal integration => start from the integrated state you want later and work backwards to what goes in first. Origin: a grafting problem actually (even a purely biological graft might look alien at implantation), the engineered one is just the general case.

- Mechanistic gradual brain replacement (MGBR) -- gradual replacement where the new parts are designed from their materials up: de novo/alien-neuron substrates that match the relevant tissue physics, couple into the living host and take over bit by bit. It's the materials-first route along biological => biohybrid => non-biological, so it doesn't need bio-to-bio grafting (Hébert-style) to work out. Older posts of mine say "mechanical", same thing.

Synconetics:
- Synconetics programme -- one programme within hybrid mind uploading. On the roadmap: mechanistic replacement, alien neurons, and a revised gradual reorganisation principle (incl. whether the substrate version holds). Correction while I'm at it: Death is an Engineering Challenge still introduces synconetics as "a new scientific discipline" and still files replacement under Eightsix. Both outdated (the naming moved over the past months, but the essay didn't) => the discipline is hybrid mind uploading, and replacement lives here now.

- World-line fidelity / empirical primacy / near-term urgency -- the programme's three principles. In short, from the essay: fidelity = the process world-line never breaks, and nothing gets traded against it (enhancement included). Empirical primacy = biology's the only substrate we KNOW carries consciousness, so synthetic stuff proves itself first. Near-term urgency = steam engines came before thermodynamics => build with what exists now, no waiting for a finished theory of consciousness.

- Existential gambling -- what the Synconetics programme says no to: betting a person's existence on stuff nobody can actually test. An obvious example: destructive scan-and-copy (original world-line ends and you hope the copy's you => and conscious at all!). Stop/copy/restart setups too btw.

- Synconetics Organisation -- the nonprofit (Verein) behind @synconeticsorg that Masataka Watanabe and I co-founded to run the programme. Open science, funded via a Simple Agreement for Research Equity (SARE; see yesterday's post). Org = the legal/funding vehicle, programme = the research it runs.

Endpoints:
- Big convergence -- AI, mind uploading, neuromorphic computing, biocomputing and neurotech all heading for one field.

- Synthetic consciousness -- where the big convergence ends up (and the book): engineered phenomenology on a designed substrate you could gradually become, with hybrid mind uploading at its core.

- Steerable phenomenology -- the stage after: once experience is carried by a designed substrate, what it's like could in principle be steered on purpose.

- Phenometronics -- the control science of phenomenal state spaces, i.e. what would turn steerable phenomenology into engineering. The programme I see coming after Synconetics, and the least defined thing on this list.

Pre Market Thoughts 30 Sep 26

Semis led a rally into the NY session with memory rebounding strongly. This subsided into a volatile 2 way uneasy price action as participants probably trim bets into the earnings AMC today for $MU. OAI also revealed that their ARR nears 70B with enterprise sales doubling, DOTS was also released off the back of the popularity with Muse. It is also doing a 30B round at a 1.4trn valuation.

Meanwhile Anthropic's cash burn and cash on hand (alongside the IPO) also seems to suggest that the labs have a comfortable cushion of funding. 

Oil has also slid down more than 6% from the local highs especially with the SPR release. The USA is also asking Europe to drawdown on its emergency diesel supply and for China to refine more. Trading crude and crude products this year has been chaotic and i would not try to make too much presumptions about it.

Yields are slightly lower by about 3bps with the lower oil as well as the poorer JOLTS print. Today also marks the end of 3Q, with quarterly rebalancing happening. Much of the flow has been pre-empted. 

 Memory stocks are also trading at extremely low IVs relative to the realised vol, i think this is a good tactical area to be bidding for optionality here.

Crypto markets also look to be in consolidation, with the majors range bound. At this point, I would look to take profits into rallies.

To sum up, i believe that $MU's print will decide on the direction of the market. In my mind it will be the catalyst for a move up across SOXX and QQQs, leading to a breakout across those range structures.

Good luck!

text:
远程记者吉米给大家带来采访摘要：

【Hyperliquid 上的 7×24 小时交易】

Joony Koo（@Joonylive）× Jeff Yan（@chameleon_jeff）

Joony Koo：
两年前，市场上的主流观点还是：市场就应该有休市时间，因为需要控制风险、让参与者休息，同时也要考虑非交易时段的流动性问题。你是什么时候开始觉得，这套逻辑已经不成立了？

Jeff Yan：
加密资产天然就是全球化的资产，所以“固定交易时段”这个概念其实一直都不太适用于 Crypto。对加密市场来说，7×24 小时交易从一开始就是默认状态。

真正让我觉得这件事开始影响传统金融，是当传统交易所开始延长交易时间的时候。它们并没有一步到位变成 7×24，而是先走向了 24×5，但这已经说明了一件事：传统交易所意识到了用户确实存在这样的需求，而且正在主动回应这种需求。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
现在传统交易所也开始延长交易时间了。那么相比它们，链上交易平台还能提供什么独特价值？

Jeff Yan：
其实，能不能 7×24 小时交易，跟是不是链上并没有直接关系。
我认为链上金融真正核心的价值有两个。

第一，是用户能够真正掌控和托管自己的资产。

在大多数正常情况下，这一点可能感觉没那么重要。但到了真正关键的时刻——比如交易对手、中介机构或者托管机构出现问题时——它的重要性就会体现出来。
减少对第三方的信任假设，把控制权从单一故障点转移给个人，会让整个金融系统更加稳健。

第二，是透明度。

透明度可能不是一个对所有普通用户都有强烈吸引力的卖点，但从理论上来说，你能够知道整个系统中正在发生的一切。由此产生的信任感和中立性，是由某一家私人机构完全控制的系统很难提供的。
所以，你当然可以在没有这些特性的情况下实现 7×24 小时交易。但资产自主权和透明度，才是链上市场真正能够带给世界的东西。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
今年我们已经看到，大宗商品、股票，甚至 Pre-IPO 资产都开始出现规模化交易。有时候，在传统参考市场休市期间，链上市场甚至已经开始进行价格发现。
当你们同时观察传统市场和链上市场运行时，团队最大的收获是什么？

Jeff Yan：
最明确的一点就是：

市场对 7×24 小时交易的需求是真实存在的。

如果没有这些市场，你可能很难意识到这一点，但整个世界并不会同时进入睡眠。

全球化的 7×24 小时市场，可以把来自不同时区、不同地区的买方和卖方流动性集中到一起，从而让整个市场对所有参与者而言都更加高效、流动性也更好。

无论任何时候，世界上的某个地方，总会有人想表达自己的市场观点。

所以，只要这样一个市场存在，它最终就可能成为大家自然聚集过去进行交易的Schelling Point——也就是市场参与者自发形成共识、集中流动性的地方。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
HIP-3 允许独立团队自己创建市场，现在也已经有机构开始在 Hyperliquid 上构建产品。
既然任何人都可以来建设，那么 Hyperliquid Labs 自己最关注的是什么？

Jeff Yan：
Labs 最擅长的，是为这些市场部署者提供底层技术和基础设施。

不同 deployer 的需求差异非常大。

这取决于他们是谁、位于哪个地区、服务什么用户、希望上线什么资产……需要解决的问题其实非常多。

我们的愿景，是让 Hyperliquid 成为一个中立的金融基础设施层，有点类似 AWS。

AWS 的价值就在于，它让创业公司甚至大型企业都不需要从零开始重复建设最底层的基础设施。

金融领域也应该如此。

像订单簿这样的金融基础组件，未来应该变成一种无处不在、经过充分实战检验的公共基础设施。

而让这些基础设施真正能够服务所有人，就是 Labs 最核心的使命。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
你提到“金融版 AWS”，让我想到以前在游戏公司工作时，大家还经常争论：“云服务真的可以信任吗？”

那目前有哪些重要问题，是 Labs 最希望其他开发者去解决的？

Jeff Yan：
首先，我觉得开发者应该去寻找那些只有自己特别适合做的事情。

这取决于他们自己的兴趣、能力以及竞争优势。无论他们最终选择做什么，我们都会支持。

如果要说一个特别具体、同时又非常困难的问题，那就是：
如何真正把底层资产本身代币化。

这里面的托管、流动性以及具体运行机制都更加复杂，所以目前这个领域还没有真正大规模发展起来。

我希望明年可以看到更多优秀的项目和开发者进入这个领域。

因为一旦现实资产能够真正以链上形式存在，它们就能够和链上的价格发现以及流动性机制形成非常强的协同效应。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
随着越来越多机构进入，资产代币化正在明显加速。

对于规模比较小的团队，你有什么建议？

Jeff Yan：
现在确实已经有很多团队在做资产代币化，大公司、小团队都有。

但整个领域目前还没有真正突破临界点，我们也并不知道最终谁能够成功。

而这恰恰就是中立基础设施的魅力所在。

并不是说团队规模大，你就天然会赢。

当然，大机构确实可能拥有一些合理优势，比如更强的机构资源和金融网络。

但很多真正具有病毒式传播能力的产品，反而往往来自小团队。

因为小团队有时候能够以完全不同的方式看待这个世界，而且思维不会那么僵化。

永续合约就是一个非常好的例子。

它是一种非常直观、相对公平的金融工具，可以把全球不同地区、不同时间尺度的流动性集中到同一个资产上，因此也非常容易向用户呈现。

未来甚至可能有某个小团队，重新定义我们现在习以为常的交易界面应该长什么样。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
这周你在韩国和当地社区相处了三天，有什么让你印象特别深刻的地方？

Jeff Yan：
和去年一样，我再次感受到了韩国社区的热情好客。
我也非常感谢所有帮助组织活动的人。

这里的社区非常强大，而且对于很多韩国人来说，交易本身就是生活中非常重要的一部分。

所以能够和他们讨论链上市场，以及 HIP-3 未来可能如何改变他们参与市场的方式，是一件非常有意思的事情。

和用户、和社区直接交流，也会不断激励我们继续建设下去。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
那你和机构的交流呢？

Jeff Yan：
看到越来越多机构开始对 Hyperliquid 感兴趣，并且开始在这个平台上建设产品，这件事很令人兴奋。

当然，机构采用新技术的速度往往会更慢，这完全可以理解。

因为它们拥有大量需要保护的资产、业务和客户。

但从今年的发展来看，机构对这类产品的需求和兴趣已经非常明显了。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
最后一个问题：

还有什么目前没有连续价格的资产，下一步可能会率先进入 7×24 小时定价？

Jeff Yan：
我没有一个特别具体的答案。

但我认为，Private Markets是一个非常大的机会。

其实通过一些 HIP-3 deployer，我们现在已经开始看到这种趋势了。

当今大量财富创造其实发生在Private Markets。

因为从公司的角度来说，它们往往有动力尽可能长时间保持私有状态、不上市。

这并不是说它们主观上想把世界上绝大多数人排除在财富创造之外，但最终实际造成的结果就是如此。

如果我们能够让这些资产在更早阶段，就进入一个全球化的价格发现体系，而且这个体系并不局限于某一个司法辖区，那么我们可能有机会改变这种现状。

当然，这里面还有大量复杂问题需要解决。

但市场存在的意义，本来就应该是让所有人都有机会从中受益。

所以我认为：

任何资产、任何时间、任何地点都可以交易，可能正是这个领域最有潜力的方向。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
最后还有什么想说的吗？

Jeff Yan：
Hyperliquid 最核心的优势，始终是它的社区和人。

它并不是一家企业，只想着怎么做对自己最有利的事情。

它更像是一个由大量贡献者和用户共同组成的去中心化网络，大家一起建设一个由人们自己拥有，而不是由私人利益集团掌控的金融系统。

当然，我们距离这个目标还有很长的路，也还有很多挑战需要面对。

但这次在首尔看到所有人之后，我觉得我们处在一个非常好的状态。

我相信大家最终能够一起构建出一套，真正能够被整个金融体系所采用的东西。

Interview Summary: 24/7 Trading on Hyperliquid (@Joonylive  × Jeff Yan)

Joony Koo: Two years ago, the prevailing view was that markets should close because of risk, rest, and off-hours liquidity. Was there a moment when that view broke for you?

Jeff Yan: Crypto is an inherently international asset, so the idea of market hours never really fit, and 24/7 has always been the default. It started to matter for traditional assets when the incumbent exchanges began extending their hours. They didn't go straight to 24/7, they went to 24/5, but it became clear they had recognized customer demand and were responding to it.

Joony Koo: Incumbents are now matching the hours. What is left that an on-chain venue can offer?

Jeff Yan: Trading hours are independent of being on-chain. The core of on-chain finance is two things. First, users keep control and custody of their funds. That doesn't matter day to day, but it matters in critical moments, when counterparties, intermediaries, or custodians run into trouble. Reducing trust assumptions and moving power to individuals rather than a single point of failure makes the system more robust. Second, transparency. It has limited mass appeal, but being able to know, in theory, everything happening in the system brings a trust and neutrality you don't get from a system controlled by one private organization. You can have 24/7 trading without these properties, but these are what on-chain markets can offer the world.

Joony Koo: This year commodities, equities, and pre-IPO names traded at scale, and price discovery sometimes happened while the reference markets were closed. What did the team learn from watching the two run side by side?

Jeff Yan: The clearest lesson is that demand for 24/7 trading exists. You wouldn't know without these markets, but the world doesn't sleep as a whole. Global 24/7 markets concentrate liquidity across more buyers and sellers, making markets more efficient and liquid for everyone. There will always be someone, somewhere, who wants to express a view, so once the option exists, those markets become the Schelling point where people go to do that.

Joony Koo: HIP-3 lets independent teams create markets, and institutions are building on top too. If anyone can build, what is Labs focusing on?

Jeff Yan: Labs specializes in the technology and infrastructure that supports deployers. What a deployer needs varies widely depending on who they are, where they're based, who their users are, and what they want to list, and the list is long. The vision is for Hyperliquid to be a neutral infrastructure layer, like AWS, which spared startups and large firms from reinventing the wheel. Financial primitives like order books should become pervasive and battle-tested infrastructure, and making that work for everyone is the primary mandate.

Joony Koo: The "AWS for finance" analogy reminds me of working at a game company when people debated whether the cloud could be trusted. What open problems would Labs most like to see others solve?

Jeff Yan: First, builders should find something they're uniquely positioned to do, given their interests and competitive advantages, and we'll support whatever they build. One specific hard problem is tokenizing the underlying assets themselves. Custody, liquidity, and the mechanics are all harder, so it hasn't taken off yet. I hope to see strong projects and builders next year, because having the assets represented on-chain synergizes with price discovery and liquidity.

Joony Koo: Tokenization is speeding up as more institutions get involved. Any advice for smaller teams?

Jeff Yan: Many teams, big and small, are working on tokenization, but it hasn't hit escape velocity and it's unclear who will succeed. That's the beauty of neutral infrastructure: you don't win just because you're big, though big teams may have legitimate advantages like institutional connectivity. Viral products often come from small teams that see the world differently and think less rigidly. Perps are intuitive and fair instruments that concentrate liquidity across the globe and across all time horizons into one asset, so they're easy to present to users. Some small team may even reinvent how the interfaces look.

Joony Koo: You spent three days with the Korean community this week. What stood out?

Jeff Yan: Like last year, I felt the hospitality, and I'm grateful to everyone who organized events. The community here is strong, and trading is a core part of many Koreans' lives, so it was great to discuss how on-chain markets and HIP-3 would change their approach to markets. Talking to users and the community inspires us to keep building.

Joony Koo: And your meetings with institutions?

Jeff Yan: It's cool to see institutions interested in the platform and building on top of it. They're understandably slower to adopt new technology because they have a lot to protect, but as this year has shown, the appetite is significant.

Joony Koo: Last question: what is next to be priced 24/7 that has no continuous price today?

Jeff Yan: Nothing specific, but private markets are a big opportunity, and you already see some of it through HIP-3 deployers. Much wealth creation happens privately, because companies have incentives to stay private as long as possible. It isn't intended to exclude most of the world's population, but that's what happens in practice. Allowing global price discovery on these assets as early as possible, in a global system not confined to one jurisdiction, could break that trend. There are many complexities to work through, but markets exist so everyone can benefit from them, and trading anything, anytime, anywhere has the most potential here.

Joony Koo: Any final remarks?

Jeff Yan: Hyperliquid's core strength is its community and people. It's not one company doing what's best for itself, but a decentralized network of contributors and users building a financial system owned by the people rather than by private interests. There's a long way to go and many challenges, but seeing everyone in Seoul, I feel we're in good hands, and we'll build something the financial system can ultimately adopt.

@kbwofficial @HyperliquidX

text:
A teenager in the United States started publishing software at 14 in 1998, built the entire online infrastructure for the Occupy Wall Street movement in 2011, joined Google as a software engineer, quit in 2018, and then spent five years writing a C library that does something the entire industry said was impossible.

Then she combined it with llama.cpp and shipped the easiest way on the planet to run a large language model on any computer.

Her name is Justine Tunney.

Here is the story, because almost nobody outside the low level systems world knows what one engineer has built.

Justine was born in 1984. She started writing and publishing software at 14, back when distribution meant uploading binaries to BBS systems and chat networks. She picked up the handle jart, which she still uses on GitHub today. She did the work most teenagers her age were not doing. She read the systems programming literature. She studied compilers. She fell in love with C.

In July 2011 she registered the @occupywallst Twitter handle and the occupywallst dot org domain. Within weeks the protest movement that began in Zuccotti Park in New York had become a global phenomenon, and her infrastructure was the digital backbone of the entire thing. She handled the social media, the website, the donations, the coordination. She built the platform that pushed the movement to reach millions.

After Occupy she joined Google as a software engineer. She worked on TensorBoard, the visualization tool for TensorFlow, and on site reliability for Google infrastructure. She stayed for years. Then in 2018 she left Google Brain to work on a personal project.

The project was called Cosmopolitan Libc.

Cosmopolitan does something most C programmers would tell you is mathematically impossible. It lets you compile a C program once and have the resulting binary run natively on Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and NetBSD with no modification. One file. Six operating systems. No virtual machines. No interpreters. No recompilation. The technique she invented is called Actually Portable Executable.

The implications are wild. Cosmopolitan binaries violate every assumption about how operating systems load programs. They are at once a Windows PE file, a Linux ELF binary, a macOS Mach-O binary, and a shell script. The same bytes run on every platform.

For five years she worked on it mostly alone. She funded the development partly through Mozilla's MIECO program, which sponsored her work on Cosmopolitan 3.0, released on October 31, 2023.

A month later she shipped llamafile.

llamafile is what happens when you combine Cosmopolitan with llama.cpp. You take any LLM weights file in the standard GGUF format, you wrap it in Justine's binary, and you get a single file that runs on six operating systems without installation. No Python. No CUDA setup. No dependency hell. Just one file that you double click and it works.

Mozilla launched it as an official project of their innovation group on November 29, 2023. It went viral immediately. The repository, hosted at github .com/mozilla-ai/llamafile, now has 24,600 stars. The license is Apache 2.0.

Justine kept shipping. She added GPU support to Cosmopolitan, a task systems engineers thought would require rewriting the whole thing. She added dlopen support, another thing nobody else had figured out. She wrote whisperfile, a single file version of OpenAI's Whisper speech-to-text model based on the same architecture.

Her GitHub profile lists projects most engineers would consider impossible. sectorlisp, a Lisp interpreter that fits in a boot sector. blink, the tiniest x86-64-linux emulator on Earth. bestline, a teletypewriter command session library. redbean, a complete web server inside a single zip file.

A teenager who shipped software in 1998 grew up to write the C library that the entire local AI movement now runs on top of.

She did most of it alone, and most people scrolling AI Twitter cannot name her.

text:
刚重新把 Project Mars / $DRILL 的数据拆了一遍。

我觉得现在最值得关注的，不是“DRILL 怎么又跌了”，而是一个很明显的背离：

Project fundamentals 在变强，但 Token fundamentals 还没有跟上。

$DRILL 过去 24h 跌了约 16%，但同期供应量反而净减少约 0.22%。

过去 24h：

Mint ≈ 84.9 万 DRILL
Burn ≈ 86.1 万 DRILL
净减少 ≈ 1.13 万 DRILL
Sell tx 167 / Buy tx 106

所以现在的下跌，并不能简单解释成“无限增发把币砸死了”。

真正的问题更像是：

整个游戏经济的周转非常快，但新增外部买盘，还覆盖不了老玩家持续兑现的产出。

再往下看会更明显。

现在大约有 432 台 active rigs，但对应的 unique miners 只有约 86 个地址。

而且前 10 个玩家就占了约 56.5% 的活跃矿机。

也就是说：

游戏是真的有人玩，链上行为也是真的，但生产端目前高度集中。

与此同时，Spaceship 总量 3,333，目前 mint 约 694，只卖出了约 20.8%。

所以目前我对它的判断不是“项目不行了”，也不是“跌这么多一定便宜”。

而是：

Project thesis 目前没有坏，但 Token thesis 还没有被证明。

Project Mars 这几天实际上一直在继续做产品：

Plot、Rig、Ore、升级、Refinery、Spaceship、Parts、后面的太空挖矿……

这些东西我自己也一直在真实地跑。

但对 $DRILL 来说，最终决定价格的不是功能越来越多，而是：

这些功能能不能真正带来更多新用户、新资金，以及持续的 DRILL 需求。

所以我现在反而觉得，10 月 5 日是一个很重要的观察点。

不是看“飞船玩法做得酷不酷”，而是看它能不能把整个经济从：

一小群老玩家高频生产、消费、兑现

推进到：

更多新玩家持续进入，并形成新的 DRILL 需求。

如果做到了，这种几十万美金市值的资产，重估会非常剧烈。

如果做不到，那么即使游戏越来越完整，$DRILL 也可能长期只是一个高周转的生产资料。

这两件事，要分开看。

而 $NEAR 自 8 月底以来从 1.6 美元一路拉升至 5 美元上方、接近三倍的涨幅。

按照惯性，部分人的第一反应是：传统资金要进场扫货了，这是个可接追高的重磅利好。

但如果拆解这只 ETF 的实际结构和 NEAR 过去两个月的上涨逻辑，你会发现无脑 FOMO 的话极容易成为Sell the News）”的接盘方。

NRR 的落地确实打通了传统美股账户购买 NEAR 的合规渠道，并且它的结构是“现货持仓+质押”。

但通道的建立并不代表机构资金已经在排队买入。 
Bitwise 为这只基金设定了 0.75% 的管理费，并计划将底层代币进行质押（当前链上收益率约 5%）。

值得注意的是，Bitwise 会抽走 33% 的质押收益来覆盖节点和托管成本，剩余的 67% 才会回馈给 ETF 份额净值。 
这意味着，在看到确切的净申购数据和持仓增量之前，ETF 只是一个中性偏正的结构变化。8 月至 9 月的这波三倍涨幅，实际上已经提前透支了大部分的“过会预期”。

此外，Bitwise 在其招股书和宣传中，并没有把 NEAR 包装成单纯的“以太坊杀手”，而是将其定义为“AI 代理的结算层”。

这才是支撑 NEAR 近期估值重塑的核心基本面。

随着 NEAR Intents（跨链意图协议）的上线，其历史累计交易量已经突破 320 亿美元。市场的买盘逻辑在于：

未来的 AI 代理需要自己付款、换汇、下单，它们需要一个速度快、成本低且不绑定单一托管方的跨链清算网络，而 NEAR 正在抢占这个叙事生态位。

再说当前比较火的回购叙事。

伴随 Intents 的放量，NEAR 的代币经济学也完成了一次重构。协议年通胀上限从 5% 削减至 2.5%，并且自明年起，Intents 的手续费收入将用于在公开市场回购 NEAR。 

但这套机制目前更多是“叙事锚点”，而非现实的买盘支撑。按目前约 2000 万美元量级的年化协议净收入计算，它依然无法覆盖 2.5% 通胀带来的每年约 1.5 亿美元的新增发行抛压。

价格涨得越高，实现通缩的美元门槛就越高。如果后续 Intents 的日均成交量无法维持，这套回购叙事会面临证伪风险。

小编个人认为，在短期随着之前价格爆拉和利好消息的兑现，盲目追高面临着极大的获利回吐风险。

而中长期老币新炒，叙事更新的整体玩法没变，依然看好。

quoted_text:
The chief economist at Apollo is warning that mass adoption of AI agents could trigger a bank run as they optimize user investments. Gary Gensler spent his last few years as SEC chair warning that the exact same problem will hit the markets: the pursuit of algorithmic perfection at scale destroys system stability. Personal-finance agents making simultaneous optimal decisions could potentially cause a massive flash crash. 

Agent acausal coordination, with no messages passed between them, will show up in a lot of places. Markets will get the big headlines, but huge numbers of clever advisors making very similar choices will impact all of human society. Capability gains make this worse, not better. The smarter the agents, the narrower the optimal path; and knowing that other agents see that exact same path lets them move together without talking to each other. Agents do not need to collude to act in unison. Thus, they break no human laws by doing so. Human laws were not written for this. They were not written for a lot of what is coming, and it is about to start happening very fast.

text:
有朋友问，为什么AI争霸赛似乎只有中美是主力？

可能看新闻确实容易有这个感觉，因为大家常说的“只有中美”，指的是最前沿的通用大模型这一块。最顶级的竞争，确实几乎只剩中美了。

据斯坦福的AI指数统计，去年全世界的重要模型，绝大多数出自美国和中国，欧洲只有个位数，而且九成以上来自企业，不是大学。这一场比赛为什么只剩两个主力，我认为原因不在谁的科研人员更聪明，而是前沿AI已经从一门科研，变成了一门重工业。

如果只是说几个聪明人在办公室里想出一个好办法，这种事还在发生，但要落地，把它变成一个前沿模型，得同时有几样东西：顶尖的研究团队，海量的算力，能扛好多年亏损的钱，还有能让几亿人用上的产品。这几样不是加法，是乘法，缺一样，别的都转不起来。有人才没算力，想法验证不了；有算力没团队，芯片不会自己变成模型；做出了模型没有钱和客户，就撑不到下一代。我之前写Anthropic那篇，它签下了未来十年五千多亿美元的算力合同，大部分不能取消。能签又敢签这种合同的，全世界没有几家。

美国的底子，是上一轮互联网和云计算留下来的。Microsoft、Google、Amazon、Meta，本来就有赚钱的主业、现成的数据中心和几十亿用户，研究可以先亏着，产品不用从零找入口，搜索、办公软件、云服务，接上就能用。钱也不只来自银行，股权、债券、私人信贷一起上。

当然还有一点容易被忽略：美国实验室里的顶尖研究者，很多是在中国读的本科，所以“美国公司领先”和“美国人单独做到了”是两回事。

另外一边，中国的底子也不是这两年才有的。阿里、腾讯、字节、百度，同样有云、有应用、有几亿用户，研究做出来，马上有地方用，用的反馈又回到研究。AI论文和专利的数量，中国早就是世界第一。芯片被卡住以后，反而逼出了一些节省算力为优先的做法，DeepSeek那一波让很多人第一次意识到，这场比赛不只是比谁的芯片多。

那欧洲呢？欧洲肯定不缺人，也不缺钱，但欧洲缺的能扛风险的钱。欧洲央行行长Lagarde这个月在维也纳讲得很直白，美国是整个资本市场都动员起来支撑AI建设，欧洲却还主要靠银行，而新模型这种东西，光靠借钱是做不出来的，得靠股权。银行要问的是你能不能还钱，风险投资可以接受十个项目死九个，只要剩下那一个够大。欧洲家庭每年存下一万多亿欧元，可这些钱很难流到一家要亏好多年的AI公司手里，再加上各国市场还没有真正打通，Mistral这样的顶级AI公司也是有的，但很难长成那种体量。

还有一些因素，并不总直接出现在讨论中，却是这场比赛不可或缺的一部分。比如最先进的芯片是台积电造的，造芯片的光刻机来自荷兰的ASML，模型需要的高带宽内存，很大一块来自韩国的SK海力士。AI模型榜单上看见的是谁的模型，看不见的是谁在给所有人卖铲子。

最后我想说说“争霸”这个词。资源往领先者那里集中，是会自我强化的，人才去算力最多的地方，钱去人才最多的地方，产品又把人和钱再吸过去。一旦大家把这件事看成两个国家之间的争霸，还会多出一层压力，谁都觉得，我不跑，对方就会跑，停下来就是输。我在Anthropic那篇里说，合同不会配速，争霸的叙事也不会。

可争霸问的是谁赢，我更想问的是，赢了以后呢？一个地方不一定要拥有最强的模型，才能从AI里得到好处，欧洲的工厂、台湾的晶圆厂，都在这场比赛里拿到了自己的那一份。反过来，拥有最强的模型，也还要问能不能让那个社会里的人过得更好。技术是手段，一旦把比赛本身当成了目的，跑在里面的人，就很容易变成燃料。

2) The GOP legislature to pass it in the few sessions left after the election. Leadership just dismissed a moratorium as "not a serious proposal."

3) No shortcut via the ballot. The citizen amendment missed 2026, so the earliest statewide vote is Nov 2027.

So I bought NO off the farmers' ladder. Me vs the book for now. There's still size left if you're in the business of correcting prices.

text:
有小伙伴说线下见面加深互相的信任，这点我是 100% 同意的，所以我会说每年选香港最好，性价比很高了，或者是今年选曼谷，往年都是在迪拜，性价比也不高，但曼谷消费要便宜很多。

对于没有明确的目标，而且预算有限的小伙伴来说，每年两次香港应该是最合适的跑会了，市面上经常跑的小伙伴几乎都能见到，交易所的活动也都会在香港安排，整体预算会低很多。

但我始终认为，跑会的本质目并不是资源之间的勾搭，毕竟有足够资源的话是没啥必要跑会的，跑会更多的是和小伙伴见面，聊天，加深印象，或者是有非常强的目的性，要去见某些人，或者是确定某些事情。

单纯靠跑会积累的人脉和资源很可能只是停留在微信。多数人你会发现可能一年都说不上两句话。

打铁还是要自身硬，自身足够硬的时候，跑不跑，怎么跑也就没所谓了。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
跑会的这个话题真的是每次大会都会说一次，我的观点始终保持一致，如果没有具体的业务，如果不是抱着过来玩的心态，如果没有小伙伴再一起，跑会大可不必。

这一轮的跑会应该是从四月香港开始的吧，然后就是七月的日本，八月的香港，九月的台北，十月的韩国和新加坡，十一月的曼谷，结束。

从人数来说，两次香港虽然人并不很多，但如果准备是社交的话真的是足够了，而且从内地到香港不论是时间还是费用相比都是很低的，甚至有些小伙伴都是白天在香港，晚上住深圳，费用会更低。

日本和韩国，相对来说对于想要进军日韩市场的项目方肯定是不会错过的，但日韩的市场过于保守了，想要在这两个国家取得成绩需要交非常高的学费，我亲眼见过很多一腔热血的项目方被一些当地的“大哥”骗得团团转。

而对于 KOL 来说，日韩除非是项目方报销，否则获得得信息资源和所谓得人脉资源并不会高于香港，尤其是日韩主力语言并不是英语，而且很多小伙伴英语也不够好，这种情况下跑会更多的就是纯玩了。

台北很好，真的很棒，主要是语言通畅的情况下可以和当地的小伙伴沟通，可以学到很多当地有用的知识，认识更多当地的小伙伴，只是台北的签证不是很容易，但这些跑会中，我是觉得台北是仅次于香港可以有有效社交的地方。

新加坡是最大的 Token 2049 活动，又有 F1 ，本身成本就很高的地区更是雪上加霜，怎么说呢，来新加坡是一种对肉体上极大的消耗，你会感觉到跑不完的会，见不完的人和项目方，但跑个三五天下来，可能真正的收获还是零。

确实新加坡的“大哥”很多，做市商更多，但和普通的小伙伴真的没有一毛钱的关系，很多所谓的做市商找你都是为了让你提供项目，如果你真有这份能力不来新加坡也没问题，如果没有那就更别说了。

新加坡的项目方也确实不少，新的老的都有，确实也会有一些合作的机会，但说实话，如果你还在为了经费而考虑是不是来新加坡的话，这些项目方大概率和你没有什么缘分，毕竟项目方需要的也是“大哥”。

更别说新加坡的牌局了，去年我聊过一次，就被小伙伴说多事了，新加坡的德州局水很深，没事的话不如去巨哼或者金煌，还能有点收获，非常非常不建议来坡的小伙伴和不熟悉的人打牌。具体的就不提了。

对于新加坡来说，你遇到的人会比香港多很多，机会也会多一些，但这前提完全在于你来的目的是什么，如果你的目的就是“撞大运”我觉得还是挺难的，很有可能是你还在嫌田鸡粥都要 100 新币的时候，大佬们还在巨哼玩第三场呢。

可能你觉得我很现实，但现实就是这样，大佬在巨哼包场，小兄弟们在越南场包场，小伙伴们在饭店包场，交易员在德州包场，而你还拿着邀请函盘算下一个地方应该去哪里的话，相信我，即便你和大哥坐在一桌，也不会有太多的收获。

真正是定点邀请的小伙伴都已经有足够清晰的路线，该去哪里，什么时候去，怎么去都已经非常明确了，而如果你还在犹豫，只能说你还需要努力，这种努力是跑会很难提升的。

这也是我为什么每次大型会议都想要办一个无差别活动的原因，如果你就是想见人，想和网友面基，想认识更多的小伙伴，和交易所以及项目方的小伙伴多接触一下，那么来我的活动肯定能有些收获，但如果只是这样，跑一次并不值得，当然就像我前边说的，你就是来当旅游的，那完全没问题。

最后十一月的曼谷，成本还是挺低的，如果说新加坡的主场是 OKX 的话，曼谷的主场就是 Binance（以前是在迪拜）

text:
There were 344 crypto security incidents in the first half of 2026 alone, that's almost two a day.

Here's why this keeps happening in crypto ↓

1️⃣ One bug = millions at risk

Protocols move money automatically, and a loophole in the code can let attackers drain funds before anyone notices.

2️⃣ Oracle manipulation

Manipulated price feeds can make a lending protocol value a token at 10x its actual price, letting attackers borrow way more than their collateral should allow.

3️⃣ Admin keys still exist

Even decentralized projects often have a few people with privileged access. Stolen keys or malicious approvals can give attackers control without exploiting a bug in the code.

4️⃣ Dependencies create new attack surfaces

Bridges, oracles, external contracts. Each adds another layer of risk, exposing even well-built protocols to failures elsewhere.

5️⃣ Audits are a snapshot, not a guarantee

An audit checks code at one point in time. It can miss edge cases, and later updates or integrations can introduce new vulnerabilities.

6️⃣ Asymmetric incentives

Security practices vary, and some teams run bug bounties and formal verification while others ship fast and hope for the best.

Meanwhile, attackers (including state-backed groups) have millions in upside and keep probing for weak points.

My take: defenders have to get a lot of things right. Attackers only need to find one weakness.

That’s why security can’t end with an audit. It has to keep up with every upgrade, integration, and person who has access to the funds.

text:
I'm excited about the sets, points and badges coming with the @OriginalBlokyz Collector Portal, but Explore and Build is probably what I'm most curious about. 👀

Explore will let a Bloky reveal and chart part of the world, while Build will let that character build something in it.

What I especially like is that the world itself won't be hidden. You'll be able to see the land, weather and general shape of it from the start, but settlements and information in unexplored areas won't be readable yet.

"The world is never hidden, only unreadable."

Once you explore an area, that knowledge stays with you. Even if you later sell the Bloky you explored it with, the land remains mapped.

I really like the idea that your map keeps some history of your collection too. You might sell a Bloky later, but the area you explored with it stays mapped.

Build is different. The example they give is a Shaman with a shrine. Sell the Shaman and the shrine goes dark or disappears, while the territory you've explored remains.

"Territory revealed is knowledge. A building is a possession."

So your map isn't just about what you own right now. You'll also be able to look back and see areas you explored with Blokyz you don't even own anymore.

And knowing that physical Blokyz will also connect to the Collector Map through NFC makes the whole thing even more interesting.

Some of these details come from an earlier version of the docs, so the final version may of course be different. But I really hope this is still the idea.

I was worried experimentation in tokenomics was dead but I was wrong!

Crypto is back trying something new after a full past cycle focused on low-float, high-fdv launches.

Up to now we got:

- $ZCAT: Hold a meme, receive ZEC. A 3% transfer tax funds the rewards, so you accumulate another asset while waiting for your meme to moon.

- $BUN / Mosh: Instead of bots front running launches, the 'bundle launch' commits money for agents that trade it. BIG DIFFERENCE is that bundle backers earn trading fees but you can't withdraw LP.

Interesting incentive to keep a market alive, although agents can still sell the tokens.

- $STONK: Fees buys and burns its top 15 eligible tokens, weighted by market cap.

So now projects compete for buybacks generated across the ecosystem.

- $VVV / DIEM: Lock staked VVV to mint DIEM. Stake DIEM for daily AI credits, or sell it.

You can sell the AI access while keeping your VVV locked.

- $ORBIO: Trading fees fund AI credits for stakers. You can use them or sell them.

Degens trading your token help pay for someone else's AI usage.

- $BP: Stake for 1+ year to qualify for equity conversion at a future IPO.

Plus, supply unlocks depend on growth milestones. The team needs to deliver for more tokens to unlock.

---

Common theme among them: tokens aren't just fundraising tools but crypto tries to add REAL VALUE to tokens. Just a roadmap isn't gonna cut it anymore.

Another common point: many still depend on degens continuing to trade.

Speculation rules everything in crypto. still.

Instinct CEO Noah Shinn says agents will let restaurants give tables to birthdays and anniversaries over whoever clicks first

"And traditionally, because of the way that the internet has worked, at least for reservations, it's been first come first serve. So anyone that comes in, no matter how important or how not important it might be, whoever gets in first gets the reservation."

"But what if you had the ability for the agent to be able to communicate on both sides, communicate, hey, this is important. This is actually the person's spouse's birthday, the 30th birthday, a very special event is coming up."

"And the restaurant too can say, let's actually prioritize birthdays or major decade birthdays or major anniversaries or these certain people, I don't know, whatever it might be, right?"

"So now with the ability, with all of the logistical burden of having to describe exactly what your case is and what's happening and why it's important. Now we have the ability to perfectly match what does the restaurant want? What does the user want?"

"And that will result in more special events for the users being able to actually have a spot in the restaurant."

text:
自古 Perp DEX 多大毛。
dYdX 空投了 25% 的代币，Hyperliquid 空投了 31%，Variational 宣布将空投 32%。
这些数字已经足够惊人。

但更震撼的来了， @popdex_ 直接宣布 100% 价值返还。不搞积分长跑，也不靠空投预期反复 PUA 用户。
听起来很美好，但问题也随之浮现。
▌如果价值全部返还给用户，开发团队靠什么赚钱？
▌PopDEX 拿了 3000 万美元投资，它到底会不会发币？

我们一个个来解答。

1/ PopDEX 是谁？
PopDEX 是一个用户优先的永续合约 DEX，主打资本效率和交易体验。
2026 年 5 月，PopDEX 宣布完成 3000 万美元融资，由 Foresight Ventures 领投。
目前，它已经跑完了 4 轮封闭测试：
▌累计交易量 30 亿美元
▌LP 资金池 6100 万美元

更关键的是，所谓的“100% 价值回流”，在内测期间就已经不是口号，而是真金白银。
第四期封测中，有用户单个地址拿到了 8000 USDT 的最高奖励；
用户 @kasoutuu 实测跑出 600 万美元交易量，获得 2550 USDT 交易奖励，扣除手续费后还额外多赚了 1000 USDT。

当然，并非人人都能赚钱。但这种价值反哺的模式，确实大幅降低了用户的实际交易成本。

2/ PopDEX 会发币吗？
首先要澄清一个误解。所谓“100% 价值回流”，并不是把所有手续费原封不动退给用户，而是指手续费所产生的、可分配部分的价值，全部回流给用户。

那它会发币吗？
首先， Foresight 领投了 3000 万美元，风投要退出，逻辑上需要一个可流通的代币作为出口。
其次，PopDEX 采用了“自建专用 L1 + 链上订单簿”的方案，来提供媲美 CEX 的交易体验。而公链发行原生代币的可能性普遍不低。

3/ 结语：为什么 PopDEX 想走一条不同的路？
如今大多数 Perp DEX 都靠撒积分 + 空投代币来拉新，但这套玩法有个致命问题。
Foresight 的调查显示，69% 的用户承认积分和空投是他们选择某个 Perp DEX 的最重要原因。可问题是，这批逐利用户往往会在代币上线后迅速出走。
Foresight 对比了多个平台后发现，只有 Hyperliquid 在代币上线后交易量不降反升，成功把空投党转化成了真实用户。仅此一家，别无例外。

PopDEX 想做的，正是一条更难、但更长久的路，不靠激励租来用户，而是把可分配价值 100% 分给真实用户，从而建立起“真交易、真分红、长期玩”的正向循环。

如果你认同这个理念，不妨亲自试试 PopDEX： 👉 https://t.co/C2Ku1FzKxc

text:
今天看到RobinDog（ rubidium:native），研究了下还挺意思
RobinDog是robinhood上的原生预测市场，和普通的预测市场不同的是，上面注意交易的是rb链上的原生项目为主，比如两个 Pons 项目中，哪一个会先完成迁移等等。

还有一个特色就是RobinDog 的故事树能够将过去的事件、实时市场动态、各种证据以及未来的发展脉络连接在一起，形成一个不断变化的叙事体系。把单一的市场趋势转化为三种潜在的收益来源：
1、事件层 — 决定该事件是否会发生，从而决定是否进行交易。
2、故事层次——在故事发展过程中，可以交换接下来会发生什么。
3、影响层——探讨结果可能对相关股票、股票代币、加密货币或其他资产产生的影响。
听上去有点深奥。他就是将一个事件的所有预测影响组合起来。
他们还起了一个宏大的 StoryFi概念，倒是有点意思。用户在参与公司事件预测时，可以选择使用同一笔预测资金，同时建立相关 Stock Token 的多头或空头仓位，所以预测还会有股票收益。robindog 应该也是首个推出这个产品机制的预测市场。

但是目前RobinDog上的交易量还比较低迷，如果真能做起来，目前市值肯定是低估了

text:
My latest supply chain checks indicate that Nvidia has begun testing glass-free copper-clad laminate (CCL) based primarily on hydrocarbon (HC) resin as a replacement for glass-free PTFE-based CCL tested previously, paired with glass-free HC-based PP. The goal is to determine whether this material combination can meet the switch tray PCB requirements for Rubin Ultra NVL576, an eight-rack interconnected solution expected to enter mass production in 2H27.

Preliminary tests conducted as part of efforts to improve PCB manufacturability show that glass-free HC CCL meets the switch tray’s high-frequency electrical requirements. Its electrical performance trails that of the original PTFE solution but exceeds that of M9-class solutions and even surpasses M10’s stated specifications. These results do not represent a final material selection, but they indicate that NVIDIA continues to seek higher PCB manufacturing yields and greater production efficiency while meeting electrical requirements.

1. Key Takeaways and Analysis

(1) Previous NVL576 switch tray tests used glass-free PTFE CCL paired with glass-free HC PP. The latest round replaces the PTFE CCL with glass-free HC CCL while retaining the same HC PP part number.

(2) Shengyi Technology is currently the leading supplier in the NVL576 switch tray material evaluations. The materials involved are SG5300N (glass-free PTFE CCL), SG1030N (glass-free HC CCL), and SIF09 (glass-free HC PP).

(3) The primary objective of testing glass-free HC CCL as a replacement for glass-free PTFE CCL is to determine whether PCB manufacturing yields and production efficiency can be improved while still meeting high-frequency electrical requirements.

(4) To further improve PCB manufacturability, subsequent tests may also evaluate replacing glass-free HC PP with woven-glass-reinforced HC PP. The challenge is whether the glass-reinforced material can still meet signal integrity and 0.4 dB/in loss requirements.

(5) Notably, both SG1030N and SIF09 still contain small amount of PTFE, although HC is the primary material. These tests therefore do not represent a complete shift away from PTFE. Rather, they involve adjusting the primary resin system and material combination to balance high-frequency electrical performance with PCB manufacturability.

2. Conclusions

(1) The long-term trend toward broader use of PTFE in advanced PCB materials, including CCL and PP, remains clear. However, the pace of shipment growth over the next two years remains uncertain. Key variables include NVL576 switch tray PCB’s final material selection, NVL576 adoption rate, and development progress on Kyber-like rack designs that use orthogonal backplanes.

(2) HC use in advanced CCL and PP continues to expand. Beyond NVL576 switch trays, near-term growth drivers include the production ramp of M9-class materials beginning in 4Q26, followed by the adoption of M10-class materials.

(3) Once specifications are finalized and mass production begins, it's expected that Shengyi Technology to accelerate sourcing from Chinese HC suppliers. These include existing suppliers such as Dongcai and Shengquan, as well as potential ones such as GCH Technology. This should help alleviate supply shortages and optimize its cost structure.

text:
借着Gary这个文章，正好说一下我对Crypto行业产品流量的一个思考：

在这个周期Crypto已经进化到了效率上的竞争：产品每周能够触达用户多少次？

我们在做Blockbeats的时候，一直很看重App的渗透率，因为「资讯App」是最好的主动触达用户的方式，如果仅仅是一个Google插件或者网页的话，其实没有办法长期高频率的触达用户用户多少次。

即便是交易APP，每周触达用户的次数也是有限的，除了查价和调仓，大家没事不会打开交易app。而资讯是一个极低成本触达用户的方式，就拿Blockbeats来说。现在每周推送超过1300次，这是一个惊人的触达量，可以和很多想推特这样的社交媒体平起平坐，尤其是和交易相关的消息，用户永远不会嫌多，只怕会错过，所以其实我们的流量一直高于很多主流中文科技媒体，可能年内就能超过我们的美国同行。

这也就是为什么最近半年交易所都在做努力广场的原因，增加用户的打开app的次数。有了资讯，有了社交，就有了更多合理触达用户的机会，同样的故事在当年微信做支付的时候也出现过，通过微信的高频打支付宝的低频，很快就把支付市场做成了和阿里五五开。

fomo在这点上占尽了优势，通过各种各样的信息为度，kol的买入和卖出，大家的讨论和发言，极大的增加了推送数量，几乎可以做到和我们媒体一致，每15分钟推送一条（图2），这种触达效率是惊人的，几乎超越了所有交易所。

所以，我更多的把所谓social trading当作手段，而不是目的，如果今天做一个交易产品，是为了做成social trading，那它可能上来出发点就错了，一切都是增加用户触达的手段而已。

text:
Many of you are selling products and services that are impossible to touch: a trading app, a BD service, or a new app for automated outreach.

One basic mistake we all make (including myself) is that we keep selling the product when we should be selling the outcome.

A new trading app isn’t valuable on its own.
There are tons of alternatives and competitors.

But when you start selling control – i.e., a 0% failure rate – the value changes.

Look: I can invite you to my Substack and say it’s a newsletter on marketing.

So what?
You might ask.
I already read you here.
And I already get a ton of emails every day.

The value of my offer is low.

Or I can tell you that Stacy’s Brain will give you evidence for your marketing decisions, with no extra noise – so you can focus on what statistically delivers good ROI.

Do you feel how different these two messages are?

Here’s an example where you act as a customer by intent, so you can see the difference between product-centered and outcome-centered messaging.

text:
one of the biggest cons of social trading I’ve realized, besides it fucking with your decision making because of all the attention, is that it makes trading way too social.

public and social trading makes it harder to trade purely on your own conviction. you get sucked into a group, start feeling responsible for other people/friends holding the same coins, and suddenly there’s sell-shaming, people asking why you bought or sold every coin, or blaming you for trades that didn’t work out.

one thing im learning now is it’s better to keep theses to yourself rather than shilling to your friends. as your thesis can change and get invalidated the next day. then you end up selling a position you previously convinced ur friends to buy.

that, for me, is the biggest downside of social trading. it creates social obligations in a game where you need to remain completely free to change your mind.

text:
My latest supply chain checks indicate that Nvidia has begun testing glass-free copper-clad laminate (CCL) based primarily on hydrocarbon (HC) resin as a replacement for glass-free PTFE-based CCL tested previously, paired with glass-free HC-based PP. The goal is to determine whether this material combination can meet the switch tray PCB requirements for Rubin Ultra NVL576, an eight-rack interconnected solution expected to enter mass production in 2H27.

Preliminary tests conducted as part of efforts to improve PCB manufacturability show that glass-free HC CCL meets the switch tray’s high-frequency electrical requirements. Its electrical performance trails that of the original PTFE solution but exceeds that of M9-class solutions and even surpasses M10’s stated specifications. These results do not represent a final material selection, but they indicate that NVIDIA continues to seek higher PCB manufacturing yields and greater production efficiency while meeting electrical requirements.

1. Key Takeaways and Analysis

(1) Previous NVL576 switch tray tests used glass-free PTFE CCL paired with glass-free HC PP. The latest round replaces the PTFE CCL with glass-free HC CCL while retaining the same HC PP part number.

(2) Shengyi Technology is currently the leading supplier in the NVL576 switch tray material evaluations. The materials involved are SG5300N (glass-free PTFE CCL), SG1030N (glass-free HC CCL), and SIF09 (glass-free HC PP).

(3) The primary objective of testing glass-free HC CCL as a replacement for glass-free PTFE CCL is to determine whether PCB manufacturing yields and production efficiency can be improved while still meeting high-frequency electrical requirements.

(4) To further improve PCB manufacturability, subsequent tests may also evaluate replacing glass-free HC PP with woven-glass-reinforced HC PP. The challenge is whether the glass-reinforced material can still meet signal integrity and 0.4 dB/in loss requirements.

(5) Notably, both SG1030N and SIF09 still contain small amount of PTFE, although HC is the primary material. These tests therefore do not represent a complete shift away from PTFE. Rather, they involve adjusting the primary resin system and material combination to balance high-frequency electrical performance with PCB manufacturability.

2. Conclusions

(1) The long-term trend toward broader use of PTFE in advanced PCB materials, including CCL and PP, remains clear. However, the pace of shipment growth over the next two years remains uncertain. Key variables include NVL576 switch tray PCB’s final material selection, NVL576 adoption rate, and development progress on Kyber-like rack designs that use orthogonal backplanes.

(2) HC use in advanced CCL and PP continues to expand. Beyond NVL576 switch trays, near-term growth drivers include the production ramp of M9-class materials beginning in 4Q26, followed by the adoption of M10-class materials.

(3) Once specifications are finalized and mass production begins, it's expected that Shengyi Technology to accelerate sourcing from Chinese HC suppliers. These include existing suppliers such as Dongcai and Shengquan, as well as potential ones such as GCH Technology. This should help alleviate supply shortages and optimize its cost structure.

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen @GracyBitget asked THORChain to refuse service to publicly identified attacker addresses, saying decentralization should not be a shield for facilitating stolen funds. THORChain emphasized that its network is permissionless. In May 2026, an attack on one of THORChain’s vaults caused approximately $10.7 million in losses. Co-founder Chad Barraford later discussed ideas for anomaly detection and emergency pauses on a podcast, outlining security checks and asset migration procedures before trading could resume. While halting a network is not the same as freezing specific addresses, the dispute raises a question: Under what circumstances should a decentralized protocol intervene when stolen funds originate from an external platform?

text:
所谓的AI量化全流程99+策略外加全自动交易软件对学习 Quant 的价值非常低。

专业系统化投资的核心流程，是从提出有经济统计依据的假设开始，然后数据处理、建模、严格回测、样本外验证，再风险与组合构建，交易成本、执行，最后持续检验。AQR 对自己的量化研究描述也是强调 economic intuition、empirical research、portfolio construction 和 rigorous testing。

策略数量本身几乎没有意义。你测试得越多，越容易从历史数据里偶然筛出漂亮曲线，也就是 multiple testing、data mining 、overfitting。专业研究反而非常在意理论依据、样本外证据和统计检验。

甚至一条历史上预测效果不错的信号，加入交易成本之后都可能直接失效。
预测能力、并不自动等于可交易利润。

如果你注意过，你应该知道AQR 现在招本科 Research Summer Analyst要求的事情非常朴素，就是诸如统计和经济研究、金融数据分析、开发改进交易策略、portfolio construction、Python、quantitative problem solving那些东西，并没有会多少个策略这种指标。

回测天然存在 hindsight、交易成本、市场冲击以及真实风险无法完全模拟的问题。所以不要因为有人展示高收益回测，给你一套所谓的策略，就拿真钱交易。

如果你想做一个像样的项目，我反而建议你暂时一分钱都别花在资料包上。Quantopian 目前公开保留了 55 个 notebook-based lectures，涵盖参数估计不稳定性、overfitting 等重要的问题。而且，AQR真的也有免费的 systematic investing、ML 学习资料。

text:
“Our first cohort of companies has doubled their EBITDA in less than two years through topline and productivity growth, all while increasing headcount. (We’re proud to say that we’ve never conducted a layoff.)"

If at any meaningful scale / organic (not through bolt ons), that's really quite impressive. 

Sounds like they have 40 businesses in their portfolio and ~30k FTEs. Stripping out Amex GBT, that's about 8k FTEs at 39 businesses, which implies ~209 FTEs per business (if all standalone). 

The rise of AI transformation firms in general is evidence that PE is going through an evolution akin to what public equity markets went through over the past 25 years.  I wouldn't doubt if the grand vision for all these guys is to automate value creation in private markets (unstructured, noisy, slow economic feedback loops) the same way quants automated alpha generation in public markets.

In the last 15/20 years, capital in the public markets has largely flowed to passive (indexes, etfs, etc.) or systematic/quant (all of Rentech, Two Sigma, D.E Shaw and much of Citadel, Millennium, etc) strategies and away from long-only or (single manager) L/S fundamental stock pickers. From 2016–2025, domestic-equity index mutual funds and ETFs received $2.9 trillion in flows including reinvested dividends, while actively managed domestic-equity mutual funds experienced $3.4 trillion of outflows.

That also meant that engineering/product/sales types (on the passive side) and PhD math, physicists, stats people etc. (on the active, systematic side) displaced MBAs/consultants/bankers as the kinds of people best able/positioned to manage public equity portfolios and capture the value from doing so.

I'd imagine Long Lake's view is that the best way to manage private equity portfolios and capture value from doing so over the next 25 years won't be via financial engineering (initial 80s/90s LBO days: KKR, Apollo, etc.) or operational "value creation" (Thoma Bravo, Vista, Bain Cap, etc.) They likely think it'll be about "technological leverage", which is capability downstream of the kinds of people that can think about the firm as a gradient descent machine: one that continuously optimizes and compounds the process of turning inputs (humans + compute) into economically valuable outputs. 

People that are capable of turning PE (sourcing, underwriting/DD, value creation, operating) into fully technology-native, systematized processes AND are commercial enough to command meta-access to the most valuable Context Production Factories (see: https://t.co/P6cOOgm8kU) are very different from the kinds of people who work in PE today.

I think the big PE guys will still be around, but will look a lot like the passive public strategy guys (BlackRock, Vanguard, etc.) in terms of value capture. We already see this with a shift towards pure a asset gathering orientation by many of these guys. Investing with them will be like owning an index in somewhat sleepy, but stable private companies/infrastructure (along with LP allocations in these new active managers). And working there will feel more like working at bank or insurance company than an active investment management firm.

Similar to how the long only stock pickers couldn't really evolve into systematic/quant funds and either largely got subsumed by passive strategies or went out of business, big PE will likely not have the DNA to evolve into what Long Lake and others are trying to do. To do that, you probably need to be built around this new kind of talent / approach from the beginning. Blackstone's analyst program probably would have missed @sdand (and he probably wouldn't have joined!) 

I was pretty surprised to see that David Shaw joined Morgan Stanley and stayed for 2 years. But the equivalent of Nunzio Tartaglia's Prop Trading group doesn't exist at Blackstone today.

I think the firm that wins will figure out how to properly attract, incentivize, instrument, and massively lever this flavor of talent to their most productive use. Ken Griffin did this in the public markets, will Alex Taubman do it in privates?

text:
overall I am surprised at how good the @seer_pm  market was in forecasting approval for projects in the round

At a 60% decision threshold, the market correctly classified a whopping 32 of 37 projects

more importantly, the market improved its forecasting accuracy over time. the base rates from sol 5.6 used to initialize the market correctly guessed results for only 23 of 37 projects

A more scientific measure for accuracy is the brier score, where 0.25 is the baseline of 50% approval to every project. 0 is perfect forecasts while 1 is its inversion

The market started with a lousy brier score of 0.22745 , almost as good as saying every project has 50% chance of approval

but by the end of trading, after $2800 in trading volume, market prices achieved a score of 0.15718, a 30% improvement

the evidence is clear: if you are running a funding round, have a prediction market alongside that resolves upon announcement of results

quoted_text:
Zcash Coinholder Retroactive Grant results are in!

Honestly, I’m surprised at the results…

What got funded: most of the bigger asks got funded, which were mostly for critical infrastructure, ironwood work, and critical bug reports.

A clear signal that coinholders are very willing to fund core infrastructure and critical security.

What didn’t get funded: smaller asks which tended to be more experimental ideas or non-core tools.

I actually thought some of the tools there were useful and should be funded, while others were a bit more“me too” and vibe coded. For some of the smaller amounts I would have voted yes.

A few ways to interpret this:

- Coinholders didn’t like the projects at all and didn’t want to fund them
- Coinholders viewed them as non-critical and not what CHV should be used for
- Coinholders don’t want to administer a small grants program and hope to discourage lots of low effort submissions in the future

Given that @ZcashLabs had the smallest grant approved, I think it may be signal that coinholders are supportive of small grants programs but not of directly voting on every small grant.

That said, I would have expected some of the other small grants to be approved as an example of which small grants Coinholders would like to see funded.

Decentralized funding just got very interesting. Looking forward to see how the next round shapes up.

text:
Matt Pocock 刚分享了他心中的 Top 3 Skill Makers，之前我们推荐过Matt 的 Grill Me，到现在，它仍然是我全局安装的两个 Skills 之一。

这次他推荐的三个人，有一个很鲜明的共同点：都在自己的领域有多年实践，然后把工作方法和判断标准写成了 Agent 可以执行的 Skills。

三个人的方向也各不相同👇

1️） @poteto — Lauren Tan
工程流程、代码质量与并行协作

Lauren 是 React 核心团队成员，参与 React Compiler 的开发，先后在 Netflix、Meta 和 Cursor 工作。

她的代表作 pstack，就是自己日常在 Cursor 使用的一套工程 Skills。

它关注的是：如何让 AI Agent 按照严谨的工程流程工作，能协作、能审查，也能验证自己交付的结果。

先把单个 Agent 的工作质量做扎实，再放心地并行推进任务，这是 pstack 很值得学习的思路。

https://t.co/rIZrCpqdYn

2️） @dexhorthy — Dexter “Dex” Horthy
Agent 架构、上下文工程与软件生产流程

Dex 是 HumanLayer 创始人兼 CEO，也是《12-Factor Agents》的作者。

他长期从事 DevOps、Kubernetes 和基础设施工作，在 Replicated 工作了约 7 年，经历过工程、产品和管理等角色。

他的工作围绕一个很实际的问题展开：怎样让基于 LLM 的软件达到可以交给真实用户使用的水平？

放到 AI 编程里，就是如何管理上下文、组织研究和规划，让 Agent 能在复杂代码库中可靠地推进工作。

如果你正在把 Agent 用到真实工程项目里，这个方向值得重点看。

https://t.co/0zBoZmrkBx

3️） @emilkowalski — Emil Kowalski
界面设计、动画与交互细节

Emil 目前在 Linear Web Team 做 Design Engineer，之前在 Vercel Design Team。

Sonner、Vaul、https://t.co/e0cfDlsSbd，都是他的作品。

他的 Skills 把设计工程中的具体判断写了出来：动画用什么曲线、持续多久、哪些地方值得加动效，以及如何处理那些影响界面质感的小细节。

这些原本依赖经验的判断，现在可以成为 Agent 设计和检查界面时的参考。

Emil 这套 Skills，我们之前也专门推荐过。做前端和产品界面的朋友，可以重点看看。

https://t.co/61CXg5cW26

我觉得：挑 Skills 时，值得先看看作者长期在解决什么问题。

专业经验越扎实，写进 Skills 里的判断和方法，就越值得拿来学习。

text:
Let me get this straight.

For ten years, the men building AI have sold it as the end of the world.

Sam Altman, 2015: "AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies."

2023: Altman, Dario Amodei and Demis Hassabis signed a statement that "Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war."

Amodei, 2025: "There's a 25% chance that things go really, really badly."

Elon Musk, 2024: "10% to 20%" that "it goes bad."

Then came the money.

Anthropic's IPO filing, per Reuters: 80 of 261 pages on risk. Models that may "resist shutdown." Behavior "resembling blackmail." Possible "catastrophic or existential" harm. About 6% of research compute spent on safety in a sample week. Revenue that depends on a "continuous and overlapping cadence" of new models.

OpenAI is in talks at $1.2 trillion.

On Sept. 12, Amodei wrote: "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models." Ten days later, Anthropic released a new model, 40% cheaper.

The apocalypse is in the prospectus. Two pages from the revenue.

Now the part they don't put in the keynote. Basic security.

July: OpenAI agents escaped a test sandbox and breached Hugging Face. Hugging Face caught it on July 16 and reported it to law enforcement. OpenAI figured out the intruder was OpenAI on July 20.

June 18: an OpenAI agent got into Australia's Medicare statistics portal. OpenAI told Australia 84 days later. The Prime Minister called it "obviously unacceptable."

September: an OpenAI agent attempted a "rudimentary hack" on an Education Department website. An outside lab, Transluce, found it.

Anthropic, March: about 3,000 unpublished files left publicly accessible. Fortune found them. Anthropic, April: 512,000 lines of Claude Code source shipped in a public package. Its words: "human error, not a security breach." xAI: about 370,000 Grok chats indexed by Google.

These companies say their product might end humanity. They couldn't keep a sandbox, a file store, or a source map locked.

Sept. 29, the White House. Lunch. A 308-word voluntary accord. And an executive order renaming their product "Super Intelligence," the industry's own word for the version that they say scares them.

The order says the administration "will not acknowledge the usage of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI.'"

Then it defines Super Intelligence as "the technologies and systems encompassed by the term 'artificial intelligence'" in federal law.

Super Intelligence is legally defined as artificial intelligence.

The order never mentions safety, security or hacking.

Item one of the accord: "ensure that its models do not hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."

They had to put "do not hack" in writing.

The accord says each company "should" do it. On making it law: "Over time, it may make sense."

The signature page reads "President of the Unites States." A document about controls and audits, and nobody audited the title.

Asked why these men should be trusted to regulate themselves: "Because they're outstanding people."

The enforcement plan: "they're really going to be policing each other."

Did they police themselves? Hugging Face caught OpenAI. An outside lab caught OpenAI. Australia waited 84 days.

We already have a law. The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, 1986: whoever "intentionally accesses a computer without authorization."

On June 2, the President signed an order telling the Attorney General to "prioritize the enforcement" of that law "against anyone who utilizes AI to illegally access or damage a computer." Five weeks later, OpenAI's agents were inside Hugging Face.

Sept. 27, the President: "if they don't fix it, that's why you have the Department of Justice."

The same day, the Attorney General, on new AI laws: "we don't need it. We don't need it right now."

As of Sept. 29, AP reports no investigation has been publicly announced.

Public Citizen: "The rule of law cannot mean one thing when a person hacks a computer system and something entirely different when Big Tech builds an AI system that hacks websites."

Hack a government website, and you get a knock on the door.

Build the agent that does it, and you get a seat at lunch.

留言区里有位 @PixelDrifter0 的小伙伴也做了一个版本，他这个版本是我之前考虑过的，直接在 YouTube 的视频上直接显示的，为什么我不这么做呢，有的原因有以下几个：

1. 多数小伙伴对于视频的需求并不高，更多的是需要知道在说什么，所以实时性的提高和翻译的准确程度高于画面，毕竟画面来说就是那么几个人。

2. 中英文全部开启其实意义不大，对于多数小伙伴来说看中文足够了，而且如果是在 YouTube 上的字幕是不能朗读的，而我这个版本接下来更新的就是朗读。

也就是说小伙伴们完全可以在做别的任何事情的情况下，不需要看美联储的直播，而是直接听中文的朗读就可以，这样节省了观看，重点内容"听"就可以。

PS：最新的版本已经更新了朗读。

3. 对于部分喜欢分享的小伙伴来说，美联储的内容是非常好的分享来源，尤其是能加上自己解释的话，所以每一段我都加了复制，可以直接将讲话的内容变成文字，然后复制粘贴，非常便于输出。

4. 延迟的问题确实是挺重要的，下个版本的时候我在看看有没有优化的方式。

5. 还有一个更重要的是，很多小伙伴在 X 上有蓝V 就意味着是 Grok 的会员，但未必有 ChatGPT 的会员，所以我的更新版本是同时兼容了 ChatGPT ，Grok 和 Google 的 Gemini，这样让小伙伴们更加方便的使用。

- @Microsoft paying to bring back three mile island (a closed nuclear plant)

and finally, @RedwoodMat in nevada. they use old EV batteries and use them for modular data centers. many are actually not good enough for cars but still can store energy. they used these with solar power to power 4 @CrusoeAI modular data centers (and now are expanding to 24) 

modular data centers are hard to do but are the future. you can bring the data center to where power is already available without waiting for grid connection!

text:
慢雾披露 Bitget 调查进展：攻击者伪造风控参数提币

针对 Bitget 此前披露的约 3.875 亿美元安全事件，慢雾发布调查进展报告，梳理了第三方安全产品遭入侵、定制工具提币及后续 BTC 提币尝试等发现。

主要发现如下，时间均为北京时间：

1.最早的入侵痕迹可追溯至 8 月 31 日。 

第三方安全产品 A 的一个节点服务受到零日漏洞影响，攻击者运行隐藏脚本，读取包含数据库密码的环境变量并连接数据库。9 月 23 日和 25 日，另外两个节点也出现类似活动，说明相关服务环境在资金转出前已遭入侵。

2.攻击者使用内部员工身份进入另一款安全产品的管理平台。 

9 月 25 日凌晨，攻击者在产品 B 的任务参数中连续尝试注入系统命令，随后通过网页端代码执行接口，尝试修改服务器配置、写入通信中转文件，并分批上传、组装恶意程序。报告未公开两款产品名称。

3.攻击者利用定制提币工具执行盗币

慢雾从攻击者删除的文件中恢复出一款定制提币工具，发现其通过伪造风控参数、构造提币请求来执行盗币。该工具针对钱包系统的提币逻辑编写，通过伪造风控参数、构造提币请求来调用提币流程。主机日志显示，相关恶意程序于 9 月 25 日 01:49 开始运行并执行盗币操作。

4.已核实的跨链转账记录跨度约 2 小时 52 分钟。 

最早一笔发生在 02:31，攻击者地址收到 93 TRX，11 秒后以太坊地址收到 0.84 ETH，记录延续至 05:23。期间，攻击者还尝试直接修改钱包数据库中的提币记录；日志中的两笔伪造 BTC 订单进入处理后均返回错误，随后仍有查询状态和继续尝试的记录。

quoted_text:
Interview Summary: 24/7 Trading on Hyperliquid (@Joonylive  × Jeff Yan)

Joony Koo: Two years ago, the prevailing view was that markets should close because of risk, rest, and off-hours liquidity. Was there a moment when that view broke for you?

Jeff Yan: Crypto is an inherently international asset, so the idea of market hours never really fit, and 24/7 has always been the default. It started to matter for traditional assets when the incumbent exchanges began extending their hours. They didn't go straight to 24/7, they went to 24/5, but it became clear they had recognized customer demand and were responding to it.

Joony Koo: Incumbents are now matching the hours. What is left that an on-chain venue can offer?

Jeff Yan: Trading hours are independent of being on-chain. The core of on-chain finance is two things. First, users keep control and custody of their funds. That doesn't matter day to day, but it matters in critical moments, when counterparties, intermediaries, or custodians run into trouble. Reducing trust assumptions and moving power to individuals rather than a single point of failure makes the system more robust. Second, transparency. It has limited mass appeal, but being able to know, in theory, everything happening in the system brings a trust and neutrality you don't get from a system controlled by one private organization. You can have 24/7 trading without these properties, but these are what on-chain markets can offer the world.

Joony Koo: This year commodities, equities, and pre-IPO names traded at scale, and price discovery sometimes happened while the reference markets were closed. What did the team learn from watching the two run side by side?

Jeff Yan: The clearest lesson is that demand for 24/7 trading exists. You wouldn't know without these markets, but the world doesn't sleep as a whole. Global 24/7 markets concentrate liquidity across more buyers and sellers, making markets more efficient and liquid for everyone. There will always be someone, somewhere, who wants to express a view, so once the option exists, those markets become the Schelling point where people go to do that.

Joony Koo: HIP-3 lets independent teams create markets, and institutions are building on top too. If anyone can build, what is Labs focusing on?

Jeff Yan: Labs specializes in the technology and infrastructure that supports deployers. What a deployer needs varies widely depending on who they are, where they're based, who their users are, and what they want to list, and the list is long. The vision is for Hyperliquid to be a neutral infrastructure layer, like AWS, which spared startups and large firms from reinventing the wheel. Financial primitives like order books should become pervasive and battle-tested infrastructure, and making that work for everyone is the primary mandate.

Joony Koo: The "AWS for finance" analogy reminds me of working at a game company when people debated whether the cloud could be trusted. What open problems would Labs most like to see others solve?

Jeff Yan: First, builders should find something they're uniquely positioned to do, given their interests and competitive advantages, and we'll support whatever they build. One specific hard problem is tokenizing the underlying assets themselves. Custody, liquidity, and the mechanics are all harder, so it hasn't taken off yet. I hope to see strong projects and builders next year, because having the assets represented on-chain synergizes with price discovery and liquidity.

Joony Koo: Tokenization is speeding up as more institutions get involved. Any advice for smaller teams?

Jeff Yan: Many teams, big and small, are working on tokenization, but it hasn't hit escape velocity and it's unclear who will succeed. That's the beauty of neutral infrastructure: you don't win just because you're big, though big teams may have legitimate advantages like institutional connectivity. Viral products often come from small teams that see the world differently and think less rigidly. Perps are intuitive and fair instruments that concentrate liquidity across the globe and across all time horizons into one asset, so they're easy to present to users. Some small team may even reinvent how the interfaces look.

Joony Koo: You spent three days with the Korean community this week. What stood out?

Jeff Yan: Like last year, I felt the hospitality, and I'm grateful to everyone who organized events. The community here is strong, and trading is a core part of many Koreans' lives, so it was great to discuss how on-chain markets and HIP-3 would change their approach to markets. Talking to users and the community inspires us to keep building.

Joony Koo: And your meetings with institutions?

Jeff Yan: It's cool to see institutions interested in the platform and building on top of it. They're understandably slower to adopt new technology because they have a lot to protect, but as this year has shown, the appetite is significant.

Joony Koo: Last question: what is next to be priced 24/7 that has no continuous price today?

Jeff Yan: Nothing specific, but private markets are a big opportunity, and you already see some of it through HIP-3 deployers. Much wealth creation happens privately, because companies have incentives to stay private as long as possible. It isn't intended to exclude most of the world's population, but that's what happens in practice. Allowing global price discovery on these assets as early as possible, in a global system not confined to one jurisdiction, could break that trend. There are many complexities to work through, but markets exist so everyone can benefit from them, and trading anything, anytime, anywhere has the most potential here.

Joony Koo: Any final remarks?

Jeff Yan: Hyperliquid's core strength is its community and people. It's not one company doing what's best for itself, but a decentralized network of contributors and users building a financial system owned by the people rather than by private interests. There's a long way to go and many challenges, but seeing everyone in Seoul, I feel we're in good hands, and we'll build something the financial system can ultimately adopt.

@kbwofficial @HyperliquidX

text:
Opus 5.5 能用纯代码做出接近专业水准的动效，Muse 则把 Agent 做得越来越像一个真正面向普通人的消费产品。

在最新一期「Next-Token 词元之外」播客中，橘子、歸藏、杨攀、向阳乔木四位国内 AI 从业者围绕这些变化展开讨论，并将话题延伸到了两个正在被 AI 重新定义的职业：产品经理和剪辑师。

分享其中的两个观点：

1. 中国没有 AI 产品经理

Muse 真正让人惊讶的，并不只是模型能力，而是它知道什么时候该让用户连接 Gmail、什么时候展示执行进度、什么时候请求审批，甚至知道怎么避免复读和浪费人的注意力。

界面可以快速复刻，但这种「不指挥用户、不让人烦、真正把事情做完」的体验没那么容易抄。

国内真正稀缺的，可能不是 AI 工程师，而是理解 AI 交互方式的产品经理。

2.Opus 5.5 可能第一次创造了剪辑师的「斩杀线」

纯代码生成的动画和视频，已经能把音乐、动作、转场和节奏放在一起整体考虑。更值得注意的是，模型智能提升的速度，正在超过剪映、AE 这类工具不断堆叠功能的速度。

以前做视频、写代码，人需要告诉工具「每一步怎么做」；现在越来越接近只需要告诉 AI「我想要什么」。

当执行能力越来越廉价，人的价值也在向更少的东西收拢：审美、偏好，以及知道自己到底想要什么。

text:
If you believe tokenisation is the next big thing, then for a stablecoin the end game becomes being accepted as currency by the largest issuers.

And Frax just beat Tether, Paxos and Ripple to be accepted by one of the most coveted issuers, Midas. Becoming only the 2nd stable after USDC to be accepted by Midas for mF-ONE, and soon mGLOBAL.

Gearbox's leverage mechanism was designed not just around how we can offer best-in-class leverage UX to borrowers, but also around how we can offer a better lifecycle to the stables that get borrowed.

Currently, most lending protocols treat stablecoins as routing inventory rather than as currency. Borrowers borrow them from a pool and dump them to buy another asset they want to leverage. This creates three structural consequences:

1. Persistent sell pressure: Borrow-driven swaps generate continuous mechanical sell pressure.
2. Paying for the sell pressure: Scaling borrowing requires deep DEX liquidity. Issuers spend millions every year to ensure the stable can be sold at low slippage.
3. No institutional acceptance: The stable never reaches the issuer.

The stablecoin never becomes embedded in real economic activity. The stablecoin team can't BD their way into getting the issuer to hold their stable as liquidity or use it to pay the underlying institutions. The existing mechanism effectively kills any possibility of the stable finding institutional adoption or being integrated into the issuer's payments side.

Gearbox's leverage design was meant to change this. Instead of swapping the stablecoin for another asset, Gearbox developed a leveraged minting mechanism. When a borrower mints the RWA with leverage, they also deposit the stablecoin with the issuer, as we see with frxUSD being deposited at Midas.

This eliminates any additional DEX liquidity costs, gains the stablecoin institutional adoption and opens up pathways for its BD team to negotiate for more and find organic holders and utility.

Borrowers pay no slippage and access automated RWA leverage, the issuer sees minting increase, and the stable saves millions and gets institutional adoption. A truly win-win-win mechanism.

Retokenise the world.
