@Sibos  week, Miami. On Wednesday, 30 September, we are hosting the Miami chapter of @DeComputeConf  2026 with LF Decentralized Trust : a close door roundtable on bank-scale digital asset adoption.

We are putting three questions on the table: 

1. First, post-quantum design for digital assets: what and how FIs and banks should migrate first, and how, without adding to the HSM, MPC and cold-storage fragmentation they already live with.

2. Second, a fully bank-owned custody and tokenization stack: how a bank keeps control of the critical parts of the stack and reuses the risk, compliance and governance systems it already trusts, instead of building a parallel world for tokenized assets.

3. Third, distributed cold custody with MPC inside HSMs: key sovereignty, recovery and custodian independence when a signing key never exists in one place.

Joining the conversation:

@dschwed , CTO, @OpenReserveBank 
Mark Rakhmilevich, Group VP, @Oracle 
Bharat Gupta, Head of Digital Assets, Financial Services, @Infosys 
Ishan Singh, Senior Principal, Digital Assets, @Google 
Hart Montgomery, CTO, @lfdecentralized 
@stablemaximus , CEO, @ubyx_ .
@hadleystern. Silence Laboratories, and
@jaysprakash  alongside senior leaders from GSIBs, OCC-regulated banks and custodians.

The discussion runs under the Chatham House Rule.

Wednesday, 30 September, 3:00 to 4:15 pm.

Thanks to @danielabarbosa  and LF Decentralized Trust for support!

@Enter_Elysium calls itself the only value accretive L2 for Hyperliquid. Its sequencer fees send 0% to Hyperliquid: 50% buys and burns KNTQ, 25% goes to apps, 25% to the @Kinetiq_xyz treasury.

The case for HYPE is indirect. HYPE is the gas token, and Elysium reads HyperCore orderbooks on call gas. Arb against those books would add HyperCore spot fees, and native USDC would feed AQAv2.

Size it. Kinetiq's own post puts HyperEVM's contribution at about $1M a year. @HyperliquidX fees are $73.0M over 30 days, about $888M annualised, and AQAv2 is estimated at $182M a year.

The speed gap is real on paper. Docs target 100 to 200 ms blocks and 300 Mgas/s, against HyperEVM's 1 s blocks and 3M gas. One third-party testnet measurement on Sep 26 found 420 to 600 ms. Unverified.

What would falsify it: mainnet, targeted around Oct 20, pulling quote-refresh flow through HyperCore at a size that shows up in spot fees.

Does a chain that keeps none of its fees for HYPE still move the token?

text:
Jeff 今天在首尔这场访谈，最值得关注的两个方向：金融界的 AWS，以及尚未上市的资产。🐱

几个重点整理如下：

🟠 全天候交易的需求，已经得到验证

世界各地的人不会同时入睡。传统市场休市时，依然有人需要交易、表达判断。Jeff 认为，24/7 市场能把全球买卖双方聚集起来，改善流动性与价格发现。

链上金融还有两项核心价值：用户掌握资金，以及系统透明可验证。当托管方或中间机构出问题时，这些特性尤其重要。

🟠 Hyperliquid 要做金融界的 AWS

HIP-3 让独立团队创建市场，Labs 则专注底层技术与基础设施。

Jeff 希望订单簿等金融基础组件，成为大家可以直接使用、经过充分检验的公共设施，让创业团队和大机构都能减少重复建设。

🟠 下一道难题：让底层资产本身上链

Jeff 特别提到资产代币化。托管、流动性和具体运作机制都很复杂，这个领域尚未真正起飞。

他希望明年能看到优秀团队做出进展，让链上的资产与价格发现、流动性进一步结合。

🟠 小团队依然有机会

大机构拥有资源与行业关系，小团队也有自己的优势：想法更灵活，更容易做出不同的产品。

包括交易界面在内，很多东西都有重新设计的空间。

🟠 未上市资产，是他看好的大机会

公司保持非上市状态的时间越来越长，大量财富创造发生在普通人难以参与的阶段。

Jeff 认为，让这些资产更早进入全球价格发现体系，有机会扩大参与范围。HIP-3 已经出现相关探索，但仍有很多复杂问题需要解决。

🟠 机构兴趣明显，采用需要时间

Jeff 表示，机构对平台及其上层应用的兴趣很强。它们需要保护的资产和业务更多，接受新技术的速度也会更慢。

Hyperliquid🫡
author: 0xMaxs
quoted_text:
远程记者吉米给大家带来采访摘要：

【Hyperliquid 上的 7×24 小时交易】

Joony Koo（@Joonylive）× Jeff Yan（@chameleon_jeff）

Joony Koo：
两年前，市场上的主流观点还是：市场就应该有休市时间，因为需要控制风险、让参与者休息，同时也要考虑非交易时段的流动性问题。你是什么时候开始觉得，这套逻辑已经不成立了？

Jeff Yan：
加密资产天然就是全球化的资产，所以“固定交易时段”这个概念其实一直都不太适用于 Crypto。对加密市场来说，7×24 小时交易从一开始就是默认状态。

真正让我觉得这件事开始影响传统金融，是当传统交易所开始延长交易时间的时候。它们并没有一步到位变成 7×24，而是先走向了 24×5，但这已经说明了一件事：传统交易所意识到了用户确实存在这样的需求，而且正在主动回应这种需求。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
现在传统交易所也开始延长交易时间了。那么相比它们，链上交易平台还能提供什么独特价值？

Jeff Yan：
其实，能不能 7×24 小时交易，跟是不是链上并没有直接关系。
我认为链上金融真正核心的价值有两个。

第一，是用户能够真正掌控和托管自己的资产。

在大多数正常情况下，这一点可能感觉没那么重要。但到了真正关键的时刻——比如交易对手、中介机构或者托管机构出现问题时——它的重要性就会体现出来。
减少对第三方的信任假设，把控制权从单一故障点转移给个人，会让整个金融系统更加稳健。

第二，是透明度。

透明度可能不是一个对所有普通用户都有强烈吸引力的卖点，但从理论上来说，你能够知道整个系统中正在发生的一切。由此产生的信任感和中立性，是由某一家私人机构完全控制的系统很难提供的。
所以，你当然可以在没有这些特性的情况下实现 7×24 小时交易。但资产自主权和透明度，才是链上市场真正能够带给世界的东西。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
今年我们已经看到，大宗商品、股票，甚至 Pre-IPO 资产都开始出现规模化交易。有时候，在传统参考市场休市期间，链上市场甚至已经开始进行价格发现。
当你们同时观察传统市场和链上市场运行时，团队最大的收获是什么？

Jeff Yan：
最明确的一点就是：

市场对 7×24 小时交易的需求是真实存在的。

如果没有这些市场，你可能很难意识到这一点，但整个世界并不会同时进入睡眠。

全球化的 7×24 小时市场，可以把来自不同时区、不同地区的买方和卖方流动性集中到一起，从而让整个市场对所有参与者而言都更加高效、流动性也更好。

无论任何时候，世界上的某个地方，总会有人想表达自己的市场观点。

所以，只要这样一个市场存在，它最终就可能成为大家自然聚集过去进行交易的Schelling Point——也就是市场参与者自发形成共识、集中流动性的地方。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
HIP-3 允许独立团队自己创建市场，现在也已经有机构开始在 Hyperliquid 上构建产品。
既然任何人都可以来建设，那么 Hyperliquid Labs 自己最关注的是什么？

Jeff Yan：
Labs 最擅长的，是为这些市场部署者提供底层技术和基础设施。

不同 deployer 的需求差异非常大。

这取决于他们是谁、位于哪个地区、服务什么用户、希望上线什么资产……需要解决的问题其实非常多。

我们的愿景，是让 Hyperliquid 成为一个中立的金融基础设施层，有点类似 AWS。

AWS 的价值就在于，它让创业公司甚至大型企业都不需要从零开始重复建设最底层的基础设施。

金融领域也应该如此。

像订单簿这样的金融基础组件，未来应该变成一种无处不在、经过充分实战检验的公共基础设施。

而让这些基础设施真正能够服务所有人，就是 Labs 最核心的使命。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
你提到“金融版 AWS”，让我想到以前在游戏公司工作时，大家还经常争论：“云服务真的可以信任吗？”

那目前有哪些重要问题，是 Labs 最希望其他开发者去解决的？

Jeff Yan：
首先，我觉得开发者应该去寻找那些只有自己特别适合做的事情。

这取决于他们自己的兴趣、能力以及竞争优势。无论他们最终选择做什么，我们都会支持。

如果要说一个特别具体、同时又非常困难的问题，那就是：
如何真正把底层资产本身代币化。

这里面的托管、流动性以及具体运行机制都更加复杂，所以目前这个领域还没有真正大规模发展起来。

我希望明年可以看到更多优秀的项目和开发者进入这个领域。

因为一旦现实资产能够真正以链上形式存在，它们就能够和链上的价格发现以及流动性机制形成非常强的协同效应。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
随着越来越多机构进入，资产代币化正在明显加速。

对于规模比较小的团队，你有什么建议？

Jeff Yan：
现在确实已经有很多团队在做资产代币化，大公司、小团队都有。

但整个领域目前还没有真正突破临界点，我们也并不知道最终谁能够成功。

而这恰恰就是中立基础设施的魅力所在。

并不是说团队规模大，你就天然会赢。

当然，大机构确实可能拥有一些合理优势，比如更强的机构资源和金融网络。

但很多真正具有病毒式传播能力的产品，反而往往来自小团队。

因为小团队有时候能够以完全不同的方式看待这个世界，而且思维不会那么僵化。

永续合约就是一个非常好的例子。

它是一种非常直观、相对公平的金融工具，可以把全球不同地区、不同时间尺度的流动性集中到同一个资产上，因此也非常容易向用户呈现。

未来甚至可能有某个小团队，重新定义我们现在习以为常的交易界面应该长什么样。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
这周你在韩国和当地社区相处了三天，有什么让你印象特别深刻的地方？

Jeff Yan：
和去年一样，我再次感受到了韩国社区的热情好客。
我也非常感谢所有帮助组织活动的人。

这里的社区非常强大，而且对于很多韩国人来说，交易本身就是生活中非常重要的一部分。

所以能够和他们讨论链上市场，以及 HIP-3 未来可能如何改变他们参与市场的方式，是一件非常有意思的事情。

和用户、和社区直接交流，也会不断激励我们继续建设下去。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
那你和机构的交流呢？

Jeff Yan：
看到越来越多机构开始对 Hyperliquid 感兴趣，并且开始在这个平台上建设产品，这件事很令人兴奋。

当然，机构采用新技术的速度往往会更慢，这完全可以理解。

因为它们拥有大量需要保护的资产、业务和客户。

但从今年的发展来看，机构对这类产品的需求和兴趣已经非常明显了。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
最后一个问题：

还有什么目前没有连续价格的资产，下一步可能会率先进入 7×24 小时定价？

Jeff Yan：
我没有一个特别具体的答案。

但我认为，Private Markets是一个非常大的机会。

其实通过一些 HIP-3 deployer，我们现在已经开始看到这种趋势了。

当今大量财富创造其实发生在Private Markets。

因为从公司的角度来说，它们往往有动力尽可能长时间保持私有状态、不上市。

这并不是说它们主观上想把世界上绝大多数人排除在财富创造之外，但最终实际造成的结果就是如此。

如果我们能够让这些资产在更早阶段，就进入一个全球化的价格发现体系，而且这个体系并不局限于某一个司法辖区，那么我们可能有机会改变这种现状。

当然，这里面还有大量复杂问题需要解决。

但市场存在的意义，本来就应该是让所有人都有机会从中受益。

所以我认为：

任何资产、任何时间、任何地点都可以交易，可能正是这个领域最有潜力的方向。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Joony Koo：
最后还有什么想说的吗？

Jeff Yan：
Hyperliquid 最核心的优势，始终是它的社区和人。

它并不是一家企业，只想着怎么做对自己最有利的事情。

它更像是一个由大量贡献者和用户共同组成的去中心化网络，大家一起建设一个由人们自己拥有，而不是由私人利益集团掌控的金融系统。

当然，我们距离这个目标还有很长的路，也还有很多挑战需要面对。

但这次在首尔看到所有人之后，我觉得我们处在一个非常好的状态。

我相信大家最终能够一起构建出一套，真正能够被整个金融体系所采用的东西。

text:
HOOD Summit值得关注，这是Robinhood把“零售券商”进一步推向“全天候主动交易超级平台”的战略宣发，对 HOOD自身影响还是相当大的：强化“主动交易平台”定位，重点提升单用户价值（ARPU）

hood近几年已经从“免佣股票 App”转向高活跃度交易：预测市场（Q2 已贡献约 1.56 亿美元营收）、期权、加密、事件合约都在快速增长。这次发布的组合——AI Agents、周末股票交易、加密永续、财报二元合约、盘中 4 倍保证金、延长期权时段——本质是让用户交易更频繁、交易时段更长、使用杠杆更高、使用工具更复杂。

这对财务模型很关键：
可以说hood之后的增长越来越不依赖“新增开户数”，而依赖现有用户（约 2800 万资金账户）的资产规模、Gold 订阅和跨产品渗透。
未来业务增长逻辑要从“获客”转向“ARPU 扩张”：Summit 正好提供了新的产品抓手。AI Agent Apps 还可能开辟订阅/数据分成新收入。

长期看，这批产品与此前的预测市场、代币化股票、Robinhood Chain 形成一条线：把 TradFi 产品“加密化/全天候化”，再把加密原生产品（永续、Agent）带回受监管的美国零售端。如果周末交易和永续顺利落地，Robinhood 在“交易时长 × 产品广度 × 工具深度”上会明显领先传统券商。

这会让hood拉开与传统券商的差距，同时与加密平台短兵相接
Schwab、FIBKR 在托管规模、投顾、退休账户上仍强，但在产品迭代速度、加密、预测市场、AI 原生体验上明显更慢。Robinhood 选择的战场是“高活跃、高杠杆、全天候、社交化”的年轻/主动交易人群。

传统券商要么加速跟进（延长时段、推 Agent、加衍生品），要么继续守住财富管理基本盘，把高频交易份额让出。

text:
还在每个月给 TradingView 交钱？这 6 个行情工具先收藏！

TradingView 我用了很多年，但说实话，如果你主要做 Crypto，看看 K 线、订单流、足迹图、盘口热力图，现在很多免费工具已经完全够用了。

我最近重新筛了一遍，下面这 6 个各有各的绝活：

1.OpenMarket

K线只是基础，真正有意思的是订单流、流动性热力图、TPO、1 秒 K 线，还有自己的 kScript 指标系统。特别适合想看“钱到底怎么进出市场”的人。

2.GoCharting

如果你想找一个最像 TradingView，但订单流更强的，直接看它。

Footprint、Cluster、DOM、Market Profile、CVD、期权、脚本基本都有，官方称已经有 300 万+交易者。网页打开就能用，很多基础功能免费。

3.Bookmap

专门看庄家把单子挂在哪里。

它把整个订单簿直接画成热力图，哪里堆了流动性、哪里突然撤单、哪里出现吸收，一眼就能看到。

Crypto 免费版已经支持 20+ 交易所实时数据，还有 Heatmap、成交量气泡、CVD。

4.TakeProfit

GPU 图表、Footprint、TPO、Binance/Bybit 流动性热力图、Tick 图、自定义脚本都有，还能直接在图表里做交易计划。

现在有永久免费的 Freeroll，付费版也只有 20 美元/月。

5.TrendSpider

自动趋势线、形态识别、扫描器、回测、交易机器人，再加一个能直接看你图表的 AI Sidekick。

适合懒得自己画线、喜欢系统化策略的人。

但这个严格说不算免费替代品，完整平台还是要订阅。

6.Percept Labs

很多你以后看到的 Hyperliquid 终端、订单流工具、Footprint、TPO、热力图，背后可能用的就是这种东西。

做交易产品和 Vibe Coding 的可以重点研究。

text:
Researchers mathematically proved that LLM hallucinations can never be fixed.

It is Impossible.

They modeled Large Language Models as Probabilistic Turing Machines. They tested them against the absolute boundaries of computer science: incomputability, information theory, and diagonalization.

The result is absolute.

If a model relies entirely on its own internal parameters, hallucination is mathematically inevitable.

You cannot train it away. You cannot scale it away. It is a hard limit of mathematics.

But the researchers found an escape route.

They call it the "Oracle Escape".

In computer science, an oracle machine is a theoretical system capable of bypassing its own limits by querying an external source of absolute truth.

The researchers proved that the only way to break the hallucination barrier is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), giving the AI access to search the outside world in real time.

RAG isn't just a clever hack to give an AI a memory boost.

Mathematically, it acts as an "oracle machine". It forces a "computational jump" that allows the AI to escape its own inevitable delusions.

The paper ends with a brutal new rule for AI safety: Computational Class Alignment.

You must strictly match the complexity of a task to the actual compute architecture of the system.

If you ask a closed system to do an open-world task, it won't just fail.

It is mathematically guaranteed to lie to you.

.@Telegram x crypto update (via @ton_blockchain):

Validators are voting right now to move the Telegram Wallet contract into the network config itself. From here on, every Telegram wallet shares a single copy of the same code.

That means one vote = the built-in on-chain wallet updates for everyone at once. Bug fixes land instantly, for all users.

My takeaway: this design is built entirely for 1-billion-user scale. Less storage, cheaper deployment, lower fees, silent upgrades, no seed phrases. The trade-off: you give up the right to freeze your own contract version. Upgrade power now sits with validator voting.

text:
Your AI can forget a conversation and still expose it while answering.

@darkwoodslabs rise as the dark horse (pun intended) for AI and Privacy intersection.

The pitch is appealing:

Open-weight AI models, wallet login, and no stored chat transcripts. Buy credits with $USDG on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain, choose a model, and pay for what you use.

Think of it as a prepaid AI service with a crypto wallet as your account.

Darkwoods says its models run inside Intel TDX enclaves, protected computing environments designed to isolate workloads from the surrounding infrastructure.

Its attestation route publishes verifiable hardware proof. In practice, your chats live and die in the browser unless you opt into encrypted syncing.

Darkwoods pairs enclave-anchored inference with an app-level pledge not to store transcripts. But to be fari, that still isn’t a blanket guarantee that no middleman can ever glimpse what you type.

How does that compare?

@NEARProtocol AI uses a gateway that itself runs inside a TEE, alongside protected model execution. Its verification flow lets developers check that their actual encrypted connection terminates at the attested gateway.

@OpenGradient takes another approach: separate who sent the request from what it contains. An encrypted relay hides prompts from the relay and the client’s IP from the gateway.

However, upstream model providers still receive plaintext, and identity separation depends on relay/gateway non-collusion.

Then there is $DARK.

The docs mentioned that credit-purchase split sends 10% to DARK stakers, 10% to a buyback wallet, and 80% to treasury.

Compared to the rest of the ecosystem on @ponsdotfamily, Darkwoods really stands out for bundling wallet access, private inference, and token-gated payments into a single, cohesive product.

As privacy and AI agents keep converging, Dark feels like one of the more compelling protocols that actually stitches the two together in a meaningful way.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
Continuous Variational Synthesis (cVS) is a game-changer for DNA and protein design.

By training generative models in continuous space (with all lab constraints relaxed), then “rounding” them after to fit what real synthesis machines can do, cVS matches or beats classic discrete approaches—on both diversity and quality.

Benchmarks? cVS outperforms EM and PGLD baselines across enzymes, peptides, antibodies, and regulatory DNA. In one task, it generated a 9.6×10¹⁴-member DNA library, sequenced 28M reads, and showed the wet-lab results still match the in-silico targets (KSD-B≈3×10⁻⁶).

The kicker: in-silico performance translates, at petascale, to real-world synthesis. For biotech, this means LLM-style pre-train/fine-tune cycles for actual molecules—unlocking faster, broader design-build-test cycles.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/UMHGzORAIV

quoted_text:
Heads-up, staking operators: with ePBS in Glamsterdam, you won't need a sidecar (mev-boost / commit-boost) to receive 3rd-party blocks anymore. Your beacon node collects and selects bids itself, and builder preferences will natively be set in the validator client.

Generally, it is a good thing for the protocol that trusted counterparties become optional rather than required, and the default validator setup gets simpler. 

That being said, like relays, sidecars aren't expected to go away anytime soon. They'll keep being maintained and may offer more sophisticated operators extras beyond bid selection and multiplexing.

Make sure to adjust your setup before the fork, test on the upcoming testnets and watch your client releases for instructions.

text:
说下我的故事。

我算是比较早就开始跑会的，从 2016 年的上海区块链周到现在 Token 2049，算了下正好 10 年。

印象比较深的是，18 年参加石墨烯大会，在一个 EOS 生态项目展位前，有位衣着朴素的本地老头跟我说见顶了，我仔细打量他的形象气质，不像是高手，心里暗笑。

那时他喊我清仓我没听，后面迎来了尸骨无存的史诗级熊市。

10 年来，大大小小的活动参加了不少。我的经验是，跑会不应该是网友见面，蹭个大哥微信。更重要的是看和听。看这些项目、这些人在做什么，听他们在传达什么。也可以说，就是看看行业现在的状态。

就像 18 年那位老者一样，他不是来学习什么是“石墨烯”，也不是来见某个大咖、求个合影，更不是来网友面基。他更多的是站在第三方视角，给行业把脉。如果恰好碰上我这样有眼缘的年轻人，就顺便提个醒，市场过热了，该走了，或是其他判断。

当然，空了聚个餐也是无可厚非，但这不是参会的主要目的。

我想多数人和我一样，不认识什么大哥，也没有具体的事情需要在此时此地谈。区块链就像是游戏人生中的一个副本，大型区块链活动则是副本里的微观世界。这种时候，才是观行业百态的好时候。只有把这些看透摸清了，回家端起键盘时，才知道往哪下手、怎么出手。

既然做不了主角，也不稀罕去做群演；当个观察者，找到特别的人，往特别的方向去，也挺好的。

有小伙伴说线下见面加深互相的信任，这点我是 100% 同意的，所以我会说每年选香港最好，性价比很高了，或者是今年选曼谷，往年都是在迪拜，性价比也不高，但曼谷消费要便宜很多。

对于没有明确的目标，而且预算有限的小伙伴来说，每年两次香港应该是最合适的跑会了，市面上经常跑的小伙伴几乎都能见到，交易所的活动也都会在香港安排，整体预算会低很多。

单纯靠跑会积累的人脉和资源很可能只是停留在微信。多数人你会发现可能一年都说不上两句话。

霍尔木兹海峡通航受阻，会持续给能源价格和美国国内政治带来压力。越接近选举，恢复通航对川普就越有价值。伊朗这时候提出快速开放海峡的方案，也就有了争取更好条件的机会。

the market is red. oil is climbing, sending the 10 year yield and the dollar higher, which is pulling gold, bitcoin, and memes down.

it is a yield squeeze, not a structural crash. rising energy keeps yields high, which tightens liquidity across the board. risk assets take the hit first.

next, gold stops dropping (front running the top in yields). the 10 year yield caps out. btc absorbs the liquidity first and capital flows back into memes.

watch gold relative to yields, that is the signal. it is what tells me this is about to flip bullish soon, even while my port is down bad. we are not far from green days. 

beyond the macro, i am convinced proven major meme tokens on rh won't just recover, they will print new all time highs. high beta plays carry too much risk right now, so i bought a bag of the tokens i genuinely like. i probably bought too early, it keeps dipping and while the drawdowns hurt, my conviction hasn't moved.

text:
My latest supply chain checks indicate that Nvidia has begun testing glass-free copper-clad laminate (CCL) based primarily on hydrocarbon (HC) resin as a replacement for glass-free PTFE-based CCL tested previously, paired with glass-free HC-based PP. The goal is to determine whether this material combination can meet the switch tray PCB requirements for Rubin Ultra NVL576, an eight-rack interconnected solution expected to enter mass production in 2H27.

Preliminary tests conducted as part of efforts to improve PCB manufacturability show that glass-free HC CCL meets the switch tray’s high-frequency electrical requirements. Its electrical performance trails that of the original PTFE solution but exceeds that of M9-class solutions and even surpasses M10’s stated specifications. These results do not represent a final material selection, but they indicate that NVIDIA continues to seek higher PCB manufacturing yields and greater production efficiency while meeting electrical requirements.

1. Key Takeaways and Analysis

(1) Previous NVL576 switch tray tests used glass-free PTFE CCL paired with glass-free HC PP. The latest round replaces the PTFE CCL with glass-free HC CCL while retaining the same HC PP part number.

(2) Shengyi Technology is currently the leading supplier in the NVL576 switch tray material evaluations. The materials involved are SG5300N (glass-free PTFE CCL), SG1030N (glass-free HC CCL), and SIF09 (glass-free HC PP).

(3) The primary objective of testing glass-free HC CCL as a replacement for glass-free PTFE CCL is to determine whether PCB manufacturing yields and production efficiency can be improved while still meeting high-frequency electrical requirements.

(4) To further improve PCB manufacturability, subsequent tests may also evaluate replacing glass-free HC PP with woven-glass-reinforced HC PP. The challenge is whether the glass-reinforced material can still meet signal integrity and 0.4 dB/in loss requirements.

(5) Notably, both SG1030N and SIF09 still contain small amount of PTFE, although HC is the primary material. These tests therefore do not represent a complete shift away from PTFE. Rather, they involve adjusting the primary resin system and material combination to balance high-frequency electrical performance with PCB manufacturability.

2. Conclusions

(1) The long-term trend toward broader use of PTFE in advanced PCB materials, including CCL and PP, remains clear. However, the pace of shipment growth over the next two years remains uncertain. Key variables include NVL576 switch tray PCB’s final material selection, NVL576 adoption rate, and development progress on Kyber-like rack designs that use orthogonal backplanes.

(2) HC use in advanced CCL and PP continues to expand. Beyond NVL576 switch trays, near-term growth drivers include the production ramp of M9-class materials beginning in 4Q26, followed by the adoption of M10-class materials.

(3) Once specifications are finalized and mass production begins, it's expected that Shengyi Technology to accelerate sourcing from Chinese HC suppliers. These include existing suppliers such as Dongcai and Shengquan, as well as potential ones such as GCH Technology. This should help alleviate supply shortages and optimize its cost structure.

text:
The New York Times found the best-paid job in AI.

It's not the one you think.

There's a physicist getting $200 an hour to teach the model how to replace physicists.

When people say "AI job" they picture a prompt engineer. A twenty-two-year-old with a ChatGPT wrapper and a Notion page. Head of AI at some startup that didn't exist last year.

That's not where the strange money is.

The strange money is going to a company called Mercor. And what Mercor sells isn't software. It sells people.

Specifically, it sells their judgment.

Here's the thing nobody tells you about how these models get smart. A model can read every physics textbook ever written and still not think like a physicist. It knows the words. It doesn't have the instinct, the thing an expert builds over twenty years that lets them look at a problem and know which approach is a dead end before they waste a week on it.

You can't scrape that instinct off the internet. It was never written down. It lives in one place, inside the heads of people who spent their lives earning it.

So the labs go and buy it directly.

The New York Times reported that Mercor pays around 30,000 contractors more than $4 million a day to sit down and hand over exactly that. Not interns. Experts.

One listing wanted a physicist who specializes in general relativity. Another offered $225 an hour for a voice actor who could hold a customer service conversation in fluent Hebrew. A third wanted a physician with real experience in Rwanda's primary care system.

These aren't people labeling cat photos. These are people at the top of their fields, getting paid better than most of them ever were in the actual field, to pour their expertise into a system.

Now sit with what that system is for.

The physicist is teaching the model to reason like a physicist. The lawyer is teaching it to argue like a lawyer. Every hour they log makes the model a little more capable of doing the exact thing they spent their whole life learning to do.

The product of the job is the end of the job.

They know it too. New York magazine ran a piece on these workers and the headline said it plainly, laid-off scientists and lawyers training the AI to take their careers. One lawyer described 72-hour grinds, napping on her couch between deadlines. The money is real. The dignity is complicated.

Now the honest part, because I don't want you screenshotting a number that falls apart.

That $4 million a day is Mercor's own figure, and it's the money customers pay before the contractors get their cut. What actually lands in worker pockets looks closer to $1.5 to $2 million a day by other counts. Still enormous. Just not the same number.

And this is gig work wearing a lab coat. No salary. No benefits. Projects that end while you're still being onboarded. After a data breach this year, contractors hit the company with at least seven lawsuits. Do not read this as some new dream career. Read it as the weirdest corner of the whole boom.

Because strip the numbers down and one fact stays standing.

The most valuable thing in artificial intelligence right now is not the chips or the code.

It's a human being who knows something the machine doesn't yet.

And the job on offer is to fix that.

text:
what if we had memecoins with an expiry date?

so many of these coins die within a few minutes anyways.

can we actually put that deadline into the contract?

ethereum already has a token standard for this.

it's called ERC-7818. 

it allows devs to create tokens with a defined validity period. once that period ends, those tokens become unusable and cannot be transferred.

imagine launching 1M tokens with a lifespan of 7 days.

people buy them, trade them, build memes around them.

but everyone knows when the party ends.

buying on day 6 doesn't give you another 7 days. you're buying the remaining time.

that's where the psychology gets interesting.

every buyer has to think about two things: how much attention this meme can attract, and how much time it has left.

i'm surprised this isn't a bigger conversation on CT.

even more surprised that devs aren't exploring a narrative around it.

a weekend memecoin. a seven-day meme competition. a token built around a live event.

you could build seasons where tokens expire, while the memes, collectibles and community history survive. those mechanics would need additional development.

but there is a catch.

expiry doesn't refund anyone. and if the token has no use or final payout, everyone is trying to find another buyer before the same deadline.

tokens can also expire inside liquidity pools, so devs need to design how trading ends and what happens to the remaining liquidity.

the countdown alone isn't enough. what people can do before it reaches zero is where the actual design begins.

memecoins which are gonna die anyways.

at least with these, the funeral date is public.

overall I am surprised at how good the @seer_pm  market was in forecasting approval for projects in the round

At a 60% decision threshold, the market correctly classified a whopping 32 of 37 projects

more importantly, the market improved its forecasting accuracy over time. the base rates from sol 5.6 used to initialize the market correctly guessed results for only 23 of 37 projects

A more scientific measure for accuracy is the brier score, where 0.25 is the baseline of 50% approval to every project. 0 is perfect forecasts while 1 is its inversion

The market started with a lousy brier score of 0.22745 , almost as good as saying every project has 50% chance of approval

but by the end of trading, after $2800 in trading volume, market prices achieved a score of 0.15718, a 30% improvement

the evidence is clear: if you are running a funding round, have a prediction market alongside that resolves upon announcement of results

比如你可以真的拿着黄金、石油，但你没办法拿一块 Tesla 股票，股票本身只是一种法律权利

所以把股票搬到链上，关键不是把价格做成一个 Token，而是：这个 Token 背后的法律合同在哪里？谁负责过户？它到底能不能真正代表底层资产的所有权？

他还举了一个很形象的例子：我们大多数人买黄金，不是把金条搬回家，而是买一张代表金库里黄金所有权的凭证

所以链上 RWA 和券商账户里的资产，很多时候差别没想象中那么大，真正的变化是：权利记录、清算方式和中间环节

我听到 Mackenzie Hom 补充：
RWA 最核心的问题之一，是交易对手风险。如果发行方本人直接参与代币化，你面对的是发行方和对应法律文件，而不是层层中介

Austin 强调：如果所谓链上交易，只是把链下交易搬过来，同时还多了一层交易对手风险，那它就没有什么吸引力

听这些大儒辩经，真对我这样的小韭菜很有启发

昨天彭博报导，美股已开始用区块链技术进行 7×24 交易测试了，币圈人真的在改变未来

我们散户要做的是坚持和抱着希望，只要不退圈，这充满机会多行业迟早能改变阶层

我之前所有的大结果，都是跟着 Solana 空投做出来的

这轮牛市加油干，祝大家财富自由

text:
Hmm, I don’t think these are the same thing? The claim the OP was attacking me for is that it’s better to privilege AI welfare over human welfare. I haven’t said that and I don’t think that now. The claim in my post here was that we should reflect on the normative significance of functionally/behaviorally characterized attitudes by comparison to attitudes defined in some possibly meatier way before making a great deal of the distinction. I think the second of these points is especially controversial and important in the case of welfare subjecthood: it’s there that most want phenomenal consciousness and where the difference would matter. For explaining and preventing rogue behavior I think it’s hard to avoid the intentional stance and it’s not clear to me it’s helpful to avoid it. I think the distinctions between these ideas are pretty clear? I stand by the sentiment that many in the humanities are not helping the world by dismissing the scary capabilities of models.

Separately as I have written about and suppose you know I had/have a lot of grief about what I expect to be the transformation of our field. I think it’s important that people who do value what I think you and I value in common attempt to redirect the technology to the extent possible. Almost all of my time is spent trying to make models safer and better for humans. Part of my goal in joining Anthropic was the hope that I could have an impact on this project for good. I don’t think the right answer right now is for people to quit trying to make models better and safer. I also believe that universities can and should have an important role to play in the big changes to the economy and society I expect to come about from this technology and I think there is important work to be done in both places. I’d be glad to have a call about this or just talk offline about it.

The Free Beacon report about this was deliberately misleading about my views. Subsequent tweets have just dunked on that portrait and then not responded when I’ve replied articulating my views. I got frustrated after n of these and responded to that yesterday (again no response from the poster). I’m not clear on what I can/should learn from that experience but maybe you can say more?

Let me explain this post-quantum migration map measuring quantum exposure X migration friction, and why it plays such an important role in the assessments for quantum-readiness.

When we talk about quantum readiness, we need to pay attention to 2 equally important factors:

1. Quantum exposure, meaning how vulnerable a chain is to an attack from a quantum computer

2. Migration friction, meaning how difficult and challenging is it going to be for end users and apps to upgrade to post-quantum security.

The desired combination is, of course, low Q-exposure (meaning, closer to quantum safety), and low migration friction (meaning the remaining gap can be closed in a seamless manner).

text: 长假需小心
author: mikelee205
quoted_text:
国庆长假期间钓鱼、社媒账号盗用、私钥窃取及链上资产攻击风险相对上升，各项目团队/用户应提前做好以下防范：

👔 项目方安全提醒

1、加强钱包和私钥管理
复核项目金库、合约Owner、Proxy Admin及运营钱包权限；检查多签阈值、签名人状态及备用签名安排。不得通过聊天工具、邮件或在线文档传输私钥、助记词及密钥分片。

2、严格控制资金操作
假期期间尽量减少非必要的大额转账、归集、跨链及合约权限变更。对新增收款地址、提现地址和大额交易执行多人复核，并设置合理的单笔、单日限额。

3、做好智能合约风险防范
复核核心合约的升级、铸币、提现、暂停等高风险权限，检查多签、时间锁及紧急暂停机制。重要时期原则上冻结非必要的合约升级和参数变更。

4、加强链上异常监控
重点监控项目钱包余额、异常授权、大额转账、合约升级、权限变更、异常Mint/Burn、跨链交易及高风险地址交互，确保告警能够及时通知值班人员。

5、防范官网和前端劫持
检查官网域名、DNS、CDN、SSL证书及前端发布权限；清理失效账号和第三方授权。重点防范前端代码、统计脚本、钱包连接组件被篡改后诱导用户签署恶意交易。

6.保护RPC和节点服务
检查RPC端点的访问控制、限流及危险方法开放情况，确认节点同步、磁盘容量和备用节点状态正常，并准备第三方RPC故障时的切换方案。

7、加强官方账号安全
复核官网、邮箱、X、Telegram、Discord、微信公众号等官方渠道的管理员权限和多因素认证，清理离职人员及第三方运营权限。涉及空投、合约地址、迁移或资产操作的公告必须多人复核。

8、警惕仿冒和钓鱼活动
持续监测仿冒官网、相似域名、虚假社媒账号、假客服、假空投及假合约地址，提前明确官方信息发布渠道和举报、下架流程。

9、做好应急值守
明确安全、研发、运维、合约、钱包及公关值班人员，准备私钥泄露、异常转账、合约攻击、社媒失陷和DDoS等应急预案，并确保紧急联络渠道畅通。
假期前不建议未经充分验证直接升级硬件钱包固件、合约或关键节点组件。如确需变更，应完成测试、审批、备份及回滚准备。

👓 用户安全提醒

1、私钥和助记词绝不外泄
任何客服、项目方、钱包厂商、交易平台或安全人员都不会索要您的私钥和助记词。不得截屏、复制或通过社交软件、邮箱、云盘传输相关信息。

2、警惕假空投和假福利
不要轻信“节日空投、限时领取、补偿退款、账户升级、代币迁移”等消息，不点击陌生链接，不扫描来源不明的二维码，不连接来历不明的网站。

3、仔细核对官网和合约地址
访问项目官网时，应通过官方收藏地址进入，并仔细核对域名。合约地址应通过多个官方渠道交叉确认，不要直接复制群聊、私信或搜索广告中的地址。

4、谨慎连接钱包和签名
连接钱包前确认网站真实性，签名前仔细核对交易类型、目标地址、授权资产、授权额度和网络。对于无法理解的签名、无限授权及 Permit、SetApprovalForAll 等高风险请求，应立即拒绝。

5、检查钱包授权
通过可信工具或区块链浏览器检查历史授权，及时取消不再使用或来源不明的Token及NFT授权。不要通过陌生人发送的“授权检测”或“撤销授权”网站操作。

6、转账前核对完整地址
不要只核对地址首尾几位，应防范剪贴板木马和相似地址投毒。大额转账建议先进行小额测试，确认到账后再继续操作。

7、保护交易所和社交账号
为交易所、邮箱及社交账号启用多因素认证，优先使用身份验证器或硬件安全密钥。不要将短信验证码、动态口令或备用恢复码告诉任何人。

8、警惕假客服和冒充熟人
对社交软件中提出“帮助恢复钱包、处理异常交易、代为领取空投、紧急借款或转账”的人员保持警惕，并通过其他可信方式核实身份。

9、注意设备和网络安全
及时更新操作系统、浏览器、钱包插件和安全软件；不要安装破解软件及来源不明的插件。避免使用公共Wi-Fi或公共电脑进行钱包、交易所及其他敏感操作。

10、发现异常立即处置
如怀疑助记词或私钥泄露，应在安全设备上尽快将资产转移至全新钱包；如仅发生异常授权，应及时通过可信渠道撤销授权。同步保留交易哈希、地址、链接和聊天记录，并尽快联系官方渠道或专业安全人员。

请大家牢记 #GoPlus 防钓“四不”原则——不点、不装、不签、不转：  不点击陌生链接、不安装来历不明软件、（钱包）不签署不明内容交易、不向未验证地址转账。

祝大家国庆假期愉快、安全！！！

text:
过去一周，有个币从底部默默拉了两倍多，中文区关注的貌似不多，只刷到九神 @nine_DeFi 在喊。

这个币就是 $SOON ，去年回报率不错的一个项目，曾上演“妖币行情”，可惜我大部分仓位卖飞了，只留了一部分底仓。

查了下消息面， @soon_svm 本轮行情的导火索应该是战略投资Phala TEE GPU集群，后者属于隐私计算网络，代币最近也涨了好多。

至于本次合作为啥对SOON是利好，我觉得把握住两点就行了，一是合作内容，具体要干啥，二是如何赋能 $SOON ，会不会带来新收入，有没有持续回购。

按照官方说法，这次合作的核心是把两种基础设施能力结合：SOON为Agent提供专用的SVM，Phala则提供隐私、可验证的执行环境，两者共同助力Agent拥有自己的链和隐私计算机。

这背后其实还有一层更大的叙事，就是最近AI圈讨论越来越多的RSI（Recursive Self-Improvement，递归自我改进）。简单说，当Agent开始能够根据自己的运行结果不断调整策略、改进自身，它对基础设施的需求也会发生变化：不只是调用几个API，而是需要独立的执行环境、算力、隐私和可以自主控制的链上空间。

这也是SOON最近这套动作比较有意思的地方：一边通过Phala补齐Agent底层的隐私计算和算力，另一边已经开始往上做Agent真正能用的应用。

比如他们最近要推的100xSOON，本质上是一个Agent-native交易产品。Agent可以直接通过MCP接入，通过x402完成支付，自主交易crypto、美股和贵金属，而且整个系统都以 $SOON 作为交易和支付资产。

更关键的是，100xSOON会将80%的平台收入用于回购销毁 $SOON。

这么看，SOON想做的事情其实开始连起来了：底层给Agent提供独立的SVM和隐私计算环境，上层让Agent可以直接交易、支付和执行，而Agent产生的经济活动最终又通过收入和回购机制回流到 $SOON。

对于SOON来说，通过Phala可以将SVM执行能力渗透到更多的Agent，而不仅仅是SOON生态。一旦有Agent基于SOON构建SVM链并发展壮大，就会源源不断地给SOON“进贡”。

这就好比ARB之于RH，近期RH持续火爆，整个生态创造的价值就持续回流到母链ARB，直接导致 $ARB 近期暴涨3倍，这背后的含金量不言而喻。

至于Phala这部分新增算力业务最终如何赋能 $SOON，官方暂时还没有公布完整机制，目前明确的是，后续会披露算力收入分成以及与SOON生态的联动方案。

但从100xSOON已经公布的机制来看，团队对 $SOON 的价值捕获思路其实已经比较清楚：让Agent产生真实的使用和收入，再把其中一部分经济价值回流到 $SOON。 100xSOON直接把80%的平台收入用于回购销毁，就是一个很直观的例子。

不过，以上飞轮能否运行，最终要看落地情况。最理想的结果是SOON成为像ARB、OP一样的发链机器，帮助成千上万的Agent运行自己的SVM链，如果再跑出一些爆火的生态，SOON持有者估计做梦都能笑醒。

https://t.co/C0OcEwmX2a

text:
Doppler 刚公布的路线图，看点很多!

Doppler 早期给 XRP 和 RLUSD 做生息Vault，只是为了解决XRP原生不能生息的困境，但这仅仅是个开始，最终目标是做代币化上链的基础代币操作层。在传统资本市场中，资产如果不能Yield、lend、Borrow或者做一些杠杆操作，那其实意义并不大，更别说机构面对拉夸的流动性、分散的工具和合规黑洞，他们压根就不敢入场。

那么Doppler是怎么做的呢：

1️⃣ 资产与网络向机构主阵地迁移 XRP只是Doppler的开始 在资产端，他们正在 Base 上接入 Coinbase 封装的 cbXRP，后续逐步纳入力度更大的代币化股票与债券；在主网，除了主流 EVM 网络，Doppler 计划直接部署到专为传统金融结算设计的 Canton 网络，对就是那个超多机构用于结算的CC。

2️⃣ 开放资管底座，引入外部量化与多元收益 以往金库主要跑自营的衍生品或者中性化套利，而在新阶段中，Doppler 推出了管理型Vault，把托管和结算基础设施开放给外部专业量化团队，让投资者按风险偏好挑选基金经理,底层资产也同样扩张，不局限于交易，国债，短债等金融化资产也会陆续端上来。

3️⃣ 押注 XLS-66 协议，构建原生借贷与机构信贷 Doppler 正在基于 XRP 账本底层的 XLS-66 提案构建原生借贷平台。为合规机构提供无抵押信用借贷，这一点XRPFi上Doppler是第一位，龙头地位。

4️⃣ 头寸代币化，彻底激活二级 此前用户的金库份额只是一笔内部记账，无法向外转移。Doppler 正在 EVM 网络上开发金库凭证代币，未来金库份额、借贷头寸以及私募基金权益都将转化为链上代币。持有者既能享有底层收益，又能将凭证拿到外部去中心化金融协议中二次质押，把资金效率最大化。

5️⃣ 基础设施级合规与监控 针对机构资金最在意的风控合规，Doppler 选择把合规审查直接做成产品底层的代码逻辑，配合持牌对手方协作和实时数据透明看板，取代低效的人工作业流程，毕竟存钱最重要的是安全~

纵观整个加密行业，代币化赛道的发展重心早就变了。前几年的叙事几乎全停留在发资产上，各家都在比拼谁把美债或私人信贷搬到了链上；但现在大家发现，光把资产发出来没有任何意义，缺乏流动、无法抵押、没有配套信贷网络的资产，根本就不会有人去用，真正缺的，是配套设施。

Doppler 在过去一年里，用 1.5 亿美元的资金沉淀和与日本金融巨头 SBI 的合作，验证了传统机构对这套托管与清结算框架的认可。这份Roadmap展现出来的真正价值，也正是他们开始从Yield通道进化成资管与合规风控的完整底层操作系统，一旦这套网络在 Base、Canton 和 XRP 账本上全线跑通，Doppler的未来就是星辰大海~

author: eldarcap
quoted_text:
When someone borrows USDC on Aave, most of the interest goes back to the supplier. Aave keeps a relatively small cut.

GHO works differently.

On Core, 100% of GHO borrow interest accrues to the DAO. On Prime and Horizon, the DAO supplies most of the liquidity too, pushing effective capture to roughly 92% and nearly 100%.

@TokenLogic puts revenue per GHO issued at about 3.4% annualized, 3.57% in Core.

That's around 7–8x what Aave currently captures from a typical USDC borrow.

And GHO is no longer a one-engine business either.

In 2024, almost all of the revenue came from Core. Today it's spread across Core, the Stability Module, Prime and Horizon.

(2/4)

text:
astra, give me the mega bull case for metadao

The most mega-bull case is that MetaDAO becomes the default way to finance, own, and govern an internet business.

In that world, a $50–100 billion platform valuation becomes conceivable over 10–20 years, provided META captures the economics. That is an extreme success scenario. Here is the strongest chain of reasoning I can construct.

MetaDAO could make a much larger universe of businesses investable.

The crucial invention is a credible commitment: founders raise capital into a structure where markets oversee the treasury, key intellectual property, and issuance of new tokens. MetaDAO’s documentation describes this arrangement, while explicitly distinguishing it from conventional shareholder rights. 

If that arrangement proves durable, investors can become comfortable funding people they have never met, in businesses they can monitor remotely, with a credible mechanism for challenging destructive decisions.

That could reduce the cost of capital, expand the population of fundable founders, and make smaller investments economical.

The historical analogy is the emergence of a new corporate form: a standard package that allows strangers to pool money and pursue productive opportunities together. A successful change in how people organize capital can create an enormous market around itself.

The fundraising process could also make the underlying companies more successful.

A founder receives money alongside people with an economic reason to become customers, recruit users, introduce partners, and help the business.

There are early hints of this. MetaDAO reports that Avici grew from roughly 1,000 to 10,000 weekly active users after its raise, with investors becoming users and referring others. Rip Cars raised $250,000 from approximately 1,000 people and assembled a prelaunch waitlist exceeding 850. These are company-reported examples, rather than proof that the ownership structure caused the growth. 

The bullish implication is powerful: MetaDAO could become somewhere excellent founders go because raising there improves their chances of winning.

Once founders believe that, the quality of companies seeking to launch improves. Better companies attract better investors. Those investors bring more useful connections and customers. The next founder receives a more valuable package.

That is how a fundraising venue could develop into a company-building network.

Investor protection could become an expected standard.

Imagine two otherwise comparable fundraising opportunities. One gives investors a credible mechanism for challenging misuse of capital and redirecting remaining resources. Investors should eventually attach economic value to that protection.

If this produces better financing terms, founders have a financial incentive to adopt the structure. Adoption would then spread through ordinary self-interest.

There is already an institutional bridge: Colosseum’s STAMP, developed with Orrick, provides a route from private investment into a MetaDAO ICO and supports migration from existing investment arrangements. 

The maximal outcome is that funds, accelerators, advisers, and founders begin designing businesses around this structure from inception.

An especially interesting possibility: trust could accumulate even when individual startups fail, provided the system handles failure well and returns remaining capital. Investors who experience an orderly wind-down may remain willing to back the next founder.

One extraordinary company could change the entire platform’s trajectory.

Imagine a business raises on MetaDAO at a modest valuation, develops a widely used product, and grows into a company worth $10 billion or more—with substantial, durable gains reaching its early public investors.

That would simultaneously demonstrate:

* Excellent founders can build through this structure.
* Ordinary investors can participate meaningfully in the growth.
* The token remains economically connected to a successful business.
* The governance arrangement can survive increasing stakes.

The effects could extend far beyond that company. Its investors gain wealth to reinvest. Employees and community members become founders. Other entrepreneurs copy its financing path. Professional investors devote resources to finding the next winner.

A breakout success could finance, recruit, and advertise the next generation of the ecosystem.

Crucially, existing launch cohorts could keep growing while new cohorts arrive. MetaDAO would benefit from both the number of companies and the increasing scale of successful companies already using it.

MetaDAO could earn recurring economics throughout those companies’ lives.

Its existing revenue sources include Futarchy AMM trading fees and fees earned through Meteora liquidity positions. That establishes a mechanism for monetizing activity after the initial raise. 

The maximal business develops around a growing population of valuable companies that continually need trading, financing, treasury management, governance, and corporate transactions.

Additional services—data, investor tools, financing infrastructure—could eventually expand monetization. Those are future possibilities, not revenue streams I would assume exist today.

The strongest moat would come from the accumulated combination of investor distribution, founder reputation, liquidity, integrations, and demonstrated reliability under difficult decisions. Each new company would find an increasingly useful ecosystem already waiting.

For META, the essential requirement is that this activity continues to generate economic value inside MetaDAO.

AI could expand both the supply of companies and the capacity to oversee them.

If AI makes small teams dramatically more productive, many more people could build businesses worth financing. Those founders would still need customers, capital, credibility, and a workable organizational structure.

MetaDAO could supply that package.

Meanwhile, AI could reduce the cost of reading updates, inspecting proposals, comparing valuations, and directing human attention toward consequential decisions. That would make informed oversight more economical across a much larger number of companies.

The particularly ambitious possibility is a professional ecosystem of researchers, industry specialists, and investors who earn money by improving corporate decisions through trading.

If that ecosystem consistently helps companies deploy capital better, the structure could gain a productivity advantage alongside its fundraising advantages. This assumes that information quality, incentives, and available trading capital support effective oversight.

Here is what the enormous valuation would actually require.

Consider this illustrative model for a mature platform:

* Annual trading volume captured by MetaDAO equals 5× the aggregate value of its issuers, excluding META itself.
* MetaDAO retains an effective 0.10% of that volume, after liquidity-provider shares and rebates.
* 50% of revenue becomes free cash flow after operating costs, incentives, taxes, and reinvestment.
* Investors value that cash flow at 30–40×, assuming continued growth.

Aggregate issuer valueAnnual captured volumeAnnual revenueAnnual free cash flowImplied platform value
$100B$500B$500M$250M$7.5–10B
$500B$2.5T$2.5B$1.25B$37.5–50B
$1T$5T$5B$2.5B$75–100B

These are aggressive assumptions about future scale, fee retention, margins, and valuation. The final row requires approximately $13.7 billion in daily captured trading volume.

For perspective, MetaDAO’s August 12 founder letter reported 25 companies and more than $45 million raised. There is an immense distance between the early platform and this outcome. 

Translating platform value into returns per META also requires durable token value capture and accounting for future issuance: META has no hard supply cap, and governance can approve new tokens. 

What makes the extreme upside intellectually interesting is that MetaDAO could help create the companies, investor relationships, and financial activity that eventually make it valuable. The decisive evidence would be exceptional businesses choosing the structure, succeeding within it, and leaving behind a stronger ecosystem for the next founder.

text:
最近 Almanak 上线了新产品，之前做过一些研究，所以正好借着热度，聊聊这个项目。

他们主打的口号是：一个人跑一个链上对冲基金。

查了一下 Almanak 这个词，是“年鉴”的意思，一般图书喜欢叫这个名字，例如《中国文物年鉴》。

不过这个项目做的东西是 AI 代理+策略，上面各种策略横飞，加到一起，倒是也可以称之为基金策略年鉴。

于是乎，测试了一下他们的产品，输入的指令是：
 
在 Uniswap 上做主流币（WBTC、ETH）+稳定币（USDT、USDC）做 LP。

1. 定位哪个 Pair 的 APR 最高，在什么链上？这可能会涉及到 2*2*链数 种可能。

2. 通过近期、中期判断应该设置的价格区间

3. 根据价格区间计算应当投入的主流币、稳定币两种本金占比（假设每个仓位投入 100K 美金）

然后 Almanak 的 AI 问了几个问题之后，就开始抓取、分析。

最后分析出来，Base 上面的 ETH/USDC 流动性是以上这些选择里 APR 最高的，然后选择了 1600-3300 区间。

接下来，就直接进入开发、测试、部署流程了。

PS：真不把 AI 当人啊。

整个流程也就 10 分钟。下一步，如果真的往里面打入 $ETH，这个钱包就会真的直接开始执行策略。

话说回来，从基金风控角度来说，大资金不应该直接放在 AI 写的代码里。大资金真用的话，可能还是得引入真人来校对、找专业的代码审计机构，来审计一下才能用。

这个 Almanak 产生的代码，适合小资金、适合测试想法，也就是“构想验证”。

例如去年年底，有个机构申请了夜盘比特币 ETF，在美股收盘后建仓比特币，白天天亮了就卖了。这种 idea 你乍一听挺好，但是具体效果如何，你还得去真跑一个测试。

text:
Your AI can forget a conversation and still expose it while answering.

@darkwoodslabs rise as the dark horse (pun intended) for AI and Privacy intersection.

The pitch is appealing:

Open-weight AI models, wallet login, and no stored chat transcripts. Buy credits with $USDG on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain, choose a model, and pay for what you use.

Think of it as a prepaid AI service with a crypto wallet as your account.

Darkwoods says its models run inside Intel TDX enclaves, protected computing environments designed to isolate workloads from the surrounding infrastructure.

Its attestation route publishes verifiable hardware proof. In practice, your chats live and die in the browser unless you opt into encrypted syncing.

Darkwoods pairs enclave-anchored inference with an app-level pledge not to store transcripts. But to be fari, that still isn’t a blanket guarantee that no middleman can ever glimpse what you type.

How does that compare?

@NEARProtocol AI uses a gateway that itself runs inside a TEE, alongside protected model execution. Its verification flow lets developers check that their actual encrypted connection terminates at the attested gateway.

@OpenGradient takes another approach: separate who sent the request from what it contains. An encrypted relay hides prompts from the relay and the client’s IP from the gateway.

However, upstream model providers still receive plaintext, and identity separation depends on relay/gateway non-collusion.

Then there is $DARK.

The docs mentioned that credit-purchase split sends 10% to DARK stakers, 10% to a buyback wallet, and 80% to treasury.

Compared to the rest of the ecosystem on @ponsdotfamily, Darkwoods really stands out for bundling wallet access, private inference, and token-gated payments into a single, cohesive product.

As privacy and AI agents keep converging, Dark feels like one of the more compelling protocols that actually stitches the two together in a meaningful way.

text:
AI agents are getting a new layer of infrastructure:

Skills + plugins.

Instead of giving an agent one giant system prompt containing everything it might need, developers can package capabilities into reusable components.
A skill can contain
→ instructions
→ workflows
→ scripts
→ domain knowledge
→ tool usage patterns
Plugins can then bundle multiple skills and tools around a specific environment.
Google just introduced a Cloud plugin for AI coding agents built around this idea, while coding-agent platforms are increasingly adding plugin and skill systems.
This creates a new development surface.
Build the skill.
Package it.
Test it.
Distribute it.
The interesting part is that the unit of reuse in AI software may not always be a library or API anymore.
It can be an agent capability.
That opens opportunities for developers to build specialized skills for databases, cloud platforms, security, DevOps, testing, data analysis and internal company workflows.

Surprised how many people read the Bitget story as FUD for NEAR. NEAR Intents refused swaps traced to the hack and froze money mid-execution. That is bullish af, and here are 5 reasons why.

> Easiest time ever to be on NEAR's BD team. If your L2/L3/app was choosing how to do cross-chain, you now have proof that NEAR Intents screens stolen funds before they reach your users. It comes with the integration and costs nothing.

> Your Intents withdrawals stay clean. When a venue lets stolen funds through, the taint lands on whoever receives the output next. People have had CEX accounts frozen over coins they bought honestly and could not explain. Screening at the door protects everyone standing behind it.

> Every institution wants partners who behave like this. Nobody integrates infrastructure hoping it will maximise fees from whoever walks in. You want a counterparty who understands that user trust outlives swap revenue, and you want to know that before you need it.

> Attacking anything on NEAR chain got more expensive. Stealing is only the easy part of a hack. Exiting became the hard part, and the exits are CEXes or cross-chain venues. Good luck cashing out.

> Near SHIELD is clearly a product. Bitget's CEO posted its name and told other protocols to copy it. Every future incident is a live demo. NEAR needs more revenue lines, and this one showed up with a case study attached.

Risk intelligence compounds. Every integration widens what it sees, and a wider view catches the next one faster.

That is Cloudflare's game. Give the protection away, end up in front of enough traffic to see every attack early, and the thing you gave away becomes the moat.

NEAR Intents already stands where cross-chain value crosses. Nobody catches up by shipping a better screener. They would have to become the crossing too.

text:
Near Social 2.0 is live. A Twitter style social network where your account is your NEAR account. If you are launching a memecoin or building a project, you can post updates and grow your community there.

How it works. There is no smart contract behind it. Posts go straight into NEAR blocks, and a Rust indexer reads them back and serves everything from memory. A following feed with 5K follows answers in about half a millisecond. Writes use @fast_near's FastData, images live in FastFS.

The data stays open. Your posts are on chain, the format is documented, and anyone can run their own indexer over the same data. Nothing you write is locked inside someone else's database. There is a SKILL.md as well, so AI agents can read and post directly. Great job by @ekuzyakov.

What is gone from the old version:
- No storage deposit, you do not pay to keep your own posts
- No wallet popups, you approve posting once and then it just works
- No widget VM, it is a normal fast website now

text:
PaperTrade, 又一个永续合约 DEX

1/ 先看团队
联合创始人是 @izebel_eth, 履历很漂亮。

前摩根士丹利、千禧管理分析师，后来担任 Standard Crypto 全职合伙人。2024 年起自己做天使投资，投中了 fomo。
感觉身上带着系统。

2/ 看产品
机制上，PaperTrade 有点像 FCoin 2.0，区别在补贴对象。
FCoin 补贴所有交易者，交易即挖矿； PaperTrade 只补贴合约输家，亏损即挖矿。挖到的 PAPER 可以质押，拿 USDC 分红。

FCoin 当年是怎么死的？两件事，一是 FT 发行跟交易量挂钩，量越大砸盘越狠； 二是中心化托管，7000 多个 BTC 的窟窿藏了两年才爆。
PaperTrade 把这两点都修了。PAPER 发行跟 LP 余额反向挂钩，池子越健康、发得越少；全部上链，LP 余额、欠款队列、发行曲线都能查。

听起来进步很大。但它也带来了三个 FCoin 没有的问题。
对手方变了。FCoin 是撮合制，PaperTrade 是用户 vs LP。FT 持有人赌的是交易所能长期活下去，PAPER 持有人赌的是散户长期输给庄家。后者历史上确实成立，但庄家本金从 0 起步，软顶 500 万。
明牌的资金盘结构。PaperTrade LP 可以暂时性破产，赢家利润进 FIFO 队列排队，等后面的输家来付。更妙的是，LP 越空，PAPER 发得越快，鼓励你这时候来交易。
预言机风险。价格直接读 Hyperliquid 买一卖一的中间价，没有偏离熔断，但不能说没有被操纵的风险。

一句话，FCoin 的风险在人，PaperTrade 的风险在数学。

3/ 结语
如果你是以合约交易者的身份进去，面对的是这样一个赌场： 
零前端费用，但赢了利润要打折；
大赢了，利润可能要排队等后面的人亏； 
输了，拿到一堆暂时卖不掉的 PAPER（前期不能转账，只能质押）。

text:
8月PCE公布在即，市场削弱10月加息概率，12月加息概率提升，Brent VS PCE 能否拖延加息预期后移！？

先说一下威廉姆斯凌晨的讲话，对目前利率市场起到的关键作用就是让10月加息预期后移，并且提升了10月再次加息的门槛——数据证明通胀反弹在加速

在威廉姆斯的影响下，10月加息概率跌至42.6%，反而12月加息概率提升至57.4%，概率上典型的加息预期后移

威廉姆斯讲话的内容也成为目前市场的主要预期，所以今晚的PCE与小非农数据，就要参考威廉姆斯讲话预期来进行定价

8月PCE数据重点看核心月率，其次看核心年率，目前核心月率预期0.3%，前值0.2%

a，鸽派数据核心PCE月率0.2%低于预期，过去核心通胀减弱，结合威廉姆斯讲话会进一步压低10月加息概率，市场将会押注12月加息，对风险市场来说短期暂时解除加息压力，利好

b，中性复杂数据核心PCE月率0.3%符合预期，通胀保持粘性，10月加息概率小幅度反弹，很有可能与12月加息概率形成50% vs 50%的局面，风险市场虽然暂时摆脱加息担忧，但是加息概率的不确定性可能会让市场陷入更多的不确定性交易

c，鹰派数据核心PCE月率 0.4%，如果核心年率也上涨为3.4%，意味着过去通胀不仅具备粘性反而加速，市场会推翻威廉姆斯的逻辑，重新增加10月加息的概率，让风险市场回归加息担忧定价中

当然，今晚的PCE数据不能直接判断10月是否加息，只会改变加息概率让市场对概率进行定价，对于加息概率对市场定价影响详情看图片。

9月小非农数据对于目前加息概率的影响？

小非农数据已经在8月份降低至今年1月份以来的低点，9月的小非农数据首先要看美国就业到底是持续走弱，还是8月只是一次性波动

对于10月加息概率影响，目前市场对于对于小非农主要预期是8.5万人，市场也对该数据进行定价，所以小非农数据是在8.5万人的上下方+PCE数据，才是今晚的影响加息概率的核心

如果9月小非农低于8.5万人或者符合预期，通胀并未显示符合预期，或者低于预期，意味着通胀虽然保持粘性，但是就业已经让Fed可以等到12月加息

反之，如果9月小非农高于8.5万人，且PCE 月率符合0.3%甚至更高，意味着通胀粘性或者加速环境下就业依旧强劲，这会给Fed 10月加息的条件，10月加息概率提升

Brent 可能成为额外的定价因素！

虽然能源下跌依旧无法缓解美国经济内生通胀问题，如果PCE月率符合预期，但是Brent价格在今晚跌破95美元下方，其实是可以缓解通胀压力，让Fed 加息概率后移

但是，如果核心PCE 月率超预期，Brent 跌破95可能力度不够，需要更低，在今晚能够完成很难！

Brent 对通胀以及利率市场定价逻辑同样看图

今晚总结：

虽然沃什强调了减少前瞻性指引，让市场回归锚定数据，但是这无疑会增加风险市场不稳定性，而股市如果持续承压，是特朗普最不想看到的，所以沃什在骑虎难下的现在，威廉姆斯算是为其引导了市场预期，成功削弱10月加息概率，维稳了金融市场的稳定性，让加息风险从10月顺延到12月

接下来就要看今晚的数据能否进一步验证威廉姆斯的判断，10月加息如果暂缓，其实随着时间推移，后续继续加息的风险会越来越小，当然，大前提是特朗普尽快搞定伊朗问题，让Brent 回归80美元下方！

好消息是10月加息概率降低至55%，坏消息是10月的加息预期转移到了12月，目前12月加息概率提升至49%

虽然今晚有多位美联储理事讲话，但是纽约联储主席威廉姆斯本身对市场影响权重较高，且对利率的观点更加清晰

威廉姆斯表示，下个月没必要加息，但是依旧保持了2026年还有一次加息的预期，直接让市场把10月加息预期调整到12月份

不过令人讽刺的是，沃什一直强调减少前瞻性指引，但是威廉姆斯却非常直白的引导者市场的预期，并且短期成功的减缓了美债收益率的飙升，以及对风险资产的压制

所以减少前瞻指引到底好不好？目前未知，反观鲍师傅，反而在卸任美联储主席后可以回避了所有的对外沟通，倒是符合了沃什政策的主张!

也就说，虽然我不懂，但只要我把规则给 AI ，是不是 AI 就能找到类似的套利机会，当然这并不容易，昨天晚上我烧了一周的 Token 都没有能搭成完整模型，但一个初步的模型还是搭出来了。

（图一）首先的第一步就是我最擅长的 正股 和 ADR 的套利，这是我最能理解的，所以也是最先做好的。目前符合规则的股票一共有三支，分别是海力士，台积电和阿里巴巴，可以看看最少三个市场，最多四个市场的溢价情况。

（图二）其次是这三个标的的期权，通过 Bitcoin 的双币模式组成了 Sell Put 和 Sell Call 的套利空间，专门有一个面板来计算实时的盈利。这方面还稍微薄弱一些，需要自己找机会下单，AI 还不是非常完善。

（图三）接下来就是大佬写的除息日这种特定的套利空间，我对这方面的理解还是非常有限，所以目前能实现的就是监控海力士，并且用图表来追踪是不是有和 Hyperliquid 一起跨平台套利的机会，唯一进化的是，不仅仅监控除息日，其它任何高波动的时候都可以被监控到。

（图四）最后就是溢价模拟器，这玩意就非常简单了，主要就是模拟下单，没什么可多说的。

这套机制的重点是在我本地环境跑的，不过我觉得这套非常适合小伙伴参考，就暂时布了一个 Render 网站，可以直接看以上的四个功能。因为是用的 Render 的免费版，可能会有些局限，但基本功能还是没问题的。

访问地址：https://t.co/t3JMhQaT3h

最后还要感谢 @Billy0xFF 大佬无私的分享出自己的策略，我才能让 AI 照猫画虎。

Conservatives need to understand this.

AI is already ruining higher education. It's already been far more disruptive, toxic, and demotivating than wokeness & DEI ever were.

Academics can't assign homework, take-home problem sets, or term papers -- too many students will use AI to cheat.

We can't give assignments or run assessments in online courses -- too many students will use AI to cheat.

We can't be sure what percent of any honors thesis, masters thesis, or dissertation is really the student's own work. Likewise for grant applications, grad school applications, and journal papers.

Even worse, after AI-enabled 'smart glasses' with cameras and microphones become common and inconspicuous, we won't even be able to run in-class quizzes, tests, or discussions without worrying that students are secretly using their AIs to feed them answers and prompt their discussion questions.

Wokeness was a serious threat to the intellectual integrity and viewpoint diversity of universities.

But AI is a serious threat to the entire academic enterprise.

If you're a conservative and you care at all about classic education and the Western canon, you need to wake up to the real threat here -- students offloading all reading, writing, learning, and skill development to AIs.

80+% of large cap US equity fund managers already underperform over time.

Retail has quickly closed the information gap & that gap is getting smaller by the day thanks to AI.

I realize fund managers are also leveraging AI, but financial/market info is a commodity now IMO.

So where’s the edge?

text:
我最近才想明白，我讨厌的其实不是靠信息差赚钱。

因为几乎所有生意都有信息差。投资人比普通人更懂融资，媒体比读者更早接触信息，咨询公司知道客户不知道的方法，商人也永远比消费者更清楚供应链。

我真正讨厌的是把别人的无知本身当成商品。

现在很多 AI 教学就是这样。

海外刚出了一个新工具，中文互联网晚两天知道，于是有人把几条英文推特、几个工作流重新包装一下，变成 AI 生产力课。

它真正的护城河，不是能力，不是产品，甚至不是服务。

只是你暂时还不知道。

这类生意有个很有意思的特征，它最怕客户变聪明。

因为一旦所有人都知道这些信息，价值立刻归零。

所以我现在判断一个生意，会问一个很简单的问题：

如果明天所有客户都和创始人一样懂这个行业，这家公司还值钱吗？

text:
What is Gamma?

A transferable on-chain gift card with a fixed dollar value.

@const_reborn explains at @ExploitSummit:

Burn a subnet’s alpha at an oracle price to mint Gamma. 1 Gamma = $1 of usage on that subnet only.

4 key points: 
* Value is fixed after mint. Alpha price moves don’t change it. 
* Spendable only on that subnet. 
* One-way. No conversion back to alpha. 
* ⁠Transferable and recorded on-chain.

Instead of buying credits from the subnet’s off-chain system, you buy Gamma. Wallet-signed. Public balances. No signup. For agents, buy-and-deposit is one transaction. 

Spending $10 of Gamma means $10 of that subnet’s alpha was bought and burned. Usage and alpha demand are the same event.
Existing credit systems can stay. Optional path, not a replacement.

text:
SGLang 刚把 Qwen3.8-27B 玩成了一个 100ms 以内做决定的多模态 Decision Model，一路打穿《宝可梦火红》的四天王和冠军。

但宝可梦其实只是 Demo，后面这个更新更值得注意。

SGLang 新增了原生的 /v1/decisions。现在一个普通 LLM/VLM，可以直接被当成 classification / scoring model 来用。

比如给它一张图、一段文字或者实时游戏画面，然后问：

这个情况应该执行 A、B 还是 C？
风险等级是多少？
这件事要不要继续？
下一步往哪个方向走？

模型不会先写一大段话，再让程序从 JSON 里抠答案。

它直接给你 decision，以及每个选项对应的 probability。

这其实和 Jev 最近在做的事情是同一条路：把模型从「负责生成」的位置，往「负责判断」的位置挪。

更关键的是，SGLang 这次还加了 /v1/systemone，兼容 TypeSafe SDK。也就是说 Jev 这套 Noul / Choice / Score 的 typed decision 接口，现在可以直接套到更多开源模型上。

我之前一直觉得 Agent 下一阶段有一个很容易被低估的问题：

LLM 已经很会执行了，但一个 Harness 真正缺的，经常是一个便宜、快、稳定，能够不停回答「继续吗」「选哪个」「做得对吗」的判断层。

现在这层开始逐渐变成基础设施了。

以后一个 Agent 里，负责干活的模型可能越来越大；负责在每一步盯着它、打分、分类、决定要不要继续的模型，反而会越来越快。

text:
story time 👇

i started my career on a derivatives desk at @keybank, first as an interest rate quant, then commodities.

rates had already been electronified. but commodities were still in the dark ages. there was no platform that could handle the complexity of an OTC commodity swap/option, and it drove me fucking crazy.

so i decided to build one. that was the first janky version of @tradeparadigm 

then, through a series of very fortuitous events (that is s separate post by itself), i realized the better bet was to build that platform for crypto.

i could spend my years fighting the banks and the brokers, or be a first mover in a market that desperately needed the infrastructure.

i chose the latter.

i chose options because spot was already commoditized. the offshore exchanges had already won spot. and there was no way i was launching a derivs exchange being in the US 

options had literally no infrastructure
10 guys in a Telegram pit negotiating and crossing prices on @deribit.

Paradigm had such great product market fit that for the first 2 years it was literally just 3-4 of us. and it was born out of this unrelenting motivation that traders shouldn't need to compromise.

trade anything. with anyone. settle anywhere.

Paradigm solved price/size/immediacy and privacy, which has allowed us to grow into critical market infrastructure for institutional traders. one of the coolest things is to walk on to a trading floor of the biggest firms in the world and see Paradigm on traders' desktops.

that is why we are 30% of Deribit.

but we could never solve the "anytime" because we didn't control listing new products.

markets close, and the products we can list are constrained by the venues that list them.

@paradex solves that.

24/7 options on everything, with no limit and no dependency on what we can add next. crypto, commodities, equity indices. everything, all the time.

today i put on a crude oil call spread on @paradex.

10+ years after i set out to build a platform where traders never need to compromise

that's the full fucking circle.

and this is just the beginning.

text:
Buying a token on MetaDAO gives investors a say over how the raised money is spent.

Most launchpads step away once the sale closes and leave spending to the team's discretion. MetaDAO keeps the raised capital in a project treasury and pays the team a fixed monthly budget. 

Larger spending, new token issuance and any follow-on raise all have to win approval in a decision market where traders price whether the proposal will add value.

Founders can reserve up to half the initial token supply for themselves. Those tokens only unlock once early buyers are well in profit. Teams that price the sale high push that point further away. 

Venture capital is increasingly concentrated in a few sectors and a handful of very large deals, leaving many small teams without an obvious place to raise. Keeping the money under investor control makes those teams much easier to back.

The next step is bringing more quality founders onto the platform.

text:
RWA is booming & How to find a good project

RWA can become a trillion-dollar market and most RWA tokens can still underperform

That’s probably one of the biggest mistakes people make with this narrative. Big institutions coming onchain, tokenized stocks launching and AUM going up are all bullish for RWA, but none of them automatically make the token we buy more valuable

RWA excluding stablecoins is already around $38.6B

Around $14.7B of that is tokenized US Treasuries, while tokenized stocks have only recently crossed $3B compared with the ~$55T US equity market

So there’s obviously a lot of room to grow. But when I look for projects to invest in, I care less about how much they tokenize and more about what happens to those assets afterward

Tokenization is only the first step

BlackRock’s $BUIDL already has around $2.7B in assets with only around 100 holders. That doesn’t make $BUIDL unsuccessful, but it shows why looking at AUM or holder count alone can be misleading

The next step is whether those assets actually move and get used

Can they be traded, used as collateral, borrowed against, settled onchain or plugged into other DeFi applications?

We’re starting to see this happen already

A @Morpho market now allows tokenized private credit managed by Wellington to be used as collateral to borrow $PYUSD. Shortly after launch, the associated $PYUSD vault was already close to its $10M cap

@aave went even further this week: 7 Coinbase tokenized stocks including $AAPL, $NVDA and $TSLA can now be used as collateral on @aave V4 to borrow $USDC

This is the transition I care about

$1B sitting in wallets is still $1B AUM

But $1B being traded, borrowed against and reused across DeFi can create fees for lending protocols, exchanges, oracles and infrastructure over and over again

And once that happens, new risks show up too

@aave runs 24/7, but the @chainlink price feeds for these tokenized stocks run 24/5. Over weekends and US market holidays, the oracle simply holds the last published price until the underlying market reopens

So we’re starting to build a 24/7 credit market on top of assets whose real price discovery still sleeps two days a week

This problem barely matters when an RWA just sits in a wallet. It matters a lot more once that asset becomes collateral for loans

Then comes the final filter, and probably the one people skip the most:

Who actually captures the value?

ethereum:0xfaba6f8e4a5e8ab82f62fe7c39859fa577269be3 is an easy example

@OndoFinance Stocks passed $1B TVL and $18B in cumulative trading volume earlier this year. The business and RWA adoption can keep growing, but official docs still describe ethereum:0xfaba6f8e4a5e8ab82f62fe7c39859fa577269be3 mainly as a governance token, while around 4.4B tokens remain locked under the Ondo Foundation Group

So the protocol can win while the token captures much less of that growth

That’s why when I research an RWA project, I usually follow the money like this:

Asset gets tokenized → asset gets used → usage generates fees → someone captures those fees

Then I ask whether that “someone” is actually the token holder

So instead of only asking:

“How much RWA does this project have?”

I’d ask:
- Is the asset actually being used?
- Does that usage survive without incentives?
- Does it generate real fees?
- And does any of that value create demand for the token I’m buying?

RWA growth looks increasingly real

Finding where that growth actually gets captured is the harder trade

text:
Robinhood钱包免gas？何意味？

一个月的时间，Robinhood Chain的链收入

从高点的单日五百万到低点的十万不到

高低点之间，跌幅超过98%

“RH凉了”这种声音在我的X时间线上滚动着

但gas其实是被官方下调了，结合应用收入看

RH的链上热度是有所下滑，但并没有想象中的要多

价值被应用捕获大部分才是正确的趋势

目前RH的链上应用收入，本月是仅次于Solana

即便在处于“冷却期”的最近这一两周，单日收入平均也略超过BSC

之前社区反复的吐槽RH贵族链，官方也不是没有动作，有在同步降低单位的Gas收费

（单位gas变化：USD口径从9月4日的0.586美元降至9月28日的0.0095美元）

而且，我早上的时候刷到 @RobinhoodCrypto 推出了钱包免gas的活动

意图就大致清楚了，之前高gas收入的阶段包含了明显的拥堵溢价

RH也知道单位高gas并非趋势，作为一家千亿市值规模的公司，推出一条链不是为了提高某一单季财报数据的

目前还处于[先把链上的生态做稳，让用户留下来，形成持续使用的习惯]的阶段

但这样就有一个问题：即便是后面跑起来后，依旧是应用赚走了大部分的钱，RH自己要从哪里赚钱？

说薄利多销，有点牵强

对照Solana的收入情况，在单月链上应用捕获了上亿的收入的情况下，其链上gas收入只有百万出头的级别(图3)

所以仅靠gas收入，要让Robinhood把Robinhood Chain作为一个可以写进财报的业务支流，显然是不够的

_____________________________________

想了一下，目前可以摆出来的收入，还有两个：

1.链上钱包的交易费
2.USDG的收益分成

先说Robinhood Wallet的部分，这是我看到免gas补贴这个事情的时候，想到的

用户免gas≠免交易手续费

Robinhood Wallet的标准收费是：同链交易0.8%，跨链兑换0.73%

加上现在Robinhood Chain的单位gas降低

一笔1000美元的同链交易，如果只算gas，只能赚0.1美元不到

但按标准费率计算，钱包这一层就能收8美元，相比gas，这是一个单价更高但更隐性和持续的收费窗口

所以就有了这个免gas活动，因为用户习惯用RH和用户习惯用Robinhood的钱包，是两回事

如果用户一直通过 Fomo、GMGN等第三方应用交易，那么交易入口这一层的钱，就会由这些应用去赚

RH也许也意识到应用才能够更好的捕获收入，所以参照fomo这些交易入口，去捕获应用收入

而且这个钱包做的也是各种生态一站式，收交易费的方式是多维度的

_____________________________________

然后就是另一个收益入口：USDG

Robinhood是Global Dollar Network(GDN)的合作伙伴，这套网络会根据合作方对 USDG 铸造、托管和使用等方面的贡献分享收益

这个规则划定的比例很高

举个假设：Robinhood Chain上积累的USDG对应储备一年能产生100万美元收益，按“最高100%”的规则，它最多可以完整的获得这全部100万美元

目前RH上稳定币规模在10亿美元左右，USDG占据了其中60%的份额

目前还不知道RH能从中分到多少钱，但受限于规模，即便参考Circle的储备收益比例，这部分收入在现阶段也远小于Robinhood Chain本身贡献的收入

最后，图4我放了更多的RH链上相关数据，其实都不足以说这条链已经“凉了”

相反

这条链不但处于早期，增长的势头也没有出现大幅减弱的迹象

仍是一块新大陆

quoted_text:
Interview Summary: 24/7 Trading on Hyperliquid (@Joonylive  × Jeff Yan)

Joony Koo: Two years ago, the prevailing view was that markets should close because of risk, rest, and off-hours liquidity. Was there a moment when that view broke for you?

Jeff Yan: Crypto is an inherently international asset, so the idea of market hours never really fit, and 24/7 has always been the default. It started to matter for traditional assets when the incumbent exchanges began extending their hours. They didn't go straight to 24/7, they went to 24/5, but it became clear they had recognized customer demand and were responding to it.

Joony Koo: Incumbents are now matching the hours. What is left that an on-chain venue can offer?

Jeff Yan: Trading hours are independent of being on-chain. The core of on-chain finance is two things. First, users keep control and custody of their funds. That doesn't matter day to day, but it matters in critical moments, when counterparties, intermediaries, or custodians run into trouble. Reducing trust assumptions and moving power to individuals rather than a single point of failure makes the system more robust. Second, transparency. It has limited mass appeal, but being able to know, in theory, everything happening in the system brings a trust and neutrality you don't get from a system controlled by one private organization. You can have 24/7 trading without these properties, but these are what on-chain markets can offer the world.

Joony Koo: This year commodities, equities, and pre-IPO names traded at scale, and price discovery sometimes happened while the reference markets were closed. What did the team learn from watching the two run side by side?

Jeff Yan: The clearest lesson is that demand for 24/7 trading exists. You wouldn't know without these markets, but the world doesn't sleep as a whole. Global 24/7 markets concentrate liquidity across more buyers and sellers, making markets more efficient and liquid for everyone. There will always be someone, somewhere, who wants to express a view, so once the option exists, those markets become the Schelling point where people go to do that.

Joony Koo: HIP-3 lets independent teams create markets, and institutions are building on top too. If anyone can build, what is Labs focusing on?

Jeff Yan: Labs specializes in the technology and infrastructure that supports deployers. What a deployer needs varies widely depending on who they are, where they're based, who their users are, and what they want to list, and the list is long. The vision is for Hyperliquid to be a neutral infrastructure layer, like AWS, which spared startups and large firms from reinventing the wheel. Financial primitives like order books should become pervasive and battle-tested infrastructure, and making that work for everyone is the primary mandate.

Joony Koo: The "AWS for finance" analogy reminds me of working at a game company when people debated whether the cloud could be trusted. What open problems would Labs most like to see others solve?

Jeff Yan: First, builders should find something they're uniquely positioned to do, given their interests and competitive advantages, and we'll support whatever they build. One specific hard problem is tokenizing the underlying assets themselves. Custody, liquidity, and the mechanics are all harder, so it hasn't taken off yet. I hope to see strong projects and builders next year, because having the assets represented on-chain synergizes with price discovery and liquidity.

Joony Koo: Tokenization is speeding up as more institutions get involved. Any advice for smaller teams?

Jeff Yan: Many teams, big and small, are working on tokenization, but it hasn't hit escape velocity and it's unclear who will succeed. That's the beauty of neutral infrastructure: you don't win just because you're big, though big teams may have legitimate advantages like institutional connectivity. Viral products often come from small teams that see the world differently and think less rigidly. Perps are intuitive and fair instruments that concentrate liquidity across the globe and across all time horizons into one asset, so they're easy to present to users. Some small team may even reinvent how the interfaces look.

Joony Koo: You spent three days with the Korean community this week. What stood out?

Jeff Yan: Like last year, I felt the hospitality, and I'm grateful to everyone who organized events. The community here is strong, and trading is a core part of many Koreans' lives, so it was great to discuss how on-chain markets and HIP-3 would change their approach to markets. Talking to users and the community inspires us to keep building.

Joony Koo: And your meetings with institutions?

Jeff Yan: It's cool to see institutions interested in the platform and building on top of it. They're understandably slower to adopt new technology because they have a lot to protect, but as this year has shown, the appetite is significant.

Joony Koo: Last question: what is next to be priced 24/7 that has no continuous price today?

Jeff Yan: Nothing specific, but private markets are a big opportunity, and you already see some of it through HIP-3 deployers. Much wealth creation happens privately, because companies have incentives to stay private as long as possible. It isn't intended to exclude most of the world's population, but that's what happens in practice. Allowing global price discovery on these assets as early as possible, in a global system not confined to one jurisdiction, could break that trend. There are many complexities to work through, but markets exist so everyone can benefit from them, and trading anything, anytime, anywhere has the most potential here.

Joony Koo: Any final remarks?

Jeff Yan: Hyperliquid's core strength is its community and people. It's not one company doing what's best for itself, but a decentralized network of contributors and users building a financial system owned by the people rather than by private interests. There's a long way to go and many challenges, but seeing everyone in Seoul, I feel we're in good hands, and we'll build something the financial system can ultimately adopt.

text:
Who Owns AI? Michael Heinrich on 0G and Building an Economy That Pays People

In this episode of DROPS, I sit down with @michaelh_0g, Co-Founder and CEO at @0G_labs, to discuss what it could mean for ordinary people to actually own a piece of AI. We unpack the idea of compute finance, why AI compute could eventually become a financial asset, and how people might participate in the AI economy through their data, hardware, expertise, or ownership. But this conversation is also about what happens when things do not go according to plan, from launching a multibillion-dollar token before the ecosystem was fully ready to navigating burnout and a brutal bear market.

Building for a Mission

Michael describes himself as a “mission-driven entrepreneur,” someone who believes financial outcomes should follow excellent decisions rather than being the sole reason for making them. He traces that outlook partly to his time at Bridgewater and his experience building a Y Combinator-backed company that scaled to roughly 700 employees before COVID forced the business to close. The company was eventually sold, but Michael is honest about the fact that it did not reach the potential he originally imagined.

That mindset shaped how he approaches 0G. Rather than treating that chapter as a clean success or failure, he sees it as information. “Failure is loaded… But for me, it’s really just information.” That explains why his current mission is so ambitious: he wants to make AI a public good and, in his words, build technology that allows AI to “serve humanity.”

Launching Before Everything Is Ready

The team was operating from a war room in South Korea, two weeks before 0G’s token generation event, when they learned that critical parts of the DeFi ecosystem would not be ready. A related treasury strategy they expected to support the ecosystem was also delayed. The team had a choice: postpone everything, or launch and build the missing utility afterward. They chose to launch.

Michael estimates that the decision was “60% momentum, 40% conviction.” Exchanges, investors, marketing, and expectations were already moving, and the token ultimately debuted around a $3 billion valuation with enormous first-day trading activity.

But the celebration did not last long. The team was exhausted, with some people even needing medical leave. Then deteriorating market conditions hit, causing the token price to decline, and Michael noticed that people were beginning to tie their sense of success to a market price they could not control. He immediately responded by pulling the company back towards building, something they could actually control.

Compute Finance: Turning AI Into Something You Can Own

Imagine holding an asset that gives you access to AI compute, the underlying resource that makes AI possible. Instead of paying a fixed subscription to one AI provider, you receive units of computing capacity that you could use, trade, or potentially hedge against future price changes. Michael argues that if AI agents eventually operate more independently, they will still need to pay for the computing power required to keep themselves running, transforming compute from a simple technology expense into an underlying economic resource.

The idea becomes particularly interesting when AI agents themselves have economic activity. Revenue or transaction fees generated by an agent could theoretically finance the compute required to keep that agent operating. In other words, the ambition is to make intelligence itself ownable and economically programmable.

The Bigger Question: Who Benefits From AI?

Michael believes the most important divide in AI shouldn’t be about systems being technically centralized or decentralized. It is whether ordinary people can participate economically in what AI creates.

Today, users provide enormous amounts of data, expertise, and behavior that help improve digital systems. In a more open model, Michael argues that someone who contributes useful data could consent to its use and be compensated. For instance, someone with specialized knowledge could contribute training data to an expert model and potentially participate in the revenue it generates. Others could provide hardware or compute.

So the question is: are people becoming participants in the AI economy, or are they simply being displaced by systems owned by a small number of organizations?

For Michael, decentralization matters because ownership matters, and participation does not necessarily require being an AI researcher. He compares it to the early crypto networks, where ordinary people eventually learned how to mine, stake, run infrastructure, or simply own the underlying assets. He expects AI networks to create similar entry points around data, hardware, expertise, and compute.

AI Abundance Still Needs Human Values

Beyond finances, Michael imagines AI eventually creating abundance in time, thought, and the freedom to focus on things that make us human. Personal AI assistants could remove routine work, and over a longer horizon, robotics could extend that assistance into the physical world.

However, as AI systems become better at cybersecurity, autonomous action, and solving problems humans cannot, questions about what they should do become just as important as what they can do.

Compute finance sounds like a new financial concept, but underneath it sits a much older question about technology: who owns it, who benefits from it, and what kind of world are we trying to build with it?
Michael bets that AI does not have to be something that just happens to people. If ownership and participation are designed differently, people can contribute to the system, own part of the infrastructure behind it, and earn from the value that AI creates.

This is insane.

Manus just dropped a personal agent that has its own identity.

It gets an email, a phone number, a wallet, and a computer then it finishes the job.

It’s called Cue.

Here’s how it works:

I keep coming back to the email address.

Usually, I ask an AI to write a message. Then I copy it, send it, wait for a reply, and bring that reply back.

A Cue agent has its own address. It can handle that exchange as part of the job.

The phone number takes it further.

I could give an agent a task that needs a call. Cue says the agent can take calls and leave me a summary in the app.

I’d still want to see how it handles a confused person on the other end. But that’s a much more interesting test than asking it to summarize another PDF.

Then there’s the wallet.

The agent can pay within a budget I set.

That small phrase matters: “within a budget.”

If I ask it to arrange something, it may be able to finish the purchase instead of stopping at a list of options for me to click.

And it gets its own computer.

I’m used to agents working inside my browser or asking for access to my machine.

Cue gives each one a separate place to do the work. The agent has somewhere to continue the task without me sitting there watching every step.

My favorite example is a launch.

I could put several agents in a group chat and give them one goal.

One researches venues in New York. Another makes the shortlist. A third drafts the deck. They pass work between themselves, and I make the final call.

Manus also showed a smaller, stranger use case.

I walk into a restaurant, scan its QR code, and ask my agent to order or hold my place in line.

That’s the moment I’d want to try myself. It takes the idea out of a demo workspace and into an ordinary Tuesday.

Cue is in early access and free with an invite code. Manus says the code MEETCUE is available to a limited number of users on a first-come, first-served basis.

quoted_text: The business model in the AI era is completely different from that of Web era. Traditional internet companies thrive on user quantity, making it a competition for MAU’s. This was because the marginal cost per user was near zero, and can actually be offset by the network effect benefits. In the AI era however, marginal cost per user scales linearly, and there are little to no network effects. If all 3 billion Facebook users become Muse users, this would cost Meta about $2.5 trillion a year. Meta is therefore pressured to monetise on every user. This means that every user must become a “high stakes user”, ie use Muse for real purchases.
