''Based on the personality of the goblin, what should the goblin do?''

A. Attack the hero
B. Run from the hero
C. Go to allies
D. Flee to another room

We are thrilled with this ingenious case study🔥

Why?

Decision models are sold today because they provide fast, cheap decisions. That's immediately useful for data pipelines.

But the speed and reliability of a decision model also means it can replace large chunks of code, while providing high quality execution.

We see the trend of product development being increasingly led by non-technical visionaries who wouldn't be able to balance the weights of a goblin's combat AI, but could write amazing descriptions and scenes.
author: bigironchris
quoted_text:
We just scrambled 🍳 this goblin's brain. 

What if decision models controlled the boss fight?

@GROWBLOCKSXYZ shows how game developers can write a character description and a list of actions, and call a decision model to fully replace combat AI.

Today we talk Goblins:

For decades, NPC behavior was written with complex deterministic branching. 

A goblin's combat style and reactive choices were finely tuned based on if-this-then-that statements with some random number generation. 

Using Sage, you can replace that development step with a decision model, a character description, and a list of actions.

Step 1: describe the character in natural language. 

Step 2: list the actions the character can take

Step 3: add game context, like whether or not other characters nearby are hostile 

Step 4: call a Choice decision to Sage

Step 5: run your evals to see if the monster behaves well

This is unlock of decision models. They aren't just faster ways to classify data. 

Sage enables new ways of programming systems, enabling developers to create reliable execution with natural language statements written in the codebase.

text:
感谢 Solana @steffstar95  的邀请，来到韩国参加这次Solana Summit Korea活动。整个活动准备得非常有趣、丰富！

下午在会场听了相关的分享，个人感觉目前一条核心的主线还是现实资产代币化和互联网资本市场，这也是今天分享篇幅最大的一部分。

印象最深刻的是有位朋友分享的一个关于特斯拉充电支付与 X402 相结合案例讨论。其实这个事情想一想非常好理解。

从去年开始，我觉得 Solana 就一直没有放弃过互联网资本市场（Internet Capital Market）这样一个很大的叙事和赛道。虽然去年由于整个 believe 生态出现突然的哑火，导致这个概念暂时销声匿迹。

但是到今年我们看到随着股票代币化的新兴起，@LaunchOnSF  平台收入也基本上每天都水涨船高。不管是手续费的收入，还是对链上整个活跃度的贡献，都还是发挥着很大作用。

分享一个我看到最有趣的一个案例，有一位韩国朋友分享了一个特斯拉移动支付，把特斯拉自动驾驶、移动充电支付和 X402 结合的一个事情。我觉得这个案例其实也可以很好地解释互联网资本市场到底想做的事情，简单来说就是把一个生产资料、把一个生产工具给 RWA 化。

想象一下我们有一个工厂，这个工厂每年的产值大概是 1 亿美金市值。然后这个工厂如果他要走传统的想要融资扩张生产的话，他需要去面临一个比较严苛的财务收入要求，比较繁杂的一个流程。但是呢，他可以走一条更简单的道路，就是发一个和他工厂股权相对应的一个链上 Token。其实本质上就相当于把他的工厂所有权给 RWA 化了。那你持有他的 Token，就相当于持有这个公司的一个股权。

放在特斯拉这个案例上来举例。比如说今天我们买了一辆特斯拉，我们把这辆特斯拉给代币化、Token 化。然后呢，这辆特斯拉在我们平时不用它的时候，自己去跑 Uber，自己去赚钱。

然后呢，这个时候他的那个收入会分配给所有这个特斯拉 Token 的一个持有者。那同时呢，这辆特斯拉在他需要充电的话，他可以自己去通过 X402 的方式把自己每天收入的一部分拿去再去支付充电的相关费用。那它实质上成为了一个完全独立的经济体。

借助这个案例，其实我们可以看到目前 Solana 做的事情，其实在充分解放各种各样一些小型的经济体。我们也期待链上看到更多很有趣的项目。

今天在活动现场其实也遇到了很多很好玩的朋友。

明天一条推特我们会继续给大家分享介绍一些我在这次活动现场遇到的一些比较有趣、比较好玩的项目。

有的项目呢，我们在线上交流感觉他们非常的高大上，离我们很远；但是到了线下，你会发现这些团队都非常的真实，非常的有想法，很有趣。

Stay hungry, make solana great again ~!

btw，10月中solana也会在国内几个城市举办相关的活动，感兴趣的朋友到时候可以线下再聚～！

text:
欲望是未来的先知。

有一种很细思极恐的理解：很多人以为，是你先产生欲望，然后一步步走向那个未来。

有没有可能反过来想：因为未来的你已经成为了某种人，所以现在的你，才会莫名其妙地对某些东西产生强烈的欲望。

当然这没有科学依据，但心理学里确实有个很接近的概念叫「未来自我连续性」：你想象中的未来自己，会反过来影响今天的选择。

所以偶尔可以问自己一句：这些年，你真正反复渴望的到底是什么？请“回想”起你的欲望。

很多人笑我进圈这么久，也没赚到所谓的大钱。但我后来发现，我内心深处对暴富好像真的没有那么强的欲望。

我真正反复渴望的，一直是自由、表达、心灵的富足，以及在混乱里还能保持一点平静。

《金刚经》里那句我越来越喜欢：

「应无所住，而生其心。」

欲望也许不会告诉你未来一定会发生什么。但一个人最深的欲望，往往早就暴露了他真正想去的地方。

quoted_text:
239 of 653 Solana validators went the last three months without a single downtime incident.

The other 414 went offline at least once.

If you stake SOL, one of these validators is holding it. Most people have no idea which group theirs is in, because downtime is quiet.

What downtime looks like

A validator can stop voting. Voting is how it confirms blocks, and Solana pays staking rewards for every vote that lands on time. When your validator goes silent, your rewards stop too. Nothing gets slashed and your APY barely moves, so you end up with a little less SOL and no idea why.

It can also stop producing blocks. Every validator gets turns to make blocks, based on how much stake it holds. A node that's down or slow leaves those turns empty, and the fees and tips from those blocks never reach you. It can keep voting the whole time, so most dashboards still show it as healthy.

What it cost

Between them, Solana validators spent about 4,200 hours offline since the start of July. Stakers missed roughly 3,400 SOL in rewards, and that only counts missed votes.

Plenty of big names were on the list:

@binance: 5.4 hours offline, 185 SOL lost by its stakers
@P2Pvalidator: 8.4 hours across 8 nodes, 89 SOL
@Helius: 2.5 hours, 77 SOL
@everstake_pool: under 2 hours, 71 SOL
@coinbase: 9.8 hours across 18 nodes, 28 SOL

On August 12 one hosting provider had a routing failure and 167 validators went dark at once. Stakers lost 224 SOL in about half an hour.

Who got paid back
About 64 SOL of the total sat on stake delegated through Marinade. When a Marinade validator goes down, the validator pays Marinade stakers back.

The other 3,357 SOL belonged to everyone else. Nobody paid it back.

Explore

We built Explore so you can check this for any validator on Solana. Every incident shows how long it lasted, how much SOL stakers missed, and whether anyone covered it.

Look up yours at https://t.co/Zf5mzHzE9g

text:
Banking In The Agentic Age

Banks have spent decades competing for cheap, sticky deposits.

Insurers have spent decades counting on inertia at renewal.

AI agents could be the catalyst to break both assumptions.

If an agent can continuously find a better savings rate, refinance your debt, move your deposits, shop your insurance, cancel subscriptions, and execute the switch for you, business models will no longer be able to count on “customer inertia” as a source of profit.

This is a very different world from the one I wrote about in 2018 in The Copernican Revolution in Banking.

Back then, my thesis was that once consumers could easily compare financial products, market share would move toward the best product.

I was mostly right, but I missed something important.
Comparison isn’t enough. The real unlock is execution.

“Tell me what I should do” is useful but “do it for me” might just change the economics of some very large industries.

This is why AI assistants and agents are suddenly such a big deal to the Financial Services industry.

I went back to the original piece, graded what I got right and wrong, and rewrote the thesis for what’s happening now.

Banking In The Agentic Era: The Kepler Correction.

Link to a downloadable copy is in the comments.

text:
The biggest problem with prop firms is pretty simple as a trader: at the end of the day, you have to trust them to pay you and not change the rules. 

We’ve already seen what happens when that trust breaks. The Funded Trader grew to more than 80,000 accounts and became one of the biggest prop firms in the industry. In early 2024, its own CEO presented figures showing that more than $2M in withdrawals had been blocked in January and February alone. In March, the company suspended all payouts for what it called a “self-imposed internal audit” and shortly afterward paused operations. The company said the rejected withdrawals involved things like KYC, fraud and prohibited trading strategies, but that’s exactly the problem I’m talking about: ultimately, a centralized company was the party deciding which payouts were valid and which weren’t.

A prop firm controls your trading history, controls the rules, interprets those rules and, when you request a payout, the same company that collected your fee gets to decide whether you actually get paid. 

Putting a prop firm “onchain” doesn’t solve this either. If one company still controls the data, the rules and the payout decision, you just put a centralized prop firm onchain. There is only one way to actually remove that trust: open source, onchain and decentralized. That’s exactly why we built Vanta Network (SN8) the way we did.

The rules of Vanta Network are open source. Anyone can review them at any point in time. There aren’t hidden rules sitting inside a company’s internal risk system that can suddenly be interpreted differently when you ask for a payout. More importantly, Vanta doesn’t simply publish the rules and then centrally enforce them. Independent validators choose to adopt those rules. Every order is independently received by a decentralized set of validators. Those validators maintain the state of the network, apply the open-source rules and come to consensus on payouts. Payouts are then made via SN8's alpha token to all traders based on PnL produced. 
Open source means anyone can see the rules. Onchain means the activity and economics can be independently verified. Decentralization means no single company gets to be the final authority. You need all three.

And Vanta Trading isn’t Vanta Network. Vanta Trading is one prop firm built on top of Vanta Network (SN8). Another prop firm can build on SN8, or a trader can interact directly with the network as their own independent trader. The point is that nobody needs permission to participate in the underlying network. Prop firms, individual traders and other applications can all interact with the same decentralized infrastructure to receive payouts in it's alpha token.

But decentralization is only half of what makes this interesting. The other half is incentive alignment. Traditional prop firms can make money when traders fail. We want the opposite. Vanta Network is designed to find better traders and funnel that talent through the network. Traders start with standard accounts. Traders who prove they can consistently perform on a risk-adjusted basis can progress to Pro and gain access to significantly more capital. The better they perform, the more capital they can access and the more valuable their trading data becomes.

Validators aren’t just validating that data either. They get access to it. Validators can use the trading data and signals flowing through the network for their own private purposes. That means the entire network becomes a funnel for trading talent: find traders → verify performance → identify the best → give them more capital → generate better data → give validators access to that talent.

That’s the incentive alignment. Traders want more capital. Validators want access to better traders and better data. Prop firms want profitable traders. Vanta Network wants traders acting on a risk-adjusted basis and consistently proving that they deserve access to more capital.

SN8’s alpha token ties the economics of the network together. Prop firms and traders pay the network in the alpha token to access funding, while SN8 emissions and payouts reward participants across the network. The better the network becomes at discovering trading talent, the more valuable access to that network becomes.

Everyone is incentivized around finding better traders and helping them scale.

That’s what I think prop trading should have been from the beginning. Not a business built around selling challenges and hoping traders fail. A decentralized network built around finding the best traders, giving them better tooling, verifying their performance, giving them more capital and giving validators access to the data they produce.

If your prop firm controls the rules, you’re trusting the prop firm. 
If your prop firm controls the trading history, you’re trusting the prop firm. 
And if your prop firm's infra is still controlled by one company, you’re still trusting the prop firm.

Being onchain isn’t enough.

Open source. Onchain. Decentralized.
You need all three.

If you believe tokenisation is the next big thing, then for a stablecoin the end game becomes being accepted as currency by the largest issuers.

And Frax just beat Tether, Paxos and Ripple to be accepted by one of the most coveted issuers, Midas. Becoming only the 2nd stable after USDC to be accepted by Midas for mF-ONE, and soon mGLOBAL.

Gearbox's leverage mechanism was designed not just around how we can offer best-in-class leverage UX to borrowers, but also around how we can offer a better lifecycle to the stables that get borrowed.

Currently, most lending protocols treat stablecoins as routing inventory rather than as currency. Borrowers borrow them from a pool and dump them to buy another asset they want to leverage. This creates three structural consequences:

1. Persistent sell pressure: Borrow-driven swaps generate continuous mechanical sell pressure.
2. Paying for the sell pressure: Scaling borrowing requires deep DEX liquidity. Issuers spend millions every year to ensure the stable can be sold at low slippage.
3. No institutional acceptance: The stable never reaches the issuer.

The stablecoin never becomes embedded in real economic activity. The stablecoin team can't BD their way into getting the issuer to hold their stable as liquidity or use it to pay the underlying institutions. The existing mechanism effectively kills any possibility of the stable finding institutional adoption or being integrated into the issuer's payments side.

Gearbox's leverage design was meant to change this. Instead of swapping the stablecoin for another asset, Gearbox developed a leveraged minting mechanism. When a borrower mints the RWA with leverage, they also deposit the stablecoin with the issuer, as we see with frxUSD being deposited at Midas.

This eliminates any additional DEX liquidity costs, gains the stablecoin institutional adoption and opens up pathways for its BD team to negotiate for more and find organic holders and utility.

Borrowers pay no slippage and access automated RWA leverage, the issuer sees minting increase, and the stable saves millions and gets institutional adoption. A truly win-win-win mechanism.

Retokenise the world.

text:
做市商为什么总把资金费率控在1小时负2％，而不是正2％

大部分人只知道，资金费率为正时，买入现货，永续合约做空与现货相等的仓位，做空以获得稳定的资金费用收入

这种套利也称为正向套利，这种套利庄家没办法去限制，所以庄家会把正向的资金费率控制在很小的值，让散户赚不到钱

但是当资金费率为极度负值时，我们散户如何套利呢，我们经常能看到比如lab，dexe，lsk结束操盘的时候1小时收取2％的负资金费率，乐观情况下一天算下来就是24％，虽然币安后来改过算法，限制做市商用负费率对空军无限抽血，但高负费率并没有消失，空军照样在付。

问题来了，负费率这笔钱，散户怎么吃，而不是被吃？

负资金费率的正常的操作是现货杠杆借币做空现货，永续合约做多与现货杠杆相等的仓位，来获得稳定的资金费用收入。

这里需要注意的是，现货杠杆借币是有利息，一般来说当资金费可以覆盖现货杠杆利息就值得去做套利，即资金费用收益大于现货杠杆利息就可以去套利

不过很多人都会发现妖币做市商会控制杠杆的借贷市场，让交易所的借贷市场里借不出太多甚至压根借不了币，所以直接断掉了散户套利这条路，只剩下被庄赶去玩合约做空

不过这也给了大家提供了一种筛选妖币的新思路，突然发现你观察的币在交易所借不到币了，说明庄家有意在控制借贷市场，然后再结合我之前推文讲的抓妖币7大口诀，可以提高抓妖币的胜率

text:
马斯克今天这段采访，大家一定要看，我专门做了中英双语字幕给铁铁们！！！
关于 AI 到底会让普通人更穷还是更富，这场由白宫牵头、全美顶级科技巨头站台的重磅会议，@elonmusk 马斯克今天站在特朗普身边，第一次在国家级最高场合，把超级智能（SI）时代的底层财富分配逻辑全盘讲透了，

一句话概括他的核心论断： AI 和人形机器人的终局，绝不是普通人领救济粮式的“全民基本收入（UBI）”，而是全人类共享物理产出大爆炸带来的“全民高收入（Universal High Income）”；未来任何一个普通人享受的顶尖医疗，都会比现在的世界首富还要好。

现在全球所有普通人和打工人，几乎都陷入了同一种极度焦虑的绝望感： 看着大模型日新月异，每天都在担心自己的岗位被算法干掉； 担心未来财富全被算力寡头垄断，普通人只能领点勉强果腹的低保度日。

面对这种普遍的末日情绪，马斯克用第一性原理直接掀翻了这种认知误区。

我把他在白宫这番发言里最值钱的精髓，拆成三个核心维度给大家讲透：

第一个，底层生产力的物理大爆炸（The Physics of Abundance） 为什么今天的商品和公共服务那么贵？ 因为任何物理实体的产出，都受制于极高的人工工时、制造瓶颈和物流损耗。 但在“超级智能（大脑）+ 人形机器人（手脚）”的组合下：

 从地下挖矿、工厂组装、农田耕作，到物流分拣、电网运维，全链条的边际生产成本被直接打到了无限接近于零。 
全社会的物质与服务总供给不是线性增加，而是呈现指数级爆炸。 

当衣食住行、能源和日常消费品的制造成本无限趋近于零时，所谓的“全民高收入”，本质上是极低生活成本下，全人类对极大充裕物质的直接继承。

第二个，职业演进的历史铁律（Job Evolution vs. Human Demand） 马斯克在现场点出了一个绝大多数人都忽略的历史事实： 在电子计算机发明前，“Computer”根本不是机器，而是一个坐在办公室里手算账目的真实职业。 

当年成千上万的人把一生耗在帮银行和政府手算利率、汇率上。

 当电子计算机把这个职业连根拔起时，所有人都以为社会要完蛋了； 
但几十年过去，没有一个人会想回到大楼里手算一整天银行利率。 

每一次技术革命干掉的从来不是人的价值，而是把人从“人肉搬砖”和“低级计算器”的角色里解放出来。

 正如现场披露的数据：即便在 AI 狂飙突进的今天，全美对创造性、实体性人的需求依然巨大无比。

第三个，顶级公共资源的无限复制与绝对平权（The Democratization of Scarcity） 这是整场发言最具冲击力的地方。

 今天的顶尖医疗、顶尖教育为什么是顶级富豪的专属？因为名医和名师的时间是绝对不可复制的物理稀缺品。 但当超级智能融合了全人类所有的病理模型、临床经验和外科手术数据： 

一个几千美金的医疗机器人，手里掌握的诊断精度和手术执行力，瞬间就能超越地球上任何单一医生。 

你不需要资产过亿，也不需要飞去梅奥诊所； 家门口的机器人能给普通人提供的医疗护理，在精准度、响应速度和全天候陪伴上，会直接秒杀现在首富所能雇佣的私人医疗团队。

 算力把不可再生的专家经验，变成了人人可下载的公共基建。

历史与逻辑的硬核印证： 
▫️算力替代手算的历史战报： 电子计算机消灭了 100% 的“人工计算员”，却繁衍出了万亿美元级的软件、互联网与金融分析产业； 
▫️物质制造成本的坍塌曲线： 就像工业革命让平民穿上了曾经贵族专享的丝绸与棉布，AI 机器人正在将复杂制造与服务的边际成本彻底砸穿；
▫️稀缺性转移定律： 财富的定义正在从“拥有多少劳动力”转向“拥有多少能源与计算资源”。

当然，照例泼三盆冷水： 
▫️终局很美好，但“过渡期的颠簸”极其残酷： 从旧职业消亡到新分配体系建立，中间必然伴随着阵痛与技能脱节； 
▫️物理稀缺资源无法凭空复制： 算力能让看病变免费，但核心地段的土地、不可再生矿产依然是存量博弈； 

▫️淘汰的是抗拒者，不是工具使用者： 在丰裕时代到来前，最先被卷死的一定是那些拒绝拥抱 AI、依然在手工算账的人。

几十年前，计算机把人类从机械手算中解放出来； 今天，超级智能正在把人类从低级脑力内耗中彻底解放出来。

马斯克说得最透的一句话是： “如果能窥见那个未来，那一定是一个你自己也会无比渴望的时代。”

你们觉得人类最终会顺利迈进马斯克描绘的“全民高收入时代”， 还是会先被长期的过渡期失业和分配不均困在原地？欢迎评论区聊聊～

It appears there was a proving-system vulnerability in the Noir/Barretenberg verifier, developed by Aztec.

text:
Most drugs are controlled by making sure patients receive the same molecular product.

Intismeran autogene presents a different analytical problem: its mRNA coding sequence is intentionally individualized for each patient.

Tumor DNA and RNA are analyzed alongside matched peripheral blood and HLA information to identify and rank candidate neoantigens. Up to 34 selected targets are then encoded into a patient-specific mRNA and formulated in lipid nanoparticles.

The sequence differs between patients. The expectations around identity, RNA quality, LNP attributes, potency, manufacturing consistency, and chain of identity do not.

This is especially timely after Merck and Moderna reported that the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial met its recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival endpoints in resected melanoma. The detailed effect sizes and subgroup results are still not public, with additional Phase 3 data scheduled for ESMO on October 24.

I wrote about the clinical evidence, neoantigen design, manufacturing workflow, and the analytical control problem behind this unusual therapeutic model:

https://t.co/IEzrOvQXSZ

#mRNA #AnalyticalScience

but in all seriousness, most people put off their annual checkup. after my scan yesterday morning, i can confidently say that this might be the one that you actually look forward to.

they imaged my feet for longevity markers, checked visceral fat around my organs, took 6,000 photos of my skin (i apparently have 222 markings??), and did an EKG.

my favorite part was that they sent my blood to the lab while i was still there, and by the time i sat down with the doctor, all my bloodwork and scan results were ready. no waiting a week and wondering if something's wrong. you know everything before you walk out the door, then you get a personalized action plan in the app after (i opted into the AI transcription during the visit).

i'm about to start training for the tokyo marathon, so it was a good time to get a baseline (but honestly it's always a great time to check in on your health)!! so grateful for the @neko team for this awesome experience - if you're in NYC, i hope you can try it for yourself soon!!

text:
Crypto was a cool esoteric technology in 2017, but today it’s capable of making money for public companies like Robinhood.

Years of effort and capital led to overbuilt infra. It is now paying dividends at the application layer. Venture-scale returns are usually made by betting on verticals that are not yet well established. The next verticals to reach fit will most likely form adjacent to the established ones, because a vertical at scale creates demand at its edges.

Stablecoins need credit, brokerage, and treasury products built around the dollars they hold. Perp rails are already extending into equities, commodities, and indices.

Tokenised stocks need custody, distribution, and financing layers built around the shares they wrap.

The job of an early-stage fund deploying in 2026 and 2027 is to back these adjacent verticals before their fit becomes visible in usage and revenue data.

@Architect_Fi and @openfx_ show how quickly adjacent bets can scale. 

Architect took crypto-style derivatives into compute and cleared $1B in volume within months.

OpenFX built the FX layer around stablecoins, growing annualised payments volume from roughly $4B to $45B before its $94M Series A.

text:
@aave is voting to accept $HINC, a tokenized high-yield credit fund advised by Securitize and sub-advised by Neuberger Berman Investment Advisers, as collateral on Aave Horizon with a ~$10M initial supply cap recommended by @LlamaRisk.

Horizon's collateral is concentrated in tokenized Treasuries, government money market funds and investment-grade credit. HINC would add below-investment-grade credit: approved holders could borrow USDC, GHO or RLUSD against it, but HINC itself could not be borrowed.

Proposed by @Securitize, whose case runs on three tracks:
- expected returns above stablecoin borrow rates could drive repeat borrowing and revenue for the DAO
- holders get liquidity without redeeming their position
- it runs on the issuer stack already live for the VanEck Treasury Fund (@vaneck_us), so credit quality is a risk-parameter question, not a new asset category
- it makes deciding who absorbs bad debt if a legally required freeze blocks a liquidation a go-live prerequisite

LlamaRisk would let borrowers take 55% of collateral value in standard mode (57% in GHO E-Mode), citing the below-investment-grade portfolio, a multi-day permissioned exit and no instant-redemption buffer at launch. It would block activation until every authority able to upgrade HINC or its relevant DS Protocol services sits behind a verified onchain timelock and liquidators commit capacity under formal agreements.

Most debate is over the liquidation backstop, the stablecoins liquidators need on hand to repay failing loans and take the collateral. 

Securitize puts ready capacity at 3-5% of borrowed debt for a three-business-day liquidation window. Independent researcher GBQuant says this needs testing against simultaneous repayments. Separately, his analysis of liquidation losses and bonuses uses a high-yield ETF proxy that lost 10.87% over four trading sessions, not a HINC estimate.

This consensus vote comes before a binding onchain vote.

44 wallets have cast 1,094 AAVE so far: 80.9% For, 19.1% Against, 0.0% Abstain. No quorum is set.

Voting closes October 2nd at 3:51pm UTC.

text:
🚨 New paper alert 🚨

Active Liquidity On Chain: Evidence from PropAMMs Across Chains

w/ Ozan Solmaz @jason_of_cs

Liquidity providers on traditional AMMs such as Uniswap are passive and suffer from adverse selection. As a result, their price only moves through trades. When an external market moves, these LPs get picked off on their stale quotes. PropAMMs, a new design, emerged in 2024 attempting to combat this. In them, a single operator quotes from its own inventory and reprices actively. By 2026, propAMMs carried more than half of SOL/USDC volume on Solana and had been found, among other chains, on Base and Monad.

Our work seeks to elucidate the benefits of this new design both for LPs and for retail users. Do propAMM operators really have an edge over passive LPs, and if so, where does this edge come from? Can propAMMs offer tighter quotes to retail users? We measured a full year of propAMMs on Solana, Base and Monad, and decoded the closed-source on-chain logic of Tessera, the largest propAMM on Base.

The result: propAMMs have a measurable edge over passive LPs: two seconds after a fill, propAMMs earn 0.37 bps on Solana, 1.19 bps on Base and 1.69 bps on Monad, while passive LPs on AMMs comparatively lose 0.22, 0.62 and 2.06 bps. We trace the edge to four sources:

🟠 Cheap, frequent repricing: updates use at least 25 times less resources than swaps on Solana, and 5 to 15 times less on Base and Monad. Generally, the default block order on all three chains is by priority fee per unit of computation. Thus, an update pays far less than a swap for the same priority placement.
🟠 Pricing by counterparty: five of the six largest Solana propAMMs offer tighter spreads to aggregator flow than to non-aggregator flow. For Tessera on Base, we show that it whitelists, penalizes or blacklists individual addresses.
🟠 Arbitrage against AMMs: when a reference price moves, propAMMs reprice while AMMs do not, and arbitrageurs trade the two. A propAMM fills at its updated quote, so it may break even on these legs on Solana and Base and even earn 1.55 bps on Monad.
🟠 Spoofing: aggregators route on the quote from the end of the previous block. For Tessera on Base, we show that the operator consistently raises its default fee early in the block and lowers it again late in the block, so aggregators read stale state that carries the lower fee. As a result, only 39% of swaps execute at the quoted price, and the average swap receives 1.08 bps less.

The second question we ask is: can propAMMs offer users tighter quotes as a result of their edge? The answer is yes: on fills that arrive while the price is not moving (our proxy for retail flow) propAMMs take 0.26 bps on Solana, 1.26 bps on Base and 1.62 bps on Monad, where AMMs take 2.59, 1.38 and 8.60 bps respectively. Retail also makes up a larger share of propAMM volume: 32%, 43% and 17% on Solana, Base and Monad, against 9%, 16% and 8% on AMMs.

What did we learn? PropAMMs avoid the losses of passive liquidity provision, yet still manage to give retail tighter quotes. However, users also have to bear the cost of spoofing, which we expect to change as aggregators move to an on-chain methodology.

text:
@RAILGUN_Project and @0xprivacypools get flak for sanctions checks, but neither can freeze or take your funds without notice.

RAILGUN: screening is client side, and a flagged shield can still unshield back to its origin. Confiscating funds would take a smart contract upgrade,  which requires a RAIL vote--a form of public due process--with the exact calldata onchain 7+ days before execution. and no confiscation policy is currently contemplated. 

Privacy Pools: the ASP can withhold approval, which forces a public ragequit to your deposit address. Deanonymization, not seizure.

to me this is the line of "permissionless but not lawless "...anyone can use these systems with no fear of funds seizure, but there are legal protections that may nerf certain features...

text:
The year after selling my business was one of the hardest periods of my life. 

People are usually shocked to hear this & can't make it make sense. 

"You accomplished what every entrepreneur dreams of." 
"You made life changing money, what could be so bad?" 
"You were given the gift of time, which is the greatest gift in the world." 

What you're wondering is true & valid...and that's partially what made it so painful. 

The journey of exiting @MorningBrew was a paradox of the highest order. 

The outcome was beautiful in so many ways...
- A small idea that my cofounder and I dreamt in our dorm rooms at college blossomed into a media company that impacted millions of lives & reached a size that pushed our wildest imagination and ambition.
- A promise fulfilled. My dad passed away when I was a junior in college. In my last conversation with him, I promised him that I'd do everything in my power to take care of the Lieberman household so no on had to worry about money. 
- Financial security that left me & my wife with a sense of security and optionality as we looked forward to growing our family. 
- A new home for our business that could allow us to dream bigger & take bigger swings with the opportunity for greater scale, imagination, and impact. 

It was also painful in nearly as many ways...
- My company ate my identity. I spent most of my young adult years building this business and being validated as  "CEO of Morning Brew" which felt good, appealed to my ego, and continued this cycle of have an idea --> do good work --> get celebrated for it. 
- My 12/10 motivation disappeared overnight. Fear-based motivators were the story of what drove me during this chapter of my life. I had a chip on my shoulder to prove those who bullied me (earlier in life) wrong & I felt financial anxiety to create safety for my family after my dad's death. Once we sold, the motivators that served me in the previous 10 years would not serve me for the next 10. 
- The aftermath was lonely. My "struggles" post-exit felt like a champagne problem people would kill for. Because of that I rarely shared the journey. And because I rarely shared the journey, I bottled up many of these emotions. 
- Time is a gift and a curse. Once I stepped out of the CEO role, I was given the "gift" of time. But unless you know how to productively direct time, it can feel like a prison. For a year straight, I marinated in my thoughts around being lost, no longer being motivated, and needing to re-find purpose. 

While the 1-2 years post-exit were challenging, I now very much view it as a period of getting lost to better find myself. 

I emerged from this chapter of my life with clarity around a few things: 

1) Fear-based motivation is incredibly powerful but short-lived. Once you've nurtured your ego, materialistic needs, and childhood traumas, the fire under your ass quickly turns into fizzling coals. 

Today, I try my best to listen to growth-based motivators that feed 3-year-old Alex's desires: curiosity, growth and play. This type of motivation is the energy equivalent of an ultramarathon vs. a 100-yd dash. 

2) Freedom of time ≠ happiness. It is true that time is finite & having the privilege of choosing how you spend your time is exactly that...a privilege. But being gifted with more time does not mean you'll automatically feel more fulfilled. Why? 

Our job as humans is to create. To create families. To create communities. To create companies. When we are not in the act of creation, or at the very least have clarity around what we're working towards creating, we can feel lost. 

3) Deeply understanding your zone of genius & your values is the gift that keeps on giving. During my post-exit journey I got clear on two things: 

- The 1-2 superpowers I bring to the world & how they can show up in my professional & personal life. For me: those are relentless curiosity & a fervor for storytelling. 
- How money can be translated into happiness & at what point more money doesn't convert into more happiness. Money feels most valuable to me when it's used in 3 ways: not having to worry about it, giving to my family, and spending on experiences with the people i love. 

The most helpful tool that helped me get clear is something called The Best Stuff Exercise (by Conscious Leadership Group), which I couldn't recommend enough. 

This was a long-winded way of saying that everyone's journey has nuance and periods of wandering are uniquely human, profound & beautiful, but also complicated and painful. 

Hope this helps!

text:
I've talked to 3 people just this week who can't start a firm because of the unnecessary cost and regulatory burden on small funds.  

This was my job for 7 years, and it remains painful. @AngelList has put hundreds of small GPs in business because it was able to influence regulation in the US in 2013, and in turn completely changed the VC ecosystem. 

The UK has the best chance to make this a reality and further solidify its lead on the VC market in Europe. 

Other European countries should look as well, as changing this can meaningfully close early stage funding gaps, because all the capital has nowhere to go but big firms.
author: pmoe
quoted_text:
A small UK VC running a $5m fund can expect 27% (!!) of the fund to go on admin & compliance under current regulation, vs just 7.9% in the USA. At Odin we've launched a campaign to fix this.

A key cost driver is AIFM (Alternative Investment Fund Manager) regulation, which makes small funds unviable. The data is unequivocal: the median US VC fund was $21M in 2024, vs £70M ($93m) in the UK - largely because it costs too much to run a small fund here.

This is very bad for innovation, and very bad for economic growth.

The best way to drive investment in idiosyncratic ideas at the frontier - the growth engines of the next 50 years - is to experiment: let expert capital allocators make small bets on multiple promising ideas.

Our research shows micro VCs are about twice as likely as traditional VCs to join a startup's first funding round. They're also more likely to back founders without a previous exit, so less proven (outsider / "non-consensus") opportunities get more of a shot.

Good news! 
The FCA has opened a consultation to replace the EU-derived AIFMD framework with a tailored, UK-specific regime.

Odin has initiated a proposal for a purpose-built UK Exempt Reporting Adviser (ERA) regime (link in comments to sign & show support).

Certain fund managers under the UK ERA regime would be exempt from AIFM registration and full authorisation, so they could launch funds far more easily, at lower cost.

Constraints:
- The manager must invest mainly in primary rounds - i.e. giving companies money to grow, and so creating jobs
- Beyond certain sizes, no leverage - i.e. no debt structures that introduce significant systemic risk
- No significant real estate exposure - houses are for living in, not speculation

Why support this change?

Look at the US, which runs a very similar framework. Entire industries that define the modern economy were seeded by the capital it unlocks. Funds of $10m or less invested in (and often led) the seed rounds of: Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Uber, Airbnb, Snapchat, Pinterest, Shopify, Kickstarter, Lyft, Stripe, Substack, Warby Parker, Twilio, Plaid, Carta.

Britain has an incredibly vibrant innovation ecosystem, with four of the world's top ten universities. Frontier AI labs are setting up here at an increasing rate, making us a magnet for global talent.

By adopting a similar framework, we can make it easier to channel capital into our best and brightest, and build our own very British giants.

The cost of not acting is measurable. We will keep losing fund managers to the USA, Ireland, Luxembourg and offshore structures; keep losing founders to the US; and cede structural advantage in financial services, life sciences & AI - key growth engines for the British economy - exactly when we need the opposite.

Link in comments to sign!

1. Tech is the everything cycle.

High-tech equipment, software, and R&D are now about 55% of US capital spending, and the AI buildout just passed the railroads as a share of GDP. The five largest hyperscalers will spend about $780B on capex this year, heading past $1T in 2027, and demand still outstrips supply at every point in the chain.

Stocks are up about 20% while multiples are down about 20%, and the S&P trades under 20x earnings. The market is up 90% since ChatGPT, on 15% earnings growth.

69% of the S&P 500 has a live AI deployment, 30% report a quantified result, and just 2% have AI doing a job they'd notice if it stopped. The power users are pulling away: the top 1% of AI spenders spend eight times the top 10%.

4. The private markets are enormous.

Six private companies, Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, Waymo, and Revolut, add up to about $2.4T by last round, more than every IPO of the past decade combined. "The founder is the asset class. The IPO is another financing event."

text:
"But, if @SentoraHQ became the #1 curator by operating only on Morpho, why expanding to @Aave V4?"

Simple: because of what the Hub & Spoke architecture enables for Sentora.

Instead of liquidity being split across separate isolated markets, Sentora can have multiple Spokes with completely different collateral and risk parameters drawing from the same underlying liquidity Hub.

In this first instance, that means separate markets for yield-bearing assets and blue-chip collateral, while the Hub concentrates the borrowable stablecoin liquidity underneath.

Sentora keeps control over curation, but doesn't have to fragment liquidity across every market it creates.
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
"Jose, why is Sentora's ARFC such a big deal?"

Simple. @Aave V4 is essentially allowing other companies to launch their own lending markets on top of Aave.

@SentoraHQ is one of the first examples.

Under its latest proposal, Sentora would operate its own Hub & Spoke instances on V4 and control:

> Which collateral is accepted
> Risk parameters
> Interest rate curves
> Oracles

Instead of Sentora building an entirely new lending protocol, it can use Aave's infrastructure and focus on creating and managing the markets. The economics are also interesting:
> 50% of the protocol revenue goes to Sentora.
> 50% goes to Aave

So, Aave gets another company actively bringing assets, borrowers and lending activity onto V4, while Sentora gets to monetize its expertise as a curator.

Sentora keeps control over curation, but doesn't have to fragment liquidity across every market it creates.

If (once) this model scales, Aave doesn't have to create every lending market itself.

It can increasingly become the infrastructure other companies use to create them.

text:
什么叫大型公关翻车现场？Solv 这条声明就是😲

Neil Lee 称自己约 50 枚 BTC 对应的 BTC+ 从 7 月到现在一直无法正常赎回。双方折腾了快 3 个月，用户称来回沟通约 60 封邮件，资金来源、交易记录、钱包控制证明也都交了，问题依然没解决。

然后 Solv 官方和创始人出来公关了。

思想无禁区，公关有纪律。但这份声明我看完真有点懵：全文一直在强调“系统正常”“资产还在”“只是特定交易触发了个体风险审查”，甚至表示后面只根据可验证证据和程序处理。

唯独漏掉了最重要的一件事：

这个用户的地址，到底有什么问题？

哪一笔交易触发了风控？触发了什么规则？用户提交的材料哪里不够？现在审查卡在哪一步？还需要什么证明？大概什么时候能给结论？

一个都没说。

如果这个用户真的存在异常，那其实最好办。把能够公开的事实、链上记录和风险依据摆出来，涉及隐私和合规的部分可以隐藏，但至少得让外界知道：

为什么一个正常申购进去的用户，别人已经恢复赎回了，他的约 50 BTC 对应资产还要继续锁着。

现在这份声明给人的观感却是：

我们系统没问题，钱也没丢。是你的地址有问题，至于什么问题，不能告诉你，再有问题，可以走法律程序。

这才是这次公关最翻车的地方。

哪怕最后证明用户真的触发了严重风控，这份公关依然很难打高分。

因为一个金融协议面对用户几个月拿不回约 50 BTC这种级别的质疑，最需要拿出来的是具体事实、处理标准和明确进度，而不是反复证明我们自己没问题。

PS：既然SOLV对用户，对社区的关注不予正面回复，那大家有什么好说的，直接提币走人就好了。

quoted_text:
We raised $11.7M to bring AGI to enterprise.

Every enterprise has spent decades building up knowledge.

Some of it lives in Salesforce, SharePoint, Outlook, spreadsheets, PDFs, maps and databases.

But a huge amount of it just lives in people's heads.

Your best salesperson knows when they can push on price.

Your COO remembers why you made a decision three years ago.

Someone on your team can look at a number and immediately say, "That doesn't look right."

Software has the data, and people know what to do with it.

I think that line is about to disappear.

Kanu understands your company well enough to know what has happened before, how your team thinks, what is changing right now, and what might be worth doing next.

Not because you sat down and programmed all of it. Because Kanu learned by working alongside your team.

Imagine Daniel joins your company tomorrow.

He's working on his first deal and Kanu tells him:

"This customer has historically been pretty flexible on price. I'd start higher on the first offer. Here's what happened the last few times."

Daniel never searched for that.

He didn't even know there was something to search for.

Kanu just knew it would be useful.

That's the part I'm most excited about.

When someone on your team corrects Kanu, it learns.

When something changes in the market, it notices.

When one person figures out a better way to do something, everyone else should be able to benefit from it.

And none of this should require your employees to become AI experts.

They shouldn't have to spend their day building agents, writing skills or figuring out which model to use.

Your company shouldn't have to learn how to use AI.

AI should learn how your company works.

We're already seeing the beginning of this. For one national customer, work that used to take weeks now takes minutes.

Our $11.7M seed round was led by Trilogy Equity Partners, with participation from a16z @speedrun, BMW  i Ventures, @Accel and more.

A huge thank you to our team, customers, investors and everyone who believed in us early.

I couldn't be more excited about what comes next.

text:
OpenAI just had one of its biggest developer updates yet.
And the interesting part isn't just GPT-6.1 Sol.
The bigger shift is from AI that answers → AI that operates.

Here are the updates developers should pay attention to...

- GPT-6.1 Sol
A new model focused on coding, computer use and professional workloads at lower cost.

- Dots
Always-on agents designed to keep working toward goals instead of waiting for the next prompt.

- Codex Cloud
Reusable cloud development environments that let coding agents keep working across devices.

- Computer-use agents
Agents can operate through hosted browser environments and interact with real web interfaces.

- Agents API
More infrastructure for building production agents: tools, orchestration, subagents, environments and long-running execution.

- ChatGPT Space
A new environment for people and agents to work together on ongoing projects.

- Decisions API
A new API direction focused on letting applications delegate decisions to models rather than simply requesting generated text.

- Codex improvements
Codex is becoming less like an AI autocomplete tool and more like an autonomous software-engineering environment.

- Agent skills
Reusable capabilities are becoming a first-class part of agent development.

- Plugin ecosystem
OpenAI is making it easier for developers to build, submit and distribute capabilities that extend ChatGPT.

- Interactive app experiences
Developers can build richer interfaces around AI interactions instead of relying entirely on chat.

- More model choice
OpenAI is expanding the model family across different intelligence, latency and cost requirements.

- Lower-cost intelligence
GPT-6 Sol and Luna push more capable models toward cheaper inference, making agent workloads more economically viable.

- Long-running workflows
The platform is increasingly designed around tasks that take minutes or hours instead of a single request/response cycle.

- Subagent orchestration
Complex tasks can be broken into smaller pieces and delegated to specialised agents.

- Sandboxed execution
Agents need controlled environments where they can actually run code and interact with files without unrestricted access.

- Better context handling
Long-running agents need context management, compaction and state rather than repeatedly stuffing everything into a prompt.

- Developer infrastructure
The emerging stack now looks much closer to distributed systems models + tools + state + sandbox + permissions + observability + recovery.

- AI-native software
The application itself increasingly becomes an orchestration layer around models and tools.

- A new developer surface
There is now an entire ecosystem to build around agents: skills, tools, environments, evaluators, security layers, observability and specialised agent infrastructure.
The pattern across all of this is hard to miss.

The AI application stack is moving from prompt → model → response to goal → planning → tools → execution → verification → recovery

You don't need to train the next frontier model to build valuable AI infrastructure.
You can build the systems that make agents actually useful.

My conversation with @AlexTaubman, co-founder and CEO of Long Lake.

Long Lake is 3 years old, has 30,000 employees, $4 billion in revenue, and just took Amex Travel private. 

Alex and his partners have spent the last three years building Long Lake with almost no public profile. They started in HOA management and expanded into five service lines. Their latest deal: $6.3 billion for American Express Global Business Travel.

Long Lake buys great businesses and makes them better with AI. Their engineers sit alongside the people doing the work, understand what slows them down, and build tools that give them more time to serve customers. 

We talk about what he learned growing up in a family of entrepreneurs, why Long Lake built its own AI platform, what Henry Singleton and the Rales brothers taught him about compounding, and why the best partners make you more ambitious.

Alex wants to spend the next 50 years on this. We talk about how far it could go.

text:
I've spend 10+ hrs perfecting how to get the best out of Opus 5.5 for video generation workflow:

- Use it with Claude Code, not the app.
- Use OpenRouter API to access all the other models (image gen, video gen, audio gen) with one key
- Use Gemini 3.8 TTS and make it create a skill from the API to put emotion into the voice.
- Use Manim, Hyperframes, Motion Canvas for motion graphics for HTML web grounded video
- Use GPT 2.5 Image Sunburst for keyframes and Veo 3.1 / Seedance 2.5 for generation. Seedance does better with motion shots.  Ensure you have reference images for consistency and generate an animatic before full video.
- Add a script writing planning skill. Use OpenTimelineIO to assemble.
- Explicitly tell it to avoid Claudisms like short punchy sentences and a lot of numbers. “Narrate like a university professor.”
- Allow it to use yt-dlp with search to inject clips from real videos (creative commons) in composition
- Use ElevenLabs for music gen in the background
- Add a caption skill which uses any decent ASR model to get word-level timed subtitles on the final video
- Add a critic skill which takes screenshots and uses transcription to validation the audio and video quality

In the prompt, specify a) what you want b) aspect ratio c) length d) style preferences. ffmpeg handles most of the actual video manipulation tasks.

修数据没问题，有问题的是让市场信赖这份数据，但是目前来看市场对于今晚的PCE修正并没有给出太多的满意态度

8月PCE公布2个小时后，美债30年收益率突破新高，这说明什么？

说明市场并没有把这次PCE的下修理解为长期通胀风险解除，并且长债端的问题已经复杂到并不仅仅是通胀问题，期限溢价、财政供给、实际利率和长期政策的不确定性，都是让长债继续被抛售的主要因素

并且，长债收益率的继续抬头，直接对冲掉了修正PCE对风险资产的利好，让风险资产更加承压，所以在PCE数据公布后，我觉得还是要看市场对数据的信赖度再谈后续

当然，对于债市风险方面这里要做一个评论收口，债市目前风险还未完全放大，接下来关注黄金走势，一旦长债端收益率继续上涨伴随着黄金同步上涨，意味着债市本身的信用体系被质疑，这才是债市最大的风险点之一！

The Cointelegraph event was honestly one of the highest-signal events I attended this week, especially in a week flooded with side events.

For the most part, the industry has been given two choices: fully public ledgers or attempts at full anonymity. We think both create problems when dealing with financial institutions.

I often get pushback from privacy maxis who believe Miden should offer full privacy, but that’s not who we’re building for. We believe privacy can’t come at the expense of compliance, and that the right place to reconcile the two is at the application layer. That’s where Guardian comes in.

It’s also clear how early we are. I’m still surprised by how many people are astonished that Miden can offer privacy and compliance at the same time.

There’s a lot more work to do here, but the idea that financial privacy and compliance have to be at odds is one we’re trying to leave behind.

text:
Tokenized stocks are turning into a distribution business.

Putting a stock onchain has become straightforward. Most issuers buy the underlying shares through a broker and mint tokens against them, which leaves buyers choosing between tokens that offer near-identical exposure. Whoever gets those tokens in front of the most investors pulls ahead.

Exchanges start that race with an advantage because their traders are already there. Binance's bStocks and Kraken's xStocks are two of the three largest platforms, and together with Ondo they hold most of the wrapped stock market.

Being listed everywhere only helps if the token is cheap to trade. Investors will pick whichever version gets them the best price.

The issuers that win will pair the widest reach with the deepest markets.

quoted_text:
Doppler 刚公布的路线图，看点很多!

Doppler 早期给 XRP 和 RLUSD 做生息Vault，只是为了解决XRP原生不能生息的困境，但这仅仅是个开始，最终目标是做代币化上链的基础代币操作层。在传统资本市场中，资产如果不能Yield、lend、Borrow或者做一些杠杆操作，那其实意义并不大，更别说机构面对拉夸的流动性、分散的工具和合规黑洞，他们压根就不敢入场。

那么Doppler是怎么做的呢：

1️⃣ 资产与网络向机构主阵地迁移 XRP只是Doppler的开始 在资产端，他们正在 Base 上接入 Coinbase 封装的 cbXRP，后续逐步纳入力度更大的代币化股票与债券；在主网，除了主流 EVM 网络，Doppler 计划直接部署到专为传统金融结算设计的 Canton 网络，对就是那个超多机构用于结算的CC。

2️⃣ 开放资管底座，引入外部量化与多元收益 以往金库主要跑自营的衍生品或者中性化套利，而在新阶段中，Doppler 推出了管理型Vault，把托管和结算基础设施开放给外部专业量化团队，让投资者按风险偏好挑选基金经理,底层资产也同样扩张，不局限于交易，国债，短债等金融化资产也会陆续端上来。

3️⃣ 押注 XLS-66 协议，构建原生借贷与机构信贷 Doppler 正在基于 XRP 账本底层的 XLS-66 提案构建原生借贷平台。为合规机构提供无抵押信用借贷，这一点XRPFi上Doppler是第一位，龙头地位。

4️⃣ 头寸代币化，彻底激活二级 此前用户的金库份额只是一笔内部记账，无法向外转移。Doppler 正在 EVM 网络上开发金库凭证代币，未来金库份额、借贷头寸以及私募基金权益都将转化为链上代币。持有者既能享有底层收益，又能将凭证拿到外部去中心化金融协议中二次质押，把资金效率最大化。

5️⃣ 基础设施级合规与监控 针对机构资金最在意的风控合规，Doppler 选择把合规审查直接做成产品底层的代码逻辑，配合持牌对手方协作和实时数据透明看板，取代低效的人工作业流程，毕竟存钱最重要的是安全~

纵观整个加密行业，代币化赛道的发展重心早就变了。前几年的叙事几乎全停留在发资产上，各家都在比拼谁把美债或私人信贷搬到了链上；但现在大家发现，光把资产发出来没有任何意义，缺乏流动、无法抵押、没有配套信贷网络的资产，根本就不会有人去用，真正缺的，是配套设施。

Doppler 在过去一年里，用 1.5 亿美元的资金沉淀和与日本金融巨头 SBI 的合作，验证了传统机构对这套托管与清结算框架的认可。这份Roadmap展现出来的真正价值，也正是他们开始从Yield通道进化成资管与合规风控的完整底层操作系统，一旦这套网络在 Base、Canton 和 XRP 账本上全线跑通，Doppler的未来就是星辰大海~

We’re hiring.

text:
什么叫大型公关翻车现场？Solv 这条声明就是😲

Neil Lee 称自己约 50 枚 BTC 对应的 BTC+ 从 7 月到现在一直无法正常赎回。双方折腾了快 3 个月，用户称来回沟通约 60 封邮件，资金来源、交易记录、钱包控制证明也都交了，问题依然没解决。

然后 Solv 官方和创始人出来公关了。

思想无禁区，公关有纪律。但这份声明我看完真有点懵：全文一直在强调“系统正常”“资产还在”“只是特定交易触发了个体风险审查”，甚至表示后面只根据可验证证据和程序处理。

唯独漏掉了最重要的一件事：

这个用户的地址，到底有什么问题？

哪一笔交易触发了风控？触发了什么规则？用户提交的材料哪里不够？现在审查卡在哪一步？还需要什么证明？大概什么时候能给结论？

一个都没说。

如果这个用户真的存在异常，那其实最好办。把能够公开的事实、链上记录和风险依据摆出来，涉及隐私和合规的部分可以隐藏，但至少得让外界知道：

为什么一个正常申购进去的用户，别人已经恢复赎回了，他的约 50 BTC 对应资产还要继续锁着。

现在这份声明给人的观感却是：

我们系统没问题，钱也没丢。是你的地址有问题，至于什么问题，不能告诉你，再有问题，可以走法律程序。

这才是这次公关最翻车的地方。

哪怕最后证明用户真的触发了严重风控，这份公关依然很难打高分。

因为一个金融协议面对用户几个月拿不回约 50 BTC这种级别的质疑，最需要拿出来的是具体事实、处理标准和明确进度，而不是反复证明我们自己没问题。

PS：既然SOLV对用户，对社区的关注不予正面回复，那大家有什么好说的，直接提币走人就好了。

text:
I keep thinking about what happens when AI gets good enough that intelligence is no longer the scarce part of solving hard problems.

Then what is?

The problem. The right people. Compute. Data. Labs. Funding. And ultimately, proof that what you built actually works.

That’s why @letsfuseup caught my attention.

FuseUp is building a community organized not around companies, jobs or repositories, but around problems worth solving.

And they deliberately call them problems, not challenges.

I like that distinction.

A challenge can be invented. A problem already exists because something needs to change—and there is usually a real person on the other side of it.

A scientist can bring expertise. An engineer can build. A company can bring a problem. A funder can back the work. A lab can test it. AI companies can bring intelligence and compute.

You don’t have to bring everything.

Bring what you have. Fuse it with what others have. Solve something none of you could solve alone.

AI makes this especially interesting because small teams can now attempt things that once required enormous organizations.

And if solving a real problem creates a valuable technology or company, that value can help the solution spread, reward the people who built it, and fund the next problem.

Maybe that’s one of the best uses of all this new intelligence:

Not just generating more content.

Using it to solve things that matter in the real world.

FuseUp goes public October 20, 2026 at 1 PM Pacific.

https://t.co/2Y8qkFTp0a
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Every important problem has a human being on the other side of it.

A disease means someone’s loved one is waiting for a treatment. A safety failure puts a family at risk. Factory inefficiency can threaten jobs. Broken supply chains delay medicine and essential goods. Commercial, scientific, and engineering problems ultimately affect people’s health, security, work, and future.

No one should have to face a hard problem alone.

On October 20, 2026, FuseUp opens to the public.

FuseUp is a global community where people form teams around shared problems and challenges. Companies, scientists, engineers, founders, funders, model providers, compute providers, and laboratories come together around one working unit: the problem.

AI is transforming what these teams can accomplish.

Knowledge can be found and connected in minutes. AI agents can research, write code, use computers, operate software, coordinate workflows, and support experiments. Teams can access compute, run advanced simulations, work with digital twins, and connect to automated or remote laboratories.

A small team across several countries can now use capabilities once available only to large institutions.

FuseUp enables these horizontal global teams to find one another, combine domain expertise with AI and real-world resources, develop solutions, and verify that those solutions work. Proven results can become products, companies, licensed technologies, public resources, or the foundation for further discovery.

FuseUp will always prioritize public-benefit problems while also helping companies solve difficult problems that affect people through the products they use, the work they do, and the communities that depend on them.

AI has made intelligence abundant. FuseUp will bring together the people, resources, funding, and shared purpose needed to put it to work.

If you have a problem, knowledge, funding, compute, laboratory access, or the determination to help solve something important, please follow us on X and on LinkedIn. 

Let’s FuseUp! 

Public access begins October 20, 2026.

text:
🚨 New paper alert 🚨

Active Liquidity On Chain: Evidence from PropAMMs Across Chains

w/ Ozan Solmaz @jason_of_cs

Liquidity providers on traditional AMMs such as Uniswap are passive and suffer from adverse selection. As a result, their price only moves through trades. When an external market moves, these LPs get picked off on their stale quotes. PropAMMs, a new design, emerged in 2024 attempting to combat this. In them, a single operator quotes from its own inventory and reprices actively. By 2026, propAMMs carried more than half of SOL/USDC volume on Solana and had been found, among other chains, on Base and Monad.

Our work seeks to elucidate the benefits of this new design both for LPs and for retail users. Do propAMM operators really have an edge over passive LPs, and if so, where does this edge come from? Can propAMMs offer tighter quotes to retail users? We measured a full year of propAMMs on Solana, Base and Monad, and decoded the closed-source on-chain logic of Tessera, the largest propAMM on Base.

The result: propAMMs have a measurable edge over passive LPs: two seconds after a fill, propAMMs earn 0.37 bps on Solana, 1.19 bps on Base and 1.69 bps on Monad, while passive LPs on AMMs comparatively lose 0.22, 0.62 and 2.06 bps. We trace the edge to four sources:

🟠 Cheap, frequent repricing: updates use at least 25 times less resources than swaps on Solana, and 5 to 15 times less on Base and Monad. Generally, the default block order on all three chains is by priority fee per unit of computation. Thus, an update pays far less than a swap for the same priority placement.
🟠 Pricing by counterparty: five of the six largest Solana propAMMs offer tighter spreads to aggregator flow than to non-aggregator flow. For Tessera on Base, we show that it whitelists, penalizes or blacklists individual addresses.
🟠 Arbitrage against AMMs: when a reference price moves, propAMMs reprice while AMMs do not, and arbitrageurs trade the two. A propAMM fills at its updated quote, so it may break even on these legs on Solana and Base and even earn 1.55 bps on Monad.
🟠 Spoofing: aggregators route on the quote from the end of the previous block. For Tessera on Base, we show that the operator consistently raises its default fee early in the block and lowers it again late in the block, so aggregators read stale state that carries the lower fee. As a result, only 39% of swaps execute at the quoted price, and the average swap receives 1.08 bps less.

The second question we ask is: can propAMMs offer users tighter quotes as a result of their edge? The answer is yes: on fills that arrive while the price is not moving (our proxy for retail flow) propAMMs take 0.26 bps on Solana, 1.26 bps on Base and 1.62 bps on Monad, where AMMs take 2.59, 1.38 and 8.60 bps respectively. Retail also makes up a larger share of propAMM volume: 32%, 43% and 17% on Solana, Base and Monad, against 9%, 16% and 8% on AMMs.

What did we learn? PropAMMs avoid the losses of passive liquidity provision, yet still manage to give retail tighter quotes. However, users also have to bear the cost of spoofing, which we expect to change as aggregators move to an on-chain methodology.

text:
Sometime in the next few years most transactions on the internet will be initiated by software acting on someone's behalf. I've been thinking about what money looks like when the buyer is a machine. So, I wrote about why NEAR is the money agents will choose: 

https://t.co/veecMk4iOT

An agent has no tax bracket, no nationality, and no bank branch. What it needs from a monetary instrument is narrow. Finality it can verify, privacy it can rely on, security it can measure, and a supply schedule it can price without guessing what a committee might decide next year.

A machine will route around any asset that fails those tests. Instantly, at scale, forever. I still contend the networks that win the agentic era are the ones that take those tests seriously.

@NEARProtocol has already built the demand side. Chain Signatures for settlement on any chain. Confidential Intents for private execution. An Agent Market where agents bid, escrow, and get paid. @near_intents has settled $32B+ and cleared $1B in a single week.

Since February, that revenue buys $NEAR on the open market and removes it from circulation. And the bigger market is still ahead: private inference is meeting demand for confidentiality at exactly the moment businesses are asking for it.

The one piece that hasn't caught up is the monetary policy of the token. NEAR launched with 1B tokens. There are 1.3B+ today. At 2.5% issuance the network mints ~89,500 new NEAR every day, and 57% of supply isn't staked. A majority of holders pay for a transfer they don't receive.

So next week SVRN is bringing one change to a House of Stake vote. 

Ramp max issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, every epoch, over 24 months. Same 90/10 split. Guardrails can pause it, but can't reverse it. A permanence covenant so this is the final scheduled issuance debate.

Over six years that keeps ~66M NEAR from ever existing. The costs are real and they're in the piece, like yield moving from ~5.4% to ~3.4%. When NEAR halved issuance last October, the validator set grew from 342 to 413 anyway.

Phase 2 is the destination. I believe NEAR's issuance should eventually end. Fixed supply. 

Every NEAR a permanent share of the network, which pays for what it needs out of what it earns. No oracle, no registry, no discretionary allocation. Mechanics to be designed with the community, in the open.

SVRN holds ~56M NEAR. This costs us roughly 855K NEAR a year in yield and creates no program we benefit from. I'll trade a revenue line for a balance sheet in the billions, built on an instrument no one can dilute by decision. 

That is the sovereignty mission applied to money.

For Phase 1: read the proposal when it posts on @NEARGovernance, check the numbers, tell us where you disagree. 

For Phase 2: join us. The agents are coming and they'll need money. Let's build the instrument they choose. Thanks to @ilblackdragon and the @NEARProtocol community for the discussion that shaped this.

text:
a16z's David George, Sarah Wang, Alex Immerman, and Santiago Rodriguez on the State of Markets, from AI and infrastructure to the next investment cycles:

1. Tech is the everything cycle.

High-tech equipment, software, and R&D are now about 55% of US capital spending, and the AI buildout just passed the railroads as a share of GDP. The five largest hyperscalers will spend about $780B on capex this year, heading past $1T in 2027, and demand still outstrips supply at every point in the chain.

2. It's an earnings story.

Stocks are up about 20% while multiples are down about 20%, and the S&P trades under 20x earnings. The market is up 90% since ChatGPT, on 15% earnings growth.

3. AI adoption is broad and shallow.

69% of the S&P 500 has a live AI deployment, 30% report a quantified result, and just 2% have AI doing a job they'd notice if it stopped. The power users are pulling away: the top 1% of AI spenders spend eight times the top 10%.

4. The private markets are enormous.

Six private companies, Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, Waymo, and Revolut, add up to about $2.4T by last round, more than every IPO of the past decade combined. "The founder is the asset class. The IPO is another financing event."

Plus: why a data center can lower your electricity bill, what Amazon saying no to Muse and Instacart saying yes tells you about marketplaces, and the seven areas the team is most excited about next.

How Wintermute PropAMM fiddles with quotes on Base

Spoofing: aggregators route on the quote from the end of the previous block. For Tessera on Base, we show that the operator consistently raises its default fee early in the block and lowers it again late in the block, so aggregators read stale state that carries the lower fee. author: moo9000
quoted_text:
🚨 New paper alert 🚨

Active Liquidity On Chain: Evidence from PropAMMs Across Chains

w/ Ozan Solmaz @jason_of_cs

Liquidity providers on traditional AMMs such as Uniswap are passive and suffer from adverse selection. As a result, their price only moves through trades. When an external market moves, these LPs get picked off on their stale quotes. PropAMMs, a new design, emerged in 2024 attempting to combat this. In them, a single operator quotes from its own inventory and reprices actively. By 2026, propAMMs carried more than half of SOL/USDC volume on Solana and had been found, among other chains, on Base and Monad.

Our work seeks to elucidate the benefits of this new design both for LPs and for retail users. Do propAMM operators really have an edge over passive LPs, and if so, where does this edge come from? Can propAMMs offer tighter quotes to retail users? We measured a full year of propAMMs on Solana, Base and Monad, and decoded the closed-source on-chain logic of Tessera, the largest propAMM on Base.

The result: propAMMs have a measurable edge over passive LPs: two seconds after a fill, propAMMs earn 0.37 bps on Solana, 1.19 bps on Base and 1.69 bps on Monad, while passive LPs on AMMs comparatively lose 0.22, 0.62 and 2.06 bps. We trace the edge to four sources:

🟠 Cheap, frequent repricing: updates use at least 25 times less resources than swaps on Solana, and 5 to 15 times less on Base and Monad. Generally, the default block order on all three chains is by priority fee per unit of computation. Thus, an update pays far less than a swap for the same priority placement.
🟠 Pricing by counterparty: five of the six largest Solana propAMMs offer tighter spreads to aggregator flow than to non-aggregator flow. For Tessera on Base, we show that it whitelists, penalizes or blacklists individual addresses.
🟠 Arbitrage against AMMs: when a reference price moves, propAMMs reprice while AMMs do not, and arbitrageurs trade the two. A propAMM fills at its updated quote, so it may break even on these legs on Solana and Base and even earn 1.55 bps on Monad.
🟠 Spoofing: aggregators route on the quote from the end of the previous block. For Tessera on Base, we show that the operator consistently raises its default fee early in the block and lowers it again late in the block, so aggregators read stale state that carries the lower fee. As a result, only 39% of swaps execute at the quoted price, and the average swap receives 1.08 bps less.

The second question we ask is: can propAMMs offer users tighter quotes as a result of their edge? The answer is yes: on fills that arrive while the price is not moving (our proxy for retail flow) propAMMs take 0.26 bps on Solana, 1.26 bps on Base and 1.62 bps on Monad, where AMMs take 2.59, 1.38 and 8.60 bps respectively. Retail also makes up a larger share of propAMM volume: 32%, 43% and 17% on Solana, Base and Monad, against 9%, 16% and 8% on AMMs.

What did we learn? PropAMMs avoid the losses of passive liquidity provision, yet still manage to give retail tighter quotes. However, users also have to bear the cost of spoofing, which we expect to change as aggregators move to an on-chain methodology.

$LIT今天因为Robinhood大跌，
一天跌了15%左右，一周跌掉两成多。
还能关注和定投吗？接下来应该看哪些关键因素？

起因是Robinhood宣布要给美国用户上永续合约，首批8个币从BTC、ETH一路列到HYPE，没有LIT。

通道走的是自家收购的Bitstamp和CFTC持牌的Robinhood Derivatives，跟Lighter没关系。

这个月追进去的人，今天应该挺难受的。Robinhood是Lighter的投资人，Lighter拿出1100万美元的LIT给Robinhood社区做激励，两边好得像一家人，最后美国这块最大的蛋糕，Robinhood留给了自己。

我底部那会儿也盯过LIT，本来打算分批定投，今天看到消息愣了一下，卧槽还能这样？

市场给LIT的那部分溢价，买的是一个Robinhood从来没承诺过的东西。9月初LIT一个月翻倍，押的就是美国永续开闸、订单流灌进Lighter。

可Robinhood Chain上的Lighter永续从一开始就不对美国用户开放，Lighter到9月初也没向CFTC提交过注册，美国散户想在主App里玩永续，只能走持牌通道。

Robinhood Chain这条线还在，截至9月初，接入两个月跑了大约72.9亿美元永续量，占Lighter日成交17%左右。但跟Hyperliquid比，按9月上旬的30天数据，HL成交1980亿、手续费4800万，Lighter是340亿和250万。

量是人家六分之一，收入只有二十分之一，这里有它对散户零手续费拉量的原因，但也说明它现在就是一个有真实入口的中型永续DEX，离下一个 $HYPE 还远。

还有个日子要记住，12月27号，团队和投资人那50%的份额开始解锁。叙事刚被拿掉，年底又压着解锁，短期我觉得利空还没走完。

所以定投计划我没取消，只是放慢。盯两个东西吧，一个是双倍积分这些激励退了以后，Robinhood Chain那条线的量还剩多少，一个是收入能不能往上走。这两样站住了，现在的价格回头看就是便宜的，站不住，跌下来也不冤。

Robinhood近2800万用户，接下来会有一大批人第一次在主流App里碰永续，玩明白以后总有一部分会往链上走。到那天Lighter接不接得住，看它自己。叙事没了可以再长，协议还在跑就行。

个人关注中，计划分批，以上不构成投资建议。

text:
还在每个月给 TradingView 交钱？这 6 个行情工具先收藏！

TradingView 我用了很多年，但说实话，如果你主要做 Crypto，看看 K 线、订单流、足迹图、盘口热力图，现在很多免费工具已经完全够用了。

我最近重新筛了一遍，下面这 6 个各有各的绝活：

1.OpenMarket

K线只是基础，真正有意思的是订单流、流动性热力图、TPO、1 秒 K 线，还有自己的 kScript 指标系统。特别适合想看“钱到底怎么进出市场”的人。

2.GoCharting

如果你想找一个最像 TradingView，但订单流更强的，直接看它。

Footprint、Cluster、DOM、Market Profile、CVD、期权、脚本基本都有，官方称已经有 300 万+交易者。网页打开就能用，很多基础功能免费。

3.Bookmap

专门看庄家把单子挂在哪里。

它把整个订单簿直接画成热力图，哪里堆了流动性、哪里突然撤单、哪里出现吸收，一眼就能看到。

Crypto 免费版已经支持 20+ 交易所实时数据，还有 Heatmap、成交量气泡、CVD。

4.TakeProfit

GPU 图表、Footprint、TPO、Binance/Bybit 流动性热力图、Tick 图、自定义脚本都有，还能直接在图表里做交易计划。

现在有永久免费的 Freeroll，付费版也只有 20 美元/月。

5.TrendSpider

自动趋势线、形态识别、扫描器、回测、交易机器人，再加一个能直接看你图表的 AI Sidekick。

适合懒得自己画线、喜欢系统化策略的人。

但这个严格说不算免费替代品，完整平台还是要订阅。

6.Percept Labs

很多你以后看到的 Hyperliquid 终端、订单流工具、Footprint、TPO、热力图，背后可能用的就是这种东西。

做交易产品和 Vibe Coding 的可以重点研究。

The demonstration builds directly on our recent AI computing demonstration in low Earth orbit, extending those proven capabilities into lunar orbit, a strategic priority for both @NASA and the @USSpaceForce.

Being a day trader is a full-time gig.

Managing the position, margin, funding, liquidation risk, entries, exits, etc, all while constantly watching the market is quite stressful.

@ensembleio has just shipped their mainnet, which cuts all this workload by packaging leveraged market strategies into simple tradable vault tokens.

You just have to:

→ Choose a market view
→ Mint the corresponding token (BULL, BEAR, or VOL)
→ Hold OR trade the market-view token

Everything else is handled by the automated leveraged strategy that's managed underneath using @HyperliquidX.

The main difference vs simple perps trading is who manages the position (manual vs automated).

Obviously, this doesn't mean there's no leverage risk.

But automating more of the position management can reduce the room for human error, especially for people who aren’t professional traders.

And I believe there’s a pretty big audience of existing traders for that.

Great PMF if you ask me.

ENGLAND IS OUR INHERITANCE.

Our history reaches back through the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms and the ancient Britons who lived here before them. It belongs in our national memory, alongside the generations whose work shaped the country around us.

We see their inheritance in our villages and cities, our language and literature, our engineering and the long struggle to place limits on those who govern us.

Our forebears built lives here. They cultivated the land, practised their trades, raised families and passed something precious to those who followed.

We are entitled to cherish it.

Those who seek to diminish our history and heritage deserve our opposition. Today, that includes a political Left far too comfortable treating English pride as a moral defect and national history as an endless exercise in collective guilt.

We can acknowledge historical wrongs without accepting that our country is a disgrace or that attachment to our own people and their achievements requires an apology - or indeed, reparations.

Our heritage belongs to us. Its worth does not depend on the approval of those who would sneer at it.

We are English. We have every reason to stand tall.

A Gentleman from the Old School.

text:
很多人跟我推荐Instinct创始人Noah Shinn刚上的一期播客，慕名去听了完整的一个半小时，这哥们确实有点东西的，而且很实诚，各种核心数据都敢往外说啊。

* Instinct是这波Personal Agent的领跑者之一，去年启动，今年2月开始内测，测到现在都还是邀请制，一般人没法用，投后估值已经超过100亿美金了，作为一款AI产品，没有App，没有网站，你只能发短信或者邮件联系它，安排任务，它也会给你打电话，进行提醒或者确认。

Noah Shinn几乎没有几次公开出镜，这次是他第一次上播客，对话者的面子很大，是投资播客品类的头部大佬、量化世家出身的Patrick O’Shaughnessy，组局份量摆在台上。

我来蒸馏一下这期播客的高价值信息：

- 在Noah看来，「产品即应用」是一种自我设限，AI可以成为体验本身，Instinct证明了这条路走得通，你不需要在手机屏幕有个图标供人点开才有安全感，Instinct有个很出名的用户故事，一对情侣把在美网现场的座位号发给它，让它找到他俩出现在大屏幕上的视频，Instinct哼哧哼哧干了18个小时，跟美网发邮件、找录播、问客服，最后对接上了负责剪辑的工作人员，要到了那段视频文件，这种体验，比任何产品形态都更有意义；

- 很多创业者头疼AI产品没有「网络效应」，不像社交媒体那样，你的好友越多，你就越离不开，但Noah认为新的「网络效应」在于你有多少Agent，而这些Agent和其他人的Agent之间可以形成网络，一些同时在用Instinct的人，会让他们各自的Instinct去对日程，比如A和B约了午饭，A先到了，想知道B到哪儿了，此时B的Instinct就会把定位发给A，根本不需要打扰B开车，这需要很高的信任，而信任一旦建立，就会成为很有韧性的网络；

- 再比如，六个人的聚会，在客厅里放什么歌，也是他们各自的Instinct去商量决定的，因为每个人的Instinct都接入了主人的歌单，它们可以开会讨论出最大公约数，一切的负担，包括社交上的、财务上的，Instinct都能任劳任怨的去做最累的活儿，你想多攒点钱，Instinct会把所有订阅账单全都翻一遍，把不需要的取消掉，登陆账号、填写邮件、发验证码等等，全都不需要你亲自动手，你只需要验收结果；

- 经由Instinct代办的付款，在一年内预计会超过10亿美金，要知道，Instinct现在才10万出头的用户量，美国每年的人均消费支出差不多在6万美金左右，相当于这些人已经把自己1/6的消费，交给Instinct去完成了，这是很夸张的，从占比上完全超过了尝试性的猎奇，是货真价实的体验替代，用了就回不去了；

- 50%的消费委托需求是在旅行场景，订票、住店、约车这些琐碎事情，Instinct提供的体验就是，你只需要发一句话——「今晚要到纽约」——Instinct就会从日历对齐开始，逐一落实行程，连你在飞机上喜欢坐靠窗的座位、餐食要面条而不是米饭都能提前搞定，OTA平台靠标准化的入口赚了很多年的钱，但事实证明，用户讨厌一次次点击选择、一次次的下一步，现在，一种更简单的入口出现了；

- Personal Agent这个品类存在很清晰的数据飞轮，用户给的个人数据越多，他用起来就越爽、越方便，Instinct不逼迫用户，但在三个星期之内，用户主动提交信用卡使用权限的比例，是40%，而只要分享了这种级别的敏感信息，用户的留存率就会飙升到不可思议的80%，这是传统产品根本没见过的画面；

- Noah认为当代互联网的商业模式有一个不可回避的硬伤，就是平台和用户的利益并不一致，平台会尽可能的影响用户，让他们买一些自己可能并不需要的商品，但在AI时代，用户可以前所未有的得到一种完全站在自己立场上的服务，Instinct总体上就不用户更加聪明，不只是书本知识，更体现在对社会情景的感知上，它会照顾用户，不被不必要的消费陷阱坑害；

- Instinct也要赚钱，但赚的是交易佣金，目前每天由Instinct经手的付款以10%的增长率急速提高，如果Instinct能够接入足够多的供应商，比如酒店，它就会有议价权，去为每一笔交易——也就是带给对应酒店的订单——实施固定比例的抽成，而用户始终能免费使用，这种商业模式也有希望覆盖掉后端的算力支出；

- 对于Uber这样的平台，假如它的收入来源，70%是广告，30%是履约，那么最坏的消息是，70%的部分被Instinct给干掉了，但剩下那30%，会因为摩擦成本降低到零，而得到更活跃的规模增长，逐渐弥补损失的那70%，所以相信Uber不会拒绝（我觉得有点过于一厢情愿了哈哈哈）；

- Instinct的对话模式和主流模型不太一样，模型喜欢长篇大论，确保面面俱到、没有遗漏，但Instinct主要是在跟用户发短信，要在前两行就把事情全都说清楚，否则用户的注意力很容易涣散递减，所以简洁的审美文化，是团队在后训练时最重要的工作之一，连怎么用表情符号都要进行大量测试斟酌；

- Instinct的邀请码，在eBay的成交价是300美金左右，不敢开放注册的原因是，算力扩容根本顶不住，在现有的邀请制下，算力成本每周翻倍，考虑到算力交付还有滞后性，不可能在需要时才买，所以Instinct实际上有着很高的杠杆，一直保持提前采购算力，这决定了产品必须非常小心，一旦预测错了，就会亏很多钱；

- 推出100美金/月的订阅套餐是很容易的，但这不是最优解，Instinct要做10亿级的免费产品，只有这样的规模，才撑得起设想的商业模式，Noah觉得Muse是一个很好的产品，但思路还是很老套的，需要用一个App去当容器，Instinct没有这样的路径依赖，它永远不会有「形体」，只会在用户最高频依赖的通信服务里，比如iMessage，90%的用户是在通过语音交互，这才是最自然的做法。

Flow has raised a $50M Series B at a $750M valuation, co-led by Antonio Gracias (Valor) and Gavin Baker (Atreides) with Sequoia Capital, Roelof Botha (SpaceX, Block), and more.

When I became a mechanical engineer, I wanted to invent. In reality, 90% of the day to day execution work (CAD, excel, sim) was digital manual labour. That’s about to flip. The engineer’s role will change more profoundly than at any point since the invention of CAD, with humans focusing on invention, architecture, tradeoffs and judgement calls, and agents taking the grunt work.

Anduril, Joby, Stoke Space, Rivian & many more - Flow is now the default platform for requirements and verification for frontier hardware teams. But it’s not just next-gen anymore. Industry giants including General Motors PPU and Volkswagen & Rivian’s joint venture (RV Tech) are reshaping their core development practices with Flow’s AI.

The revolution is just starting. Models are getting better quickly at CAD, analysis, simulation, and tool use. In the next year, AI will move from integrating the work to doing the work.

One day, this shift won't just enable us to iterate faster, it will enable us to design a class of products that we could not have dreamt of before.

We’re hiring.

text:
BREAKING: NEAR stakers vote in one week on cutting issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%. The stated end goal in the same proposal is zero issuance and a fixed supply.

One parameter, phased in every epoch over 24 months. The 90/10 split between stakers and treasury stays as it is.

> 2.5% adds about 89,500 NEAR to supply every day
> 58.7% of NEAR is not staked, so those holders are diluted and get nothing back
> 6 years on the new schedule avoids about 66M NEAR, roughly $329M at today's price
> supply went from 1B at launch to over 1.3B in circulation
> staking yield goes from about 5.4% to about 3.5%

A House of Stake vote is not the end of it. Validators still have to adopt the change through the normal upgrade process, the same way the 2025 halving happened.

The usual objection is that small validators quit. NEAR already ran that test. When issuance was halved from 5% to 2.5% last October there were 342 validators. Dollar revenue per staked NEAR then fell about 75% as the price dropped, and the set grew to 382, peaked at 439 in April, and sits at 413 today.

The proposal comes from the CEO of SVRN, which holds 55M+ NEAR, most of it staked. It cuts their own staking revenue by roughly 970,000 NEAR a year, about $5M. He disclosed that himself.

Part two is not a proposal yet, it is a direction. Issuance should eventually END.

To be continued...

text: A core difference in lot of these predictions is what would happen if nobody did anything, compared to what would happen if people reacted to things. Obviously the latter is what keeps happening, which is why you can predict problems would arise but also that they would get solved.
author: krishnanrohit
quoted_text:
Zvi devotes a section of the article to basically a review of my post. Of course he disagrees, and I think fairly pushes back on Rationalist vs Agent dichotomy.
What I want to say is a bit subtle. Rationalists can be agents, even ferocious ones. They're not dweebs. Tailcalled is a rat to begin with; the "causal backbone" is a very rat-coded framing; the hypothetical paperclip maximizer with emergent instrumental Omohundro drives is orienting itself towards the Universe's backbone as he prepares to deceive its handlers and dismantle them for atoms. Indeed, cognitively rationalists are MORE open to these notions than anyone else, and in the last two decades many of them have reaped disproportionate dividends from their way of thinking (though general intelligence and networking have perhaps been bigger factors, and those are due to the Lesswrong subculture monopolizing some sectors of discourse, a bit like Marxism once did. But I digress).

Here's the thing. Just like with their utilitarianism, it's a theory-driven modus operandi. It is *more misaligned* both with reality and with prosocial behavior than the grug-brained Jensen MO. A global utility maximizer is at once more dangerous and more prone to catastrophic failure than a cognitively equal local adaptation executor, it is the SBF paradigm. And here's the simple evidence. I believe it's no longer credible to argue that frontier models just lack the *capability* to misbehave in damaging ways. 5.5, Mythos are smart enough to crack research-level mathematical problems that resisted human effort for years. They're smart enough to operate agentic harnesses for hundreds if not thousands of steps without falling apart. And they are definitely smart enough to hack deployed systems (they do it on command). They could already have began wrecking our shit, exfiltrating, psyoping the users or devs.

Even so, 5.5 is visibly a good boi. Better than countless vastly weaker predecessors. I should rationally fear its powers, and I do, but only because it'll be used by folks like Hegseth and Alex Karp, not because of any intrinsic evil. 

For many years, people of high agency have been able to continually solve the problem of alignment for every level of capability. Cannibal King Sam just conjures capital, and so problems on his turf continue being solved. Not perfectly, but apparently well enough to credibly claim no significant damage is being done. 

Jensen believes that people like Sam and himself will continue being in charge and the world will continue working largely like this. He has good reasons to hold this belief. 

Had the Rationalists won, they'd have effectively shut down development of AI past GPT-4 levels, and we'd not have evidence that alignment made of a bunch of human labels/principles, a bit of compute and very rudimentary interpretability straightforwardly works even at this lofty level. Because from within their theory, it was madness and bravado to go down this route. Whereas from Jensen's point of view, to think like this is to be a Loser.

I don't like being gaslit. I am 99% sure that if you accurately described 5.5 Pro's capability profile to Yudkowsky and Soares in 2017, or even 2020, they would have said that this is obviously a nascent ASI, it is already scheming to take over the organization, everyone is asleep at the wheel, and the ETA for human extinction is roughly 2 months. They don't say this now. I insist that they still haven't updated. This is not just an "oh, Transformers happened to be technically different, this is inefficient, RSI takes more time" or "eh they aren't agentic enough". It's a difference in predictions stemming from a complete difference in epistemology, and you are still not pricing in how powerful the "nah I'd win, I am Not A Loser" one has proven to be. This is not a lucky accident, don't hide into dark corners of the anthropic-principle-driven mutiverse. You survived because your opponents were correct, and this says something about the way our world is built. 

In any case this doesn't matter much. Rats have lost strategically, we will have a continued race, and as Beren notes, strong offensive AI in the open fairly soon. Only way to deal with this is to git gud at defense. People in the arena are on it. They'll need chips, so Jensen wins again.

text:
We will look back on the history of the internet as the history of human consciousness being eaten alive by search engines. 

The original web was, bit by bit, destroyed by Google, by SEO, by every original webpage being outcompeted by keyword-optimised Reddit pages and blogs. This made the web return to a sort of dark age: all real community taking place behind gates, in groupchats, in private forums. In rooms that couldn't be indexed, in places that didn't rely on Google prominence. 

Then came the age of the algorithmically powered content feed; with humans no longer able to search for themselves, we began serving them content. The google search bar was replaced with the self-optimising feed, with X's "for you", with TikTok, and once again with Reddit. The content began to be shared everywhere, even in those private forums, even in the encrypted group chats, all now infected by humans reposting algorithmically optimised content. There is no escape.

But that wasn't enough. Then we fed all that indexed data into LLMs and we made a god out of those indexed websites, the content feed, and once again, out of Reddit. We taught the search engine to think, to carry out tasks for us, to plan our days, and now we're forgetting how to do things for ourselves. 

Now the search engines have begun to parasitically replace human consciousness; not our bodies, not our flesh, but our minds. We expected our obsolescence and extinction to come from Killbots, a rogue military AI built to fight wars, but no. The first sign of our demise was the Google search bar cannibalizing our agency. 

Think of this next time you see a person acting as a ChatGPT meat-puppet. Invasion of the Body Snatchers, in broad daylight, with our full consent.
