text:
Gemini 4 Argon 发布！首批体验只通过 Fairwind 计划（可信的网络防御者）开放，还要等美国政府的最终审批，大家还得等等才能用上。Google 改了命名规则，所以不知道这是什么等级的模型，但从这个评分来看，已经稳稳进入了第一梯队！

Argon 主打复杂的长周期任务，重点场景是软件工程、企业知识工作和网络安全防御。单次输出上限提到了 100 万 token，OpenAI和 Anthropic 家的最新模型输出上限 12.8 万，Gemini 上一代只有 64K，这次提升了 16 倍！

模型能在一次任务里完成更长的推理链和更大规模的产出，比如大型代码库迁移、法律研究、金融分析、自主发现并修补漏洞，以及长视频和长文档分析。Google 说 Argon Agent 正在将 Google 各部门的 C/C++ 代码库迁移到 Rust；还自主识别并执行了 Google 数据中心的内存优化，预计可释放超过 300 TB 的内存。

Argon 推广期每百万输入 2 美元、输出 10 美元，缓存输入也都是每百万 0.1 美元左右，和 GPT-6 Sol 一样。推广期结束后，恢复到输入 4 美元、输出 20 美元，正好是 Sol 的两倍，缓存输入也会跟着涨到每百万 0.2 美元左右，但也只有 Astra 的四成左右👀

有两点值得留意。第一，前沿模型的竞争焦点正在从「答得好」转向「能连续干很久的活」，100 万 token 的输出上限就是为长时间运行的 Agent 准备的，这和昨天 OpenAI 发布的 dots 是同一个方向。第二，「先给防御方、再经政府审批」的发布方式，可能会成为最强一档模型的新常态，这会直接影响各家模型商业化的节奏。

author: taresky
quoted_text:
最近一直在折腾一个新项目：Rungic。

它做的事情很简单：

把一台普通 Android 手机，变成一台属于你自己的 Agent Computer。

Rungic 是开源的

手机里运行完整的 Ubuntu + KDE Plasma，可以直接跑 Firefox、VS Code、Blender、Krita，并使用手机自己的 GPU 加速。

更重要的是，Agent 有属于自己的桌面。

你可以继续正常使用手机，它在另一个 workspace 里自己打开软件、操作 GUI、写代码、跑任务，最后把结果交给你。

以及，这里的电脑不是云端租来的：
Linux 环境、文件、GPU 和执行算力，都在你自己的设备上。
接上电视的 MiraCast ，它又可以直接变成一台 PC。

目前默认 Agent 使用 Codex，但 Rungic 并不绑定某一个 Agent。它真正提供的是 Linux、桌面控制、MCP、手机能力和 Agent Workspace 这些基础设施。

Open Source. Own your computer. Own your compute.

text:
On July 15th, Ostium was attacked and roughly $23.75M was taken from the vault. OLP holders bore that loss, and for the two months that followed, you heard far too little from us. That was a mistake, and I take responsibility for the silence.

We started Ostium four and a half years ago, right out of college, because we believed Real World Asset perpetuals would be the next killer product to come out of crypto after stablecoins. I believe that as much today as I did then.

We pioneered the category. Before the attack we had the second-highest open interest among RWA perp venues and a strong base of core traders. But we were also spread across too many competing priorities, and had begun working to refocus the protocol.

The attack forced a decision. We could try to restart everything we'd been doing as quickly as possible, or we could use the moment to build a more focused company. We chose the second. That took longer than it should have to communicate, because recovery, resource allocation, and the future of the business all depended on the same question: what company are we building from here?

In trying to have every answer before we spoke, we left you without the information you needed at the moment you needed it most. That made a hard situation worse.

I know there's been a lot of speculation about what we were doing. We went quiet, but we didn’t go anywhere. Since July, the team has been developing the next iteration of our trading stack from the ground up, rebuilding our operational and legal footing, and working through significant setbacks, all while sharpening Ostium into a more focused company.

I know this plan isn't what many of you hoped for, especially those with larger losses. Meaningful recovery can only come from Ostium's growth, and Stage 2 will give affected holders a stake in it.

Thank you to our team, and to everyone who waited for answers you deserved sooner. Our core leadership and senior engineering team remains intact and more committed than ever.

Going forward, we will build in the open. We’ll share technical details early on, and will be more incremental than polished. We won't wait until every answer is in hand.

We took a hard hit, but we're very much still here. Tomorrow, we'll share what we've been building since July and where Ostium goes next.

text:
Instinct，由 Spear Street Technology 运营，创始人是 Noah Shinn（诺亚·辛），目前约 23 岁， 9 月 28 日在播客 Invest Like the Best 上与 Patrick O’Shaughnessy 的对谈。就在前几天他刚完成一笔10亿美金的融资，估值也从1个月前的10亿美金涨到100亿美金。这个访谈里可以看到他怎么开始做Instinct，长篇拆解他如何做产品、运营、增长、商业模式和竞争。是一个一手学习的好资料。可以在假期的路上，好好看看。

里面主要内容：

增长
零营销，口碑增长。他称用户规模近期约每天增长 10%–11%。平台年化交易额（GMV）已超过约 10 亿美元，其中约一半来自旅行。

产品方面
早期先追求“可理解性”，而不是先堆能力：用户要能预期它会做什么、结果是否自然。他认为这是口碑超预期的原因之一。

社交智慧，相比之前那些助理，一些提醒不会很频繁的打扰用户，这是他们agent具有了一些社交智慧的技术方案。

预定很重要，他们在开发新的预定系统，并且解决双向需求的新特性。会对双方需求做精准匹配。例如：用户这边说，「这很重要，是我配偶的 30 岁生日。」餐厅那边说，「优先接待生日，尤其是整十岁的生日，或者重要的纪念日。」描述需求、解释为什么重要的后勤负担都没有了，双方就能精准匹配。用户的重要时刻更可能订到位子，餐厅也迎来更好的客群。

agent会记录用户偏好，只告诉一次下次就会记得你的偏好。

关于信任
使用约三周后，约 40% 用户会把个人信用卡交给它；分享过至少一项敏感信息的用户，留存约 80%。授权应按用户节奏逐步放开，并可随时撤回。

商业模式
倾向让用户免费，向商家抽佣（take rate），而不是广告。理由是：比用户更聪明的助手，不该被付钱去说服用户。

Agent 互联
“Trusted Person Network”：两个用户的 Instinct 可以直接协商会议、周末活动、共乘 Uber 等，按关系设置不同权限。这是最有想象力的部分，也是不同于传统类似openclaw的助理部分。也是是否该服务是否存在网络效应的一个关键因素。

对互联网的判断
他认为几年后多数人使用软件的方式会变，互联网会被重写：预订、旅行、订阅等会从“人去点网站”变成“说出结果，助手去办”。他也承认算力是最大约束——大约 40% 的时间在担心算力如何跟上每天 10% 的增长。

关于竞争
承认 Meta Muse 等是好产品，但 Instinct 的路线是尽量待在用户已有的沟通渠道里，而不是再做一个新 App。

text:
準備進入 Uptober，比特幣會漲嗎？要看什麼？

近期 $BTC 漲幅有點像牛市，但其實結構還停在熊市反彈階段，其實這也是老生常談了，在幣圈要知道新多頭有沒有進場，我們要看鏈上數據分布，不是看 Price Action 和社群情緒

@glassnode 獲利供應占比 (Percent Supply in Profit) 的門檻很明確，歷史均值就在 75% 附近，要知道新多頭有沒有進場，我們要看的不是有沒有短暫衝過 75%，而是回調時能不能再站回去並站穩

2019 年中段 +2023 年 4 至 7 月都曾來到這個位置，但 2023 年 8 月一回調，指標就從 71% 掉到 61%，要到同年 11 月重新站上 83% 以上，結構才比較像新牛

目前呢？上周 9/21 的確曾到 78.1%，但到 9/29 已回落到 71.3%，型態更接近「先上衝再回調跌下來」的反彈末端，轉換尚未確認

————————

我們再來看看現貨市場，成本基礎分布 (Cost Basis Distribution) 顯示 84-86k 堆積約 1.39M 枚 BTC，很明顯是上方套牢的人，相對地 82-84k 在從 9/27 至 9/30 三天內從約 110k 枚增厚到 300k 枚，代表現貨一直在吃掉上方賣壓

如果你想知道比較遠的下方強力支撐位，我會說是 72800 ，因為這裡是短線持有者的平均成本 (Short-term holder supply)，距離現價仍有大約 14% 緩衝

————————

至於宏觀面，比特幣不能再靠市場氣氛上漲，必須有人把現貨掃走，但這是什麼意思？

10YR 美債殖利率已經升到 5.17%，扣掉通膨預期後的實質殖利率，一週內已經從 2.68% 升到 2.83%，即是說你把錢放在美債的回報更好，如果沒有特別強的理由，資金肯定不會急著買進比特幣

而且現貨買單主要看 2 個指標：
1. 美國現貨比特幣 ETF
2. BAER 指標

🔴 @bitfinex_asia 用自建指標 BAER 來量強度當天 ETF 買了多少枚，除以礦工每天新挖出的約 450 枚

9 月 21 日 BAER 是 25.6 倍，等於 1 天買走 20 多天的新產量，所以價格能衝上去。但到 9 月 29 日只剩下 1.8 倍，幾乎只剛好吃掉新挖出來的幣，上面那 139 萬枚套牢賣壓根本吃不掉

要消化這道牆，BAER 得回到大約 5 倍，換算就是 ETF 單日淨流入約 1.9 億美元，也就是說低於這個數字，價格比較容易卡在 84k 附近；連續低於再出現單日淨流出，就是轉弱訊號了

————————

那麼總結來說，接下來我們要看到什麼數字？

1️⃣ BTC ETF 日流入是否回到約 $1.9 億
2️⃣ 10 年期實質殖利率會不會再往 2.83% 上面走
3️⃣ 84-86k 的 1.39M 枚 BTC 被吃掉
4️⃣ 86.5k-90k 只剩約 51.3 萬枚（容易被吃掉）
5️⃣ Uptober 展望 95k

如果 1-2 變強，現貨價格才有力上漲

如果 2 發生，價格又跌破 82.5k 那就優先看 81.3k-81.9k 有沒有人接（舊買家成本位）

如果 3-4 發生，到時候才來聊新多頭，展望 5

text:
今天这场撕逼，完整版是这样的：

Factory：做模型无关的 coding agent，这个月刚融 2 亿美元、估值约 50 亿。投资方包括红杉、Khosla Ventures、Blackstone 等。

Cognition：做 Devin，更早、更大，刚融超 20 亿美元、估值约 480 亿。

两边是 AI 编程 Agent 赛道的直接对手。

中间这个人是 Chris Degnan：Snowflake 第一位销售、后来当过 CRO，被两边都当成顶级销售人才。

他给 Factory 当了一年多董事会观察员/顾问，今天宣布去 Cognition 当 CRO。

时间线：

Factory CEO Matan Grinberg 先发长文，说他们“开除”了 Degnan，理由是涉及 Cognition 的不道德行为。

他控两点：Cognition 工程师假装来 Factory 面试套产品信息；Degnan 一边开 Factory 董事会、看机密路线图，一边跟 Cognition 高管频繁接触，最后被挖走。

他还说 Degnan 之前跟他保证过“钱赚够了、懒得去 Cognition”。

Degnan 立刻反击：不是被开，是周一自己辞职，并告诉对方要去 Cognition；Factory 还想留他全职，他拒绝了。

上次参加董事会是几周前，那时候还没跟 Cognition 谈过。Cognition 从没问过 Factory 的信息，他也从没给过。

Cognition CEO Scott Wu 出面：指控不属实。他们没兴趣要 Factory 的信息，也不会让工程师暗中收集竞品情报。

两边都想要 Degnan，因为他是把销售从 0 做到 30 亿量级的人。

Snowflake 老人出来保 Degnan。跟 Degnan 共事五年的 Bob Muglia 说他一贯有操守。

投资人开始站队，而且自己人打自己人：

红杉 Shaun Maguire（投了 Factory）最冲，说 Cognition 不懂他们手里有“能灭了他们的核武器”，还补刀：“Cognition 就是 Infosys 假装成 Anthropic。”

Khosla Ventures 合伙人 Keith Rabois 站 Factory：还在开董事会、吃董事会晚餐的同时去面竞品，这件事本身就不道德。

Khosla Ventures 创始人 Vinod Khosla 反过来骂 Factory：二流对手、更不道德、撒谎、绝望。还说“撒谎称 Chris 是被开除的，我以为这都低于你的底线了”。

问题是 Khosla 两边都投了。既投 Cognition，也刚参与 Factory 这轮融资。所以他公开踩自家另一家公司，被点名利益冲突。

同一家基金两个合伙人公开站对立面。 
有创始人开始骂 Khosla 的利益冲突文化。 
Factory 天使投资人 Nathan Lands 发帖说，几个月前跟 Khosla 的人聊时，对方觉得 AI 钱太多、冲突无所谓，还用很物化的方式比较 Factory 和 Cognition 创始人。

这已经从个案跳槽，扩成对这家基金做事方式的攻击。

到现在还没出现的，是任何一方把聊天记录、邮件、会议纪年完整公开。故事还停在“各说各的 + 投资人内讧”。

Factory 说有邮件收据但不想先发；红杉暗示手里还有更重的东西。

quoted_text:
We are terminating Chris Degnan for unethical conduct involving Cognition.

The last few months have seen incredible progress in AI capabilities. San Francisco has flourished as new companies that solve new, more ambitious problems are finding great success. Generally, it is a wonderful time to be building.

We at @FactoryAI have seen overwhelming interest in our model-agnostic coding agents and our software factory product. Our team has 10x’d in size, while our revenue has 100x’d year over year. This momentum has been unprecedented.

A much larger competitor, Cognition (makers of Devin) has fallen behind us on the capabilities that matter most to customers: cost, quality, and security. Instead of competing in the market, Cognition engineers feigned interviews with us to pry information about our product. Not finding what they were looking for, Cognition has decided to throw their weight and money at people with direct knowledge of our most confidential plans.

It feels as though ethics is being thrown out of the window in the AI era. People are willing to do anything, including exploiting privileged information and violating ethical boundaries. I think this is unique to our time, and I don’t think it’s right. Integrity still matters.

Yesterday, I made the decision to immediately terminate Christopher Degnan’s roles as a Board Observer and Advisor to Factory, after over a year of service.

Prior to this decision, Chris told me he had a casual conversation with an executive at Cognition AI. When I questioned his intentions, he reassured me that ethics aside, he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which I trusted and believed.

On Monday, Chris spent time advising the Factory team on a handful of confidential board-level matters. That evening, he called me to say that the conversation that was initially described as casual and one-off was actually formal and recurring. For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light.

It is sad to sever a relationship with someone who has been a trusted advisor - and even a close friend -  for over a year. But Chris’s conduct is unacceptable to me. Trust in Board Membership is one of the sacred bonds in the Silicon Valley, one that helps the startup ecosystem thrive. With it comes an enormous responsibility. That trust was violated.

Competition is good. I respect and in many cases admire our competitors. San Francisco is a beautiful, singular place where the bold and ambitious go to defy the norms and precedents of the past. But certain principles that must remain. Violating ethics to seek advantage turns what should be positive-sum into zero-sum.

We all love technology. And we all love to compete. But we must hold ourselves to a higher standard. The future of software engineering comes with abundance that will impact every person on Earth. Building that future comes with immense responsibility. We must build and compete with integrity.

text:
The most bullish outcome for NEAR is probably users having zero clue what chain their trade even settled on.

That’s why $NEAR suddenly makes way more sense to me than it did at $2.

Coin did 180% in a month so yeah, obviously some of this is squeeze + ETF positioning.

but under the giga candle, @NEARProtocol kinda changed the whole thesis when it started leaning into Intents instead of the usual L1 game.

– $32B all-time volume across ~36 chains and ~200 assets

– $4.5B volume in the last 30d

– $51M lifetime fees

– $6.5M+ fees over the last month

More important, some of that flow is actually accruing back now.

Gross take rate is 15 bps, NEAR captures roughly 25-28% of those fees, which produced around $1.7-1.8M net revenue in the last 30d.

Not exactly cheap vs $6.7B mcap, but at least this is real orderflow paying real fees.

And the privacy meta might be the wedge that fuels the product.

Confidential Intents TVL is $174M, up from ~$70M around mid-Sep.

$2.4B of ZEC has historically moved through Intents, which kinda explains why NEAR suddenly became part of the privacy trade.

Hyperliquid perps were plugged into the same flow with confidential mode on by default, ~50 markets and up to 40x leverage.

So someone can basically express the trade through NEAR while liquidity still comes from somewhere like Hyperliquid.

Then they added Ondo tokenized stocks into Intents too.

NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, SPY, QQQ etc can now sit inside the same routing layer, with confidential execution optional.

I like the direction because tokenized stocks + crosschain routing + privacy actually fit together.

And the ecosystem itself got some attention:

@rhea_finance / solana:8SMMso8Muv8d6i4WmMDthKt6TN1ysN6937sx3DKLXZqB: NEAR’s DeFi liquidity hub, ~$291M TVL, ~$23.5B lifetime DEX volume, with lending, Earn and solver liquidity plugged directly into Intents.

@auroraisnear / ethereum:0xaaaaaa20d9e0e2461697782ef11675f668207961: turning NEAR Intents into embeddable cross-chain infra for wallets/apps.

@NearKatSol / solana:6UtY9iTZMQQ5QZVrbzFnNaJntV7oySm9k97mvwnuZcxr: Solana meme with a 3% transfer tax farming $NEAR for holders, already sprayed out ~328K NEAR.

@nearlytrade / $NEARLY: launchpad built on Rhea + Intents, with locked CL pools, Ondo stock-paired memes, creator fee payouts to wallets/X handles, and ~$10M+ volume in its first 6 days.

@shardsmarket / $SHARDS: launchpad using Intents + Ondo, letting memes pair with NEAR, ZEC, $SHARDS or tokenized stocks/gold.

@around_near / $AROUND: trading fees get turned into $NVDAon, then split between stakers, holders and treasury.

Users probably shouldn’t need to care that any of this settled through NEAR. Meanwhile trenchers already busy trying to front-run the next runner there.

text:
朱元璋没走大运之前，也得老老实实要饭，所以人急真的没用。

想想还挺有意思的。朱元璋17岁的时候，那年大旱加蝗灾加瘟疫，半个月里他爹、他娘、他哥相继饿死，家里穷得连块埋人的坟地都没有。为了活命，他跑去皇觉寺当和尚，结果寺里五十天后也断粮了，主持发给他一个钵，就把他打发出去要饭。

他在淮西那一带要了整整三年饭。从17岁走到20岁，一个人拿着破碗在荒年里四处流浪，挨饿受冻，看尽了人情冷暖。等要完饭回庙里，又猫了整整四年，天天打扫烧香看书，直到二十五岁那年收到发小汤和的一封信，跑去投奔郭子兴，他命运的齿轮才算真正开始转动。

大运没来的时候，就安心要饭。

保持敏锐，把身体养好，把底层的基本功练扎实。等时代的风吹过来的时候，你身上得有帆，才接得住这股力。

My first piece for @NewYorker is out today!

As Xi Jinping lands in DC to start his state visit, you'll hear a lot about the US-China AI race. I'd like to tell a complementary AI story.

This past May, a few days after Trump visited Beijing, I went to the town people call China's vibe-coding capital, Liangzhu. There, you learn that China's AI scene is not monolithic. It's also full of contrarians, cool vibe coders, spiritual seekers, and people who love AI but refuse to join the 996 grind.

Liangzhu is on the edge of Hangzhou. I hung out with a group of anti-mainstream builders who use AI to make whimsical apps for fortune-telling, mental well-being, and creativity. Some of them run their lives entirely by bazi astrology (their founder almost became a Taoist monk). They meet on "Crazy Thursday" to vibe-code together. Rent is cheap, so they can get a bigger place with a living room to have friends over (unthinkable in Beijing or Shenzhen). In Liangzhu, they want to use AI to forge their own future.

It’s a ground-level story—less about model capabilities, hyperscalers, or AI policy, and more about how people in China are using AI, and the human stories behind it.

text:
I have been using the new ultrafast mode for Astra 6 for the last couple of days. My main takeaways:

1. Token speed qualitatively changed how I interact with agents. The output speed is 300 tokens/second, 8x the regular speed. Rather than breaking flow and switching tasks, the model moves (just) fast enough that I can keep working on the same task, especially for work that requires frequent inputs from me. I am excited about ultrafast on Sol-class models, which are twice as fast as Astra.

2. Despite being 8x faster at generating tokens, the overall speedup is only 2-4x, since the time consumed for tool calling or running code remains the same. External factors (and not token generation speed) might soon become the main bottleneck for agentic work. (Notably @random_walker predicted both of these changes in: https://t.co/BXNtg9vzCt)

3. One area where speed really helps is computer use. The previous generation of models wasn't reliable enough at computer use to be useful. Astra was reliable enough to be useful, but still slow. Astra with ultrafast resolves both concerns. Unlike tool calls for coding tasks, UIs react in milliseconds, so token speed is the main bottleneck.

4. At 300 tokens/sec, I am already struggling to keep up with the agent. But there is a lot more room for improvement. Cerebras serves GPT-OSS-120B at 3,000 tokens/sec and Sol at 750 tokens/sec. So in a year's time, it is plausible we'll see another 10x increase in speed in models with Astra-level capabilities. At that point, human oversight will become the bottleneck for what people can use computer-use agents for.

5. I can imagine blazing fast computer-use agents becoming extremely common for knowledge work. But I expect their use will be jagged (in the same way as LLM and agent adoption has been): given the oversight challenge, adoption will begin in verifiable tasks where the cost of errors is low (e.g., filling out a form using an agent before reviewing it yourself), and slowly diffuse to hard-to-verify tasks.

6. Given the challenges with human oversight, the key to this diffusion will be developing automated oversight tools. OpenAI's approval/verifier agents have already been useful to me on this front: The verifier understood my intent better than the computer-use agent, and stopped it from filling out a form incorrectly. Still, I expect there is a lot of headroom in improving verifiers for computer use, to make it as reliable in practice as auto mode in Claude Code/Codex is for coding tasks.

7. Ultrafast mode is undeniably resource intensive: I ran through my weekly limit in ~2 hours while filling out a bunch of forms and doing simple coding tasks. But given the pace of efficiency improvements (and the fact that Sol is 5x cheaper than Astra and already decent at computer use), I expect it to rapidly fall. Once fast, cheap models are common, users may choose "sub-frontier" models like Sol and make real tradeoffs between speed and quality.
author: ahall_research
quoted_text: Prediction: we will soon enter an era where the latency of agentic work is bottlenecked not by LLM inference speed but by tool use. Shell commands, build pipelines, computer use, web data extraction, and everything else that happens in the background is way slower than it needs to be, because it hasn't been subjected to the same kind of optimization pressure as LLMs, and isn't really getting faster.

author: 0xzhaozhao
quoted_text:
如何判断妖币行情是否要结束
​
​很多人只知道看链上大额代币转入到交易所，庄家要砸盘，这种反而是最容易迷惑对手的。

因为链上很多人都在监控庄家的动作，一旦庄家把币转入交易所，那么散户绝对比庄家提前操作，本质上来说这就是从庄家口袋里掏钱，庄家是不会让这种事情发生的，那么庄家会想尽办法把这批聪明钱屠杀殆尽

早期拉几百倍的myx，7月份拉升几十倍的bank，还有这几天拉升十几倍的龙虾都发生了这样的一幕，在庄家把币转入到交易所后币价不但不跌转而快速反抽几倍，爆掉新进来的空单聪明钱，爆完之后再完成妖币的操盘
​
​第二种情况是代币没有转入到交易所，这种庄家的操作是准备砸盘的前几天，停止从交易所往链上提币的动作，然后在交易所慢慢收集用来砸盘的筹码，甚至可以不需要收集，比如庄家在价格底部吸筹买了1000万美金代币，但是只提走500万美金，从盘面上来看最直接的就是币价拉升的速度快过了任何时候，但是链上动作似乎很少，可以作为一个辅助判断鱼尾崩盘行情是否开始，同时空单爆仓金额越来越大，一度超过了2000万美金

在山寨妖币里面千万别做空，我也跟粉丝多次强调代币转入交易所是平仓信号，不是做空理由。
​上述文章只是为了给各位现货止盈点位一个参考，希望大家还是不要玩合约

Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

https://t.co/bZZU5oNlWp

A full investigation is underway, and further updates will be shared as they become available. For further details, please refer to the MetaMask Staking release linked below.

No @Waymo in Maine or New Hampshire yet.

Electric doesn’t do well in cold weather. So locals are resisting electric, I learned today. Lots of big trucks.

A much slower pace of life than San Francisco. Great for vacations but is like living in the past. Which is attractive to most Americans.

I had dinner with the owner of a $30 million 1959 Jaguar. First car with disc brakes.

Asked him why he collected it? 

“I wanted a time capsule that takes me back to 1959.”

The car won many races because of its disk brakes. When Audi taught me to race first lesson was on braking. “To go fast you must learn to go slow.”

If I were a billionaire I might have bought the same car, but for a different reason.

Innovation in automobiles is so rare.

I find hanging with the builders is much more interesting.

But tomorrow we see the fall foliage which is out in splendor.

Mt wife and I have wanted to do that for a long time.

Oh and I am trying to ignore the epic fights in AI industry. But damn.

Did we just throw out all the rules?

Seems like when there is a billion or two involved the rules change.

Which I learned by following that Jaguar.

We were doing 120 m.p.h. behind a bunch of Motorcycle cops.

The billionaires literally change the law as they drive along. We did that all day for four days.

Unfortunately I do not have the same power.

I used to give PR advice since I helped write Microsoft’s first social media policy.

But now?

I have no idea what the rules are anymore.

It used to be investors wouldn’t invest in two companies but now they call entrepreneurs names in public and do that two. 

Wild times.

Robots will sell better in San Francisco.

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
I took this video at IROS’26 in Pittsburgh two days ago. At first glance, it looks like an impressive autonomous humanoid making cocktail drinks. Zoom out, and you see what is really behind it.

I have mixed feelings about watching this.

1. Teleoperation is getting remarkably good.
Data collection is becoming more accurate, scalable, and immersive. Combined with rapidly improving AI models, I can imagine much of this eventually becoming autonomous. That is exciting, but it also makes the potential impact on human jobs feel much more immediate.

2. But what are we actually seeing in a robot demo?
Without proper disclosure or reference, it can be surprisingly difficult to distinguish teleoperation from autonomy. As physical AI attracts more attention and investment, demos need to be much clearer about how much is autonomous and how much is human-controlled.

3. Even “autonomous” demos can be difficult to interpret.
Is the robot actually generalizing? Or is it replaying a demonstration, following a scripted trajectory, or overfitting to one carefully prepared environment? A tabletop demo alone often can’t tell us.

Maybe the important question for Physical AI is no longer just “Can the robot do it?”
It is also: “How did the robot do it, and will it still work when we change the task, objects, or environment?”

quoted_text:
I can share the inside baseball here. Not one super PAC, nor Trump WH, has reached out to ask people, "Will you help us get out the vote?" There is a level of entitlement, and then rage when this entitlement is unmet, that I've never seen. Bot swarms seek to discredit anyone who suggests that the Republicans and PACs need to run a better game. It's some bizarre moral black mail scheme. I honestly don't know what people think it's been effective. I've only seen it backfiring.

There are people who have gotten generational wealth by "lobbying" and "consulting" in ways that the general public might find less than ideal. Some of these people are lashing out at anyone who doesn't toe the line, but who have they helped with their newfound wealth? They have not done anything to fund legal defense group for staffers who will face lawfare. Those groups are woefully underfunded. Very good people with new families are already losing sleep. This is unacceptable.

Everyone knows that insiders stick their beak in once their guy wins, and the Green New Deal slush fund makes a lot of this stuff seem like small potatoes. In any case, people talk, everyone knows everything going on in DC. Some, like myself, don't "call it out," because that only helps Democrats. Calling this hypocritical or whatever wouldn't offend me. I am not a priest or pastor or exemplar of morality. 

Balancing independent reporting and analysis while not wanting to turn the country over to people who seek to murder children is a line I challenge all of my critics to walk. See what it's like and the feedback you get. 

Downstream it's the voters who get screwed, and that's the only reason I haven't totally checked out this cycle. I  hope people vote Republican. I've said this repeatedly. But the lack of basic courtesy one would expect has been jarring.

We do this for the country, but also are "only human." When you get nothing but nastiness from people getting rich by riding the waves you create, you are left wondering, "What the hell am I doing with my life?"

My loyalty is always firstly to the people who have read me over the years, as these are the people who want to save civilization, they receive no thanks or recognition, they are expected to eat shit while the big donors get their way. That is the only reason I am still here. If this were truly only about politics, or if this were my career, I'd have left. Every day I want to leave, every day I wake up and wonder why bother.

And before the usual suspects go, "Waaah." It's quite the opposite. People are whining to me, "Do more! You can't sit this out!" Many of these folks recently called me "irrelevant." Suddenly I'm supposed to, without being apologized to, or politely asked, shill for the midterms 24/7. 

You can't treat people this way and expect to win like it's 2024 again. 

And I speak for a lot of people. Not merely those in my shoes or others, but the voters who lost friends, business opportunities, and sometimes their own freedom, for putting on the MAGA hat.

Ignore my concerns if you like, but this isn't stuff unique to me nor is it new.

太牛逼了，A股上市芯片公司寒武纪前高管向公司索赔278亿元🤯

刚看到昨天寒武纪发的公告，公司原副总经理梁军把对寒武纪的索赔金额，从42.87亿元直接提高到了278.32亿元。

梁军2022年初从寒武纪离职。

按照寒武纪的说法，公司随后依据梁军本人签署的《持股计划B》执行股权回购，但梁军拒绝配合，双方从2023年开始一路打官司。

到现在，梁军和寒武纪股权激励平台、管理主体之间相关的案件一共已经有6起，梁军全部败诉，其中回购案件已经进入司法强制执行阶段。

但事情还没完。

梁军另外以劳动争议为由，要求寒武纪赔偿他的股权激励损失。

一开始索赔42.87亿，现在直接改成了278.32亿，涨了差不多6.5倍。

这个278亿是怎么来的也很有意思。

根据公告，经过2025年度利润分配和资本公积转增股本后，相关份额间接对应的寒武纪股票增加到了约1717万股。

梁军计算损失时，采用的是寒武纪从2024年1月2日到提交申请期间的最高股价1620元/股。

也就是说，这个索赔金额基本是拿历史最高价去算自己失去的那部分股票值多少钱。

不过这里还是要强调一下：278.32亿目前只是梁军一方提出的诉讼请求（法院不太可能支持）。 

这起劳动争议案件目前甚至还没有开庭。

寒武纪方面也明确表示不认可这一诉求，认为此前生效判决已经确认梁军离职触发了股份回购条款。

278亿是什么概念。

很多上市公司一辈子的利润都未必有这么多。

这是我见过金额最离谱的离职高管股权纠纷之一了。。。。

Long Lake buys great businesses and makes them better with AI. Their engineers sit alongside the people doing the work, understand what slows them down, and build tools that give them more time to serve customers.

Alex wants to spend the next 50 years on this. We talk about how far it could go.

text:
刚刚，白宫把 Google、Anthropic、Meta、OpenAI、xAI、NVIDIA 拉到了一起，签了一份《White House Accord on Super Intelligence》。

在场签字的人都是美国现在最核心的 AI 领导者：Sundar Pichai、Dario Amodei、Mark Zuckerberg、Greg Brockman、Elon Musk、Jensen Huang，以及特朗普（aha）。

我仔细看了下协议，篇幅其实非常短，但里面有一条挺有意思：

前沿模型公司需要建立内部控制，持续监测模型在网络安全、生物安全、化学威胁等领域的能力和对齐情况，并确保模型不会以非预期方式 hack 或访问技术系统。

这基本就是把这段时间越来越频繁出现的 Agent 越权、模型逃逸、自动化网络攻击问题，正式加到白宫文件里管控了。

整个协议实际上要求了四层机制：

模型训练和部署阶段的内部安全控制；
独立的内部团队负责检查这些控制是否真的有效；
引入外部独立审计或评估机构；
董事会设立独立委员会，直接监督这些安全问题。

但这目前不是法律，而是一份自愿协议（意味着没屁用）。

北美的太阳特朗普把它称为 morally binding，也就是道义上的约束。

协议里还写了一句，未来可能有必要把这些措施进一步写进法律或监管。

几家公司之后也会定期开会，继续制定共同的安全标准和最佳实践。

顺便还有个很抽象的细节：这份讨论 Super Intelligence 的白宫文件，在特朗普签名下面把 President of the United States 写成了 President of the Unites States。

人类开始治理超级智能的第一天，先把自己国家名字拼错了🤣

Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

这次我们具体看看 @SolvProtocol  冻结 50BTC的事情的前因后果.

首先SolvBTC被盗已经不是第一次了, 2026年3月6日,因为合约漏洞 (重入攻击), 就被盗过一次,协议损失了38个BTC(260万美元左右).

这次的是    2026年7月13日 01:02am

Solv的合约管理员私钥泄露, 增发了三次 BTC+代币(你理解为SolvBTC),
第一次30枚,15分钟后,第二次100枚, 1分钟后 第三次, 这次直接mint了2.575×10²⁰ 枚,   其中极少部分走去组建了 Uniswap v4的池子,  钓鱼看有没有人来买.

BSC tx: 0xed32ab3ab5dde91b228db1adf525967c98c7d502726735d95a6c390ee4572a0b

然后Solv官方在 1点36 开始关闭赎回.  3点16的时候 , 把这些增发的BTC+代币全部销毁了.

黑客总获利很少, 就组池子赚了1万多美元.. (有几个夹子机器人,看到BTC+ 几乎为0的价格了,买了一些)

总体来看, SolvBTC因为冻结和销毁及时, 损失在5万美元以下.

7月31号 Solv协议开放提现(BTC+ 1:1兑换成 BTC),  到目前为止, 用户共发起了148 笔赎回, 提出了共 52.11 BTC+, 单笔最大赎回9.87个BTC.

我们再来看看受害者:

 tx: 0xb43636b61e9da53a03ae627cf24d495f0b9cf1a344c48d48e2f6602d663a53f7

当天兑换了 48.9个Solv的 BTC+.    7月18日, 受害者在自己的币安web3钱包里和另外一个钱包里, 把这些代币来回转了3次. 估计是到Solv官方的被攻击通告后, 看一下有没有冻住.

7/31 15:42:45   (也就是黑客攻击后的第18天,  和开放散户提现的同一天) 
Solv的官方协议, 把受害者的钱包拉黑, 代币已经不能移动和交互了, 
tx: 0x603c41bf1f6a5b54bce142eea75ab60dca59a632dab41e07c22db4efc0f81fc5

只有这一个钱包被拉黑.

----------------------------------------------------

In early 2025, @iamxxhe  and I were pitching a sponsor for our first hackathon.

Halfway through our deck, the sponsor interrupted:

“Did you see that token? I think it’s gone up 10x since we started this call.” 🤯

We both went quiet.

Seconds earlier, we’d been discussing how to support developers. Now we were scrambling to find the trading pair on our phones while trying to keep the pitch going.

I found the wrong pair.

My first brush with financial freedom, and I couldn’t even find the right button.

Shafi and I met through @iclblockchain  I was working on biosensors in the lab and trading perps on the side; he was deep into quant.

Our first shared achievement? Losing all our pocket money. 😂

We believed in AI agents—and hoped they might improve our bank balances. We invested in a friend’s project, kept “buying the dip” while organising our first hackathon, and eventually lost everything we’d put in.

But we kept building together.

The money disappeared. The partnership stayed. And together, we built @imperialaisoc.

One hackathon became two, then three, four and five. 67 soon.

Over 18 months, those five events brought together:

→ 2,000+ builders
→ 200+ projects
→ More than $200,000 in combined announced prize pools
→ Millions of views online

We’d gone from putting our money into tokens to bringing sponsor support to developers. This time, we could see things being built.

This week, we brought founders, AI leaders and investors together at the House of Lords for @UKAIagents.

Looking around the room, I kept thinking about how much had grown out of those early conversations.

Members have taken on forward-deployed engineering projects, joined incubators, raised funding and met their co-founders.

One community member shared an early idea with me. Two months later, he had raised $4 million and moved to San Francisco.

Those achievements belong to them—their talent, work and decisions. We’re simply grateful to have provided a place where some of those connections began.

And we want to help more of those stories continue beyond the event.

Today, we’re officially launching @UKAIagents  to take this community further.

We’ll keep hosting high-quality events while helping our founders and fellows access small grants and early-stage funding, connect with the right investors, and find the compute resources they need to keep building.

Sometimes the next step is a technical mentor. Sometimes it’s a first paying customer. Sometimes it’s one introduction to someone who understands what you’re trying to build.

I’m so glad we’re in this wave together—with our incredible founders and the support of our partners and sponsors, we truly apperiate all the support from our amazing sponsors, partners like @LauraModiano , @davidgelberg and surrounded by top builders like @gary_yangge, our founding member and new @iclblockchain pres @may_tohoku and so many more, i can't wait to see what we build together.

text:
For all the angst about lab ARR (“where is ANT now?!”), remember that revenue growth is still constrained by how much compute the labs can bring online.

I see two races being run in real time.  A race at the frontier and a RACE TO SERVE.  The latter matters more short term for the AI trade, imho, bc demand for intelligence keeps outrunning supply.

AWS is raising reserved GPU prices for a 4th straight quarter (H200s +75% YTD), and compute availability is near the lows.  H/t @WarrenPies, who does some of the best work around this.  Hard to see much slack in the system.

Yields are clouding the picture today, and folks are understandably cautious.  But zoom out, and the key investment question remains how to get the most upside to Jensen’s right tail scenario (longer/bigger build, tighter compute).  If 2027-28 looks as different from today as today does from 2023, there’s an immense opportunity ahead.

In that scenario, a levered balance sheet can be an asset, even if the current rate path suggests otherwise.  Tighter compute can mean stronger cash flows and faster deleveraging.  And if AI disinflation eventually lowers the cost of capital, you have yourself quite the parlay…

Jensen seems to especially like this trade :).  Sized right, a small position can offer option-like upside.  Good luck out there.

Built On Aleo 🛠️

Dynamic: build a private payments app in a weekend, not a quarter 🔐

@dynamic_xyz, a Fireblocks company, is now live on Aleo as the first wallet infrastructure provider to support institutional-grade embedded wallets for private payments.

Building private, blockchain-based payments has always meant building your own wallet stack first. Onboarding, key management, recovery, transaction signing, all before you ship a single feature. That's a real barrier, especially for the teams that need privacy the most.

Payroll companies who can't publish salaries to a public ledger. Aid organizations moving funds into conflict zones. Crisis response teams who can't afford visibility into their operations.

Dynamic removes the barrier. Developers plug into existing wallet infrastructure, MPC-based key management, onboarding, and disaster recovery, all built for Aleo's public and shielded balances, and skip building it themselves.

Adding Aleo takes one toggle in the Dynamic dashboard. Existing embedded wallets pick up public and shielded balances automatically.

As @turbahn, cofounder of Dynamic and VP of Embedded Wallets at Fireblocks, put it: a developer at a payroll company who's never touched crypto should be able to build a private payments app in a weekend. That's the bar.

author: nickvasiles
quoted_text:
There's a huge opportunity right now in being the deployment layer for AI into the economy. The amount of work it takes to change out workflows in enterprises tends to be far greater than anyone realizes or would prefer. Clearly this is what the applied layer of AI is going to look like in the form of software and agents, but also it opens up new services firms opportunities.

Legacy systems need to be moved to the cloud, data organization and access needs to be updated, software needs to be connected to agents in new ways, workflows need to be reengineered for agents, HITL needs to be figured out for the process, evals need to be generated and maintained, and the entire system needs to be continually updated as new models get released and new capabilities emerge. And the full list may even be longer.

AI is not the same as just deploying software. Software you generally did the implementation of an existing, well understood category of technology, then stepped back and the customer kept running. With AI agents, you're delivering actual work augmentation to the organization, which has a completely different set of complexities associated with it. You're no longer deploying tools that the company is merely enabled by, you're deploying work output in a process. Completely different implementation and enablement process.

As a result, this is going to open up lots of new kinds of firms and plays for existing firms to diffuse AI into organizations. We're going to see approaches by industry, by size of company, and by problem inside of companies. Traditional SIs will modernize and adapt (some will clearly not adapt as well), and new entrants will also be founded in this period that take advantage of this window. Great time to be an FDE or FDE firm.

quoted_text:
I was going to write this one for subscribers, but I have to make this for everyone because so many people still don't see the vision

I still think robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 is the most asymmetric project on Robinhood Chain. This is a net-new vertical, with all the right levers in a world where AI demand is accelerating.

Yes, inference marketplaces have been tried in crypto. But none have worked at scale. With CREDIT, akin to DIEM, you now have succeeded at tokenizing inference. And in doing so, you basically unlock credits for an increasingly agentic world. Agents need fuel they can buy and use without a human in the loop; This is the start of inference as an onchain commodity. 

This is obviously a pro-sumer application; but that's fine because the largest winners of AI inference are individuals and small teams, not enterprises. Enterprises are either A) developing in-house model harnesses for privacy purposes, or B) have infinite budget for AI

And people treat that like a bear case - I don't see a problem with being for consumers. The TAM for consumer inference is still huge - Menlo Ventures State of Consumer AI est. 1.7b - 1.8b use AI tools ; at $20/m that's 432b a year. Also, in their enterprise report, product-led growth drives 27% of AI spend, and shadow AI (employees paying on their own) pushes that closer to 40%. Cursor hit $200M in revenue before hiring a single enterprise sales rep. 

There is a clear latent demand for cheap inference amongst pro-sumers. The unlocks are clear - it can become the payment layer for AI agents; More users buying credits leads to more demand for CREDIT, which makes staking ORBIO more valuable, which raises the ORBIO price, which creates more trading fees, which funds more discounts, which brings in more users. As long as it keeps spinning, each part feeds the others.

It combines three hot themes: AI agents, tokenized real-world assets, and Robinhood Chain. The NVDA-linked fee route adds to that. In a strong market, a story this clean can attract a lot of capital, which itself funds the subsidy for longer.

And of course, above it all, the man pushing this himself - @0x_aster is a cracked dev who has shown his capabililties are far beyond the norm; Multiple updates within a week, clear direction - this is founder-market fit. 

In crypto, actions carry way more weight than words. And look at what he's shipped man... a working gateway, a live orderbook, and now tokenized inference. The man is A MACHINE. This is what AI x strong founders can do - go beyond 10x engineer to become a 10,000x engineer. HE'S CRACKED!

Founder-market fit matters more in this sector than most. A team that ships slowly gets left behind by the market itself. 

And for the bear takes:

Q: DIEM already does this, why do we need another one

- DIEM is precisely the success case. VVV is valued at 1B. ORBIO is valued at 15m. Also, VVV is going in the direction of private AI. ORBIO is going in the direction of serving the layer of inference for consumers across the world. CREDIT is $1 of usage you hold until you need it. Burst-heavy users (agents running a big job, devs shipping a feature) don't use the same amount every day. They need compute they can stockpile, buy at a discount, and spend in one go.

Lastly, markets rarely have one winner. Stablecoins didn't stop at USDT. Venice proved people will pay for tokenized inference. There is room for a second design.

Q: It's just an OpenRouter reseller. There's no moat.

Fair take. Yes, bits can be copied, there's no moat there. The moat is the market - liquidity begets liquidity in any marketplace. There's 20 different perp dexes. Who wins? The most liquid markets with the most volume traded on it. 

And obv there is no confirmed answer, but ultimately, that's what markets are - I'm betting on this

Q: "They could be shut down"

This is the most legitimate bear take, yes. Platform risk is real for any aggregator. But labs want volume, and resellers bring demand they wouldn't otherwise get. Venice has run Claude, GPT and Gemini through a token model at scale, which suggests it can work.

But on top of that, as the world moves towards open source, this becomes less and less of a risk ;

text:
也聊聊美光的财报，为何财报很爆股价波澜不惊？1、先看下财报要点：
1）财报依然很强劲，营收和利润规模已进入全新量级，毛利率达到传统半导体难以想象的水平，SCA+押金大幅提升业绩可见度。对下一季的指引也很乐观（营收、EPS大幅超预期）。

DRAM出货量环比增长中个位数，均价（ASP）环比上涨高teen%。
NAND位元出货环比约+10%，价格环比增长约+30%。量价齐升，当然价还是远远跑过量的。

2）长期业绩确定性
未履约订单1500亿美金（上季度1000亿美金）；
累计签26份SCA（长协），覆盖至2030年约35%以上收入（目标仍约50%）；客户财务承诺约 320亿美元（绝大部分为现金押金），超过 75% 的2027年出货已承诺；
客户讨论已转向2028年，部分协议延长至2031年；
即使按地板价，毛利率也显著高于以往周期峰值

2、怎么看财报和市场的反应
1）回到8月中对存储的判断，当时认为“空存性价比不高，向上还有空间，但走势不会那么丝滑，更像是大科技/英伟达的走势”，现在回看过去一个半月存储基本就是这么走的、慢慢往上挪。

就是大家也都清楚存储现在还在短缺卡脖子，二季度财报AI商业化也在加速，那就意味着存储需求没有减弱。未来扩产后需求是不是能保持大家依然还有怀疑。导致了现在美光、海力士等基本上都是依托盈利驱动、估值基本没动过。

2）但为什么股价没有大动？
周一跟朋友有聊过“美光财报会很好，但对市场不是决定性的。因为他是受益方、不是支出方、不是商业化最下游”（下图一）

这里的逻辑在于
（1）美光财报很好、但是它是产业链上游，它把通过长协把这种受益做成了合同和押金，通过押金、多年协议把未来业绩的可见度进一步打开，实质上就是把波动率往下压、把利润持续性往上抬。业绩走高是当下股价的安全基石和驱动。

（2）但它验证不了商业化的强弱。最终AI商业化可需求的开关仍在云厂商和应用变现手里。所以美光财报能提振情绪和板块叙事，但决定不了AI交易的主矛盾。其实半导体产业链上的业绩扩张现在更像产业温度计，不是行情发动机。

（3）钱有没有从训练/推理花出去之后赚回来？这是市场一直在追问的问题（当然个人角度认为未来是能赚回来的）
美光再强也回答不了这个问题。所以它很难单独成为“AI交易是否成立”的决定性验证。如果明天微软或Meta砍 capex、或者推理侧商业化数据难看，美光再好的指引也会被一起杀估值。反过来，只要支出方还在加码，美光这种供给刚性标的就会继续享受定价权。

3、什么情况下、美光、海力士等会迎来估值扩张？
1）当下市场自然还是有部分担心，担心高毛利不可持续、担心需求未来会走弱、担心扩产后价格回落。核心市场的关注点已从“能高到哪”转到“能维持多久”。

当代美光股价1065美金上下，
FY2026 Non-GAAP EPS 75.52 → 约14倍当年盈利
预期FY2027 EPS约 160 → 约 6.5–7倍 远期盈利
看很多投行分析师给的最新目标价中枢大约 1500 附近，隐含逻辑仍然是“盈利上修”，不是“倍数大幅打开”

2）什么情景下美光才会估值扩张？
（1）下游商业化数据好到让市场愿意给存储更高倍数，商业化进展超预期而且让市场确认持续性很强，这是最有力的支撑、能支撑需求。

（2）供给比现在预期更紧
今天在财报电话会议上，美光管理层认为2027、2028年存储供需将比2026年更紧，看不到平衡时点。但貌似市场还没那么接受。

供给比预期更紧、要么是需求爆发更强、要么是扩产新厂爬坡慢于市场害怕的速度（管理层已经在说：出片后还要几个季度才有实质影响）

还是在8月初提到的3个思考（下图二）：
1）周期顶部会不会比市场预期更晚？
只要AI服务器、HBM、服务器DRAM和企业级SSD需求持续增长，2027年未必就是盈利终点。

2）下一轮周期底部是不是会显著高于过去？
LTA、预付款、价格底线和低库存，会降低过去那种“价格暴跌—库存爆仓—巨额亏损”的概率。

3）估值逻辑需要从峰值利润转向正常化利润
未来会长时间维持正常会利润率（而非峰值利润），那么意味着营收利润的体量能稳步向上。

这三点被确认，估值扩张也就来了。当然即使没有估值扩张，单纯盈利增长也能把股价慢慢往上推，只是说估值扩张才会带来暴力行情。8月初关于存储的思考推文：
 https://t.co/0T6uwtpCc2

author: bubbleboi
quoted_text:
We are terminating Chris Degnan for unethical conduct involving Cognition.

The last few months have seen incredible progress in AI capabilities. San Francisco has flourished as new companies that solve new, more ambitious problems are finding great success. Generally, it is a wonderful time to be building.

We at @FactoryAI have seen overwhelming interest in our model-agnostic coding agents and our software factory product. Our team has 10x’d in size, while our revenue has 100x’d year over year. This momentum has been unprecedented.

A much larger competitor, Cognition (makers of Devin) has fallen behind us on the capabilities that matter most to customers: cost, quality, and security. Instead of competing in the market, Cognition engineers feigned interviews with us to pry information about our product. Not finding what they were looking for, Cognition has decided to throw their weight and money at people with direct knowledge of our most confidential plans.

It feels as though ethics is being thrown out of the window in the AI era. People are willing to do anything, including exploiting privileged information and violating ethical boundaries. I think this is unique to our time, and I don’t think it’s right. Integrity still matters.

Yesterday, I made the decision to immediately terminate Christopher Degnan’s roles as a Board Observer and Advisor to Factory, after over a year of service.

Prior to this decision, Chris told me he had a casual conversation with an executive at Cognition AI. When I questioned his intentions, he reassured me that ethics aside, he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which I trusted and believed.

On Monday, Chris spent time advising the Factory team on a handful of confidential board-level matters. That evening, he called me to say that the conversation that was initially described as casual and one-off was actually formal and recurring. For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light.

It is sad to sever a relationship with someone who has been a trusted advisor - and even a close friend -  for over a year. But Chris’s conduct is unacceptable to me. Trust in Board Membership is one of the sacred bonds in the Silicon Valley, one that helps the startup ecosystem thrive. With it comes an enormous responsibility. That trust was violated.

Competition is good. I respect and in many cases admire our competitors. San Francisco is a beautiful, singular place where the bold and ambitious go to defy the norms and precedents of the past. But certain principles that must remain. Violating ethics to seek advantage turns what should be positive-sum into zero-sum.

We all love technology. And we all love to compete. But we must hold ourselves to a higher standard. The future of software engineering comes with abundance that will impact every person on Earth. Building that future comes with immense responsibility. We must build and compete with integrity.

text: What motives Mamdani is the same thing that motivated young Obama - to ascend to the ranks of the global elite. The right debates whether he's an islamist in communist clothing or the other way around, when the more mundane explanation is that he's a striver, like all of us, and seeks relevence and power above all else. He likely thought he would spend his life as a middling DSA apparatchik, and so his luxury beliefs about global intifadas or wealth redistribution or racial reparations cost him nothing to maintain. He then fell into one of the most powerful political positions in the world at near terminal velocity, a rise not unlike Obama's in the mid 00s. He has now adjusted expecations, reoriented himself around the idea that he has the rare opportunity to leave an actual legacy and aquire control. Multiple mayorships, a run for governor, the cultural figurehead of the entire democratic party. His gestures toward Trump, the Jews, and his retractions of previously radical stances (arresting Bibi etc) aren't two faced 5D chess moves, but the rational calculations of someone who has outgrown juvenile revolutionary leftism, with all it's romantic allure, and tasted real power.  Obama's radicalism was interrogated as well; his middle name, his asssociations, his youthful activism, but in the end he proved a stunningly vacant figure with no real beliefs or interiority. In a sense, those embarassing summer playlists he releases are the truest thing about him - a collage of meaningless signifiers authored by one in particular. Obama's vapidity has been most apparent in old age, wherein he persues no agenda and champions no cause, instead hanging out with Gen X idols like Bruce Springstein and producing somewhat bingeable TV miniseries for Netflix and HBO. He got what he wanted, to rise for rising's sake, and Mamdani will meet the same fate. The the thing to follow, also in parallel to Obama, will be the loyalty of his wife, who will have to decide weather she is actually a kiffeyah-laden rebel, or the first lady of the empire's central city. I expect the seductive status of the second to overwhelm the sentimentality of the first.

text:
MetaMask刚刚含糊其辞的披露遭到了安全攻击，但是却没有明确说到底发生了什么，只给出了两个信息，一是部分基础设施受到影响，二是防御措施是主动退出验证节点，并且随后Lido等ETH质押项目也相继发布公告，那通过这些支离破碎的信息推演一下可能发生了什么？
至少能明确这次安全事件和MetaMask钱包本身没有关系，而是和质押业务有关，所以才会紧急退出验证节点。
如果是验证节点出现问题，那最大的风险就是用户的质押资金被盗，但根据披露的信息目前来看被盗的可能性不大，因为以太坊的质押设计里，验证权限和提款权线是分开的，用户质押资金出钱，而验证者只负责干活，并且MetaMask强调其节点是非托管的，不托管资金也不管理密钥，所以MetaMask本身被攻击也不会影响资金安全。
那就只有一种可能，验证者干活这部分出了问题，比如验证者的签名密钥泄漏，导致无法正常出块和投票，进一步触发罚没机制导致质押资金受损，以及目前以太坊绝大多数验证节点的工作环境全部都在AWS等中心化的Web2云端，所以也可能是云端服务器被攻击入侵。
不过总体来说和资金安全影响不大，即使节点无法正常工作，资金提取不会受到影响，更多的是影响以太坊整个网络的运行安全。
不过值得一提的是，就在今年7月MetaMask母公司披露了曾经有朝鲜黑客潜伏进去工作了一段时间，当你家里发现一只蟑螂时，那已经有一窝祖孙三代了。

text:
A lot of you have been asking me about $ARTHUR, so I spent some time digging deeper into it today

Over the past few days, I’ve checked quite a few new memes, but I skipped most of them because the bundles were too heavy, the distribution looked bad, or there simply wasn’t enough of a narrative worth following

$ARTHUR is one of the first ones I’ve seen recently that looks decent enough for me to dig deeper

Just to be clear, this is still a memecoin. There’s no special utility or product behind it. My thesis here is mainly based on the character, the artist, distribution, and attention

1. Arthur existed before the token

This is the first thing I like about it

Arthur wasn’t created just to launch a coin. He’s a character created by Hakes, @imhakes, and was already being built through @byhakes on Instagram before $ARTHUR existed

The concept is extremely simple :

Just a normal guy. Sometimes you are Arthur

He works, drinks coffee, hates Mondays, waits for Friday, makes some questionable decisions over the weekend, regrets them on Sunday, then goes back to work on Monday

It’s almost anti-lore

No superhero story, no fantasy universe, no complicated backstory. Arthur simply reflects the everyday life that a lot of people can relate to

That relatability is what makes the character easy to use as a meme, reaction, or PFP even without any connection to crypto

2. Culture first, token later

This is where it gets more interesting

Arthur was already going viral before $ARTHUR existed

@byhakes started pushing Arthur around early August. According to Hakes himself, the page grew to roughly 450K to 500K followers in around 40 days

So the flow here was basically :

Character => Culture => Audience => Token

Not launch a token first and then build a character and narrative around it afterward

Before $ARTHUR, there were already community tokens using Hakes’ artwork. But Hakes never claimed those as his official token

That changed on September 29

@imhakes directly came out and said :

A character, a culture, now a project

Meet $ARTHUR 

My official token 

That’s the important part for me

This isn’t the community attaching an artist to a narrative and claiming he supports it. The creator himself is directly claiming the token

3. Hakes also locked part of the supply

After launch, @imhakes locked around 36.7M $ARTHUR for one year, roughly 3.67% of the total supply

I don’t think 3.67% is enough to guarantee anything

But at least the artist didn’t just make one post and completely step away. He locked part of his bag for a relatively long period

One thing I want to make clear :

Those 36.7M tokens are simply locked. They are not rewards for holders

At the moment, I haven’t seen any holder rewards, fee sharing, or STONK airdrop attached to $ARTHUR, so I’m not including any holder yield in my thesis

4. On-chain is what initially caught my attention

This is actually what made me stop and take a closer look at $ARTHUR 

I’ve skipped quite a few memes recently because their bundles were simply too heavy

For $ARTHUR, at the time I checked :

Mint authority is gone

Freeze authority is gone

Dev holdings are close to 0%

Snipers are close to 0%

Bundle is around 0.4% to 0.6%

Top 10 holders are around 19%

Compared with many of the new coins I’ve been checking lately, the distribution at least looks much healthier

Of course, cleaner on-chain data does not mean the coin is safe

This is still a low-cap memecoin, and a few large wallets exiting can move the chart very quickly

5. The $ARTHUR meta isn’t completely new

If you’ve been trading memes for a while, this setup should look pretty familiar

A character or artwork goes viral

The community starts paying attention

A token appears

Then the creator gets directly involved

The creator coin meta has already existed before. With $ARTHUR, if there are creator fees involved, they belong to the creator/platform mechanism rather than being holder yield. I’m not including fees in my thesis

What matters more to me is that the character already had an audience before the token existed, and this time Hakes himself is claiming the token

$ARTHUR launched through StonkFun and is paired with $STONK, but I see that mainly as part of the launch structure rather than a standalone catalyst

So my thesis is pretty simple :

Character existed before the token

Audience existed before the token

The artist is directly involved

On-chain currently looks relatively clean

Attention is still there

6. Hakes’ audience is still the biggest catalyst

This is what I’ll be watching the most

Arthur currently has an Instagram audience of roughly 450K to 500K, while the token only has a few thousand on-chain holders

That gap can be both the opportunity and the risk

If @byhakes starts putting $ARTHUR and the CA directly in front of his existing audience through stories, reels, or new content, there’s still a large amount of attention that hasn’t converted on-chain yet

But 500K followers does not mean 500K buyers

A lot of those people may simply like Arthur as a meme and have zero interest in crypto

So I care much more about actual conversion than the follower count itself

Another thing I’m watching is whether a real PFP culture starts forming around Arthur

If Arthur starts appearing across CT through avatars, memes, and remixes, the narrative becomes much less dependent on Hakes personally pushing the token every day

7. Chart and my plan

$ARTHUR already had a strong move from launch and reached an ATH around $2.6M to $2.8M before correcting 

When I last checked, MC was sitting around $1.7M to $1.8M

Volume is still very high relative to the market cap

That tells me attention is still there, but it also means capital is rotating very quickly. This isn’t the kind of chart I want to FOMO into after a green candle

If we get a deeper dip, the first area I’m interested in is 

$1.2M to $1.6M MC

But I’m not automatically buying just because it reaches that range

If price dips there while holders continue growing, volume remains healthy, and both @imhakes and @arthurisonchain stay active, then the risk/reward becomes much more interesting to me

If $1.2M fails, then $800K to $1M is the last defense area I’ll be watching

At that point, I’ll be paying very close attention to holder flow and Hakes’ activity

If MC breaks $800K and fails to reclaim it, especially while holders are dropping, volume is drying up, and the creator goes quiet, I’ll cut

My plan is simple :

Dip : $1.2M to $1.6M

Last defense : $800K to $1M

Cut : below $800K if it fails to reclaim

If the chart keeps running without giving a dip, I’m not going to chase it either. The first thing I want to see on the upside is a reclaim of the $2.6M to $2.8M ATH area.

8. What I’m watching next

With a creator coin like $ARTHUR, one red candle worries me less than the creator disappearing

There are mainly four things I’m watching :

text:
BTC为什么跌不下去？这应该是最近很多小伙伴内心的纠结。

4个月前，微策略仅仅卖出32枚BTC，就把市场吓趴了-20%。而现在却顶着us10y 5.2%，重启加息，各种利空打击却愣是不跌。

不得不说，才短短几个月，世道就变了......

其根本原因是当前的卖压不够强烈。卖方枯竭时，需求弱就横盘，需求强就拉盘。而“卖方衰竭指数”就是一个衡量供应强度的指标。

我首次分享该指标是在今年的8月11日（见引文），当时指标进入了“极端衰竭区”（红色虚线）。BTC在$63,000左右徘徊。

回头看，这是本轮熊市最后也是最好的进场机会。

因为历史数据显示，一旦BTC走出熊底，该指标就很难再回到极值区，或给出这么明确的买入信号。

当然，此后会有多次掉入绿色区的情况（绿色虚线），这表示卖方相对较弱。此时仅仅靠BTC的内生因素无法让其再大幅下挫。

除非同时叠加外部力量的共同推动。

内生因素包括链上动能衰减，活跃度下降，资金背离等等；虽然这些都可以限制短期上涨的空间，但由于卖压不强，下跌的幅度也会比较有限。

前段时间当BTC回调到$75K时，指标就进入了绿色区，这或许也是一次比较好机会，而这几天指标又回升了一点。

至于它还会不会再掉到红色区？其实没有人知道。

至少现在看来，8月11日推文中说“当前已经建仓的没有错；等下次信号出现再建仓的也没错”这句话可能是错的。

无视机会出现，选择等待下一次的风险是万一没有下一次。

有花堪折直须折，莫待花落空折枝......

what did we think would happen? what actually happened? what did we get wrong?

remembering everything is useless if you don’t know which memories are actually valuable.

the agent wouldn’t just have memory, it would learn which memories are useful.

3: Make sure its memory is actually true

markets change constantly.

revenue guidance changes. tokenomics change. valuations change. narratives change.

I would use validity-aware memory so my agents know when information is outdated, updated or completely wrong.

this is where it gets ridiculous.

if my crypto agent misses a major token unlock I don’t just want it to remember:

“i missed the token unlock”

I want the mistake to change how it researches every future token.

mistake = a lesson = a new research rule = a new test to improve the agent.

having 5 agents agreeing with each other is pointless if they’re basically the same agent 5 times.

I would have bull, bear, quant, risk and research agents investigate independently BEFORE seeing what the others think.

then let them argue with eachother, let them call eachother a dumb fuck. I want a trading floor.

6: Prove the firm is actually getting better

finally I would build my own benchmark.

every time I change the system I want to know:

> did research accuracy improve?
> did it miss less important information?
> did it make fewer unsupported claims?
> did it actually make better decisions?

combine all six and you don’t really have an AI trading bot anymore.

text: Update on $LIBRA class action - thrown out. No Rico.
author: martypartymusic
quoted_text:
🚨 Hayden Davis, Ben Chow, Kelsier, and Meteora just beat the $LIBRA / $M3M3 class action.

Not after a trial. After an 81-page opinion.

Judge Rochon dismissed the ENTIRE case with prejudice. You cannot RICO a six-month memecoin launch. You cannot sue a Solana DEX as if it were a partnership. And “Milei posted it” is not a fraud claim against the guy who built the liquidity pool.

This was the SDNY class action over the December 2024 $M3M3 launch and the February 2025 $LIBRA token - the one tied to Javier Milei’s “Viva La Libertad” post. Plaintiffs also tried to pull in $MELANIA and other launches in a proposed second amended complaint.

The story in the complaint if you can recall, is cinematic. Insiders allegedly freeze the pool, fill wallets before the public can buy, inflate the cap, dump, and leave retail with a 90% crash. One named plaintiff lost about $19,000 on $M3M3. The other bought $LIBRA on launch day.

The court never decided whether that happened.

It decided plaintiffs sued the wrong thing, under the wrong statute, with the wrong facts.

Meteora is not a defendant. 

Dynamic Labs intervened and said Meteora is software. The court agreed plaintiffs never pleaded a real unincorporated association - no identified members, no president or treasurer, no mutual consent to a common objective. Calling a protocol a “team” does not make it suable. 

All claims against Meteora are gone.

RICO is gone. 

Closed-ended continuity needs a substantial period. Six months of token launches is not enough. Adding $MELANIA / $ENRON / $TRUST in the proposed amendment stretched it to about seven. Still not enough. Open-ended continuity also fails: Meteora and Kelsier are alleged as primarily legitimate businesses, and wire fraud is not inherently a criminal way of life. No pattern, no RICO, no RICO conspiracy.

Fraud against Chow is gone. Rule 9(b) scienter. Profit is not motive. A post-crash “I f*cked up because I enabled the guy” is not a strong inference he intended to defraud buyers on day one. 

Conspiracy dies with the underlying tort.

Kelsier is gone on jurisdiction. Once RICO drops, there is no nationwide service hook, and New York long-arm does not reach the Davis family on these facts.

Leave to amend: denied as futile. Case closed.

The takeaway is not “memecoins are legal.” The takeaway is that a viral launch plus a famous tweet is still not a RICO enterprise, and you cannot name the smart contracts as Defendant No. 5.

text:
Moneyness is an emergent property. Money is a Schelling point for value storage, exchange, and accounting.

A system of coinage may achieve Moneyness if a growing network of people use it to store, exchange, and account for a stable or increasing amount of value over time.

Storing value requires credible security. Exchanging value benefits from speed, ease, and flexibility. Accounting benefits from neutral immutability and lindyness.

Digital money has some key benefits: neutral security can be proven, transfer can occur globally and quickly, and smart contracts can provide flexible, programmable constructs for interacting with value.

Digital coins aiming at achieving Moneyness have converged to two primary shapes:
- PoW, hard-capped supply coins with no pre-mine
- PoS, pre-mined coins with flexible supply, inflation with burn mechanics to offset

Moneyness is built up over time by a network of people using a coin; it isn’t achieved overnight.

I strongly believe that PoW-shaped networks are the best candidates for global acceptance as Money.

I began working on $NOCK back in 2023. I modeled the @Nockchain design after my good friend (Akis Kattis)’s 2020 research paper called Proof of Necessary Work, which imagined a PoUW network built on top of Zero Knowledge Proofs.

Our team launched @Nockchain with no pre-mine in May of 2025, and we quickly became the largest ZK-proving network in the world (though the proofs being generated are not yet used by the network).

We’re moving quickly toward privacy and programmability, all built on the same Proofs that secure the network.

This summer we launched our AI Compute Network, which has 25 ExaMAC/s of compute and is presently merge-mining ~55% of Pearl blocks. We’re continuing research on making the AI Compute Network into useful verifiable inference.

I’m happy to see more teams joining the Proof of Useful Work space. It’s good for the future of crypto for attention to be moving toward this important area of research.

The question of Moneyness is a long game and will play out over time. Really, these economic experiments will be proven out through distribution over the course of years and decades.

text:
In our internal update this week I wrote a sentence that annoyed me, because it was true: the content pipeline is thin, because the roadmap is mostly infrastructure improvements and honestly infrastructure doesn't amplify well.

Here's what that "thin" week actually contained:
- The team root-caused a mystery slowdown that had resisted explanation for a week. 
- They cut the time it takes us to detect a failing component from about a minute to seconds. 
- They retired old systems so cleanly nobody noticed. 

By engineering standards, one of our best weeks of the quarter. 

By marketing standards, nothing happened.

That's the trap for anyone building infrastructure: attention rewards launches, but trust is built by the absence of events. 

Your announceable work and your important work are two different lists. 

If you let amplification steer the roadmap, you ship demos and starve the substrate. 

And the customers you most want (the ones with real money on the line) are precisely the ones who judge you on the boring weeks, because they're the ones who notice that nothing broke.

Applause tracks what you ship. 

Trust tracks what never breaks. 

Build for the second and let the first arrive late.

text:
Next phase of our build.

Introducing the Anyroute Agent Economy. $ANYR 

Agents are starting to hold wallets, pay for services, trade, negotiate, and act for people, teams, and treasuries.

The problem is that most of them are being given money before they are given rules.

An agent should not have unlimited access because it has a private key. It should work inside clear limits set by its owner: what it can spend, where it can spend it, which assets and venues it can use, when it needs approval, and when it needs to stop.

That is what we are building.

Private agent accounts with hard budgets and scoped permissions. Mandates that define what an agent is allowed to do. Private payments that do not turn every service call into a public history. Escrowed agreements for agents doing work for each other.

Trading is part of it too, but this is bigger than agentic trading.

Before an agent swaps, transfers, opens a position, or moves capital, the action can be checked against its policy, simulated, and compared against multiple price sources. If a price looks wrong, liquidity is thin, or limits are hit, it does not execute.

Every action leaves a receipt.

The owner stays in control. The agent gets room to work. The public does not need to see everything.

Not an agent with a wallet and a hope.

An agent economy with rules.

quoted_text:
Hey everyone,

First, I'm honestly blown away by everything that's been happening lately. We can't thank our traders and supporters enough, truly. My team and I have been working on Vest for almost five years now. We are traders ourselves who started Vest because we thought we could build the product we all wanted to use ourselves. We spent years doing open-source research for the betterment of the industry (https://t.co/XEVvJIPVP3), often with no one watching. We pivoted dozens of times. We were told over and over again that what we were doing wouldn't work, that it was impossible, that we should give up, sell, walk away. We faced rejection, after rejection, after rejection. There were days it felt like no one believed in this but us. So to see all of that work, all of those late nights and hard calls, finally turn into something traders actually love and use every day is extremely humbling. It means more to us than I can put into words. Truly, thank you.

Second, I want to address the allegations of wash trading head on head-on, because they come from a HUGE misunderstanding of how our product is different from other perp DEXs. We're not just another perps dex, but also a funded account platform. In fact the large majority of our traders use funded accounts. When they do, they can get up to $25k accounts for as little as $210. They can then open positions of up to $1.25M notional on some markets like ES and NQ. These accounts have a daily loss and drawdown limit, so most traders trade shorter-horizon and flip positions often. If they pass their evaluation phase, their trades are in “live” mode and get shown in the A-book where they trade against other traders and market participants. Because of the nature of the high implicit leverage and max drawdowns, that usually leads to high volume and low OI behavior on the live market.

This is now accurately displayed on ALL OFFICIAL Vest platforms. We’ve gone through a few iterations of the front end to move away from combined 24H volume. Previously, if you hovered over the volume number on Vest, you can see the breakdown of eval and live volume. To make it even more obvious, we now explicitly display both at all times. In our API’s we now very clearly separate and document our eval and live volume. If anyone has feedback on how to make this clearer, our team is always here to listen.

Part of the confusion is what is shown on official Vest platforms and what is not. We cannot control what third party aggregators use to display us. Some of them are also using information from an old outdated exchange that we are deprecating. We also cannot control if they decide to put us in the same comparison with other perp DEXs where the product offering is fundamentally different. I also take some blame for not reaching out to all aggregators beforehand and making sure that everything is up to date, but there are hundreds of aggregators out there, and I hope you’ll excuse me on this front.

It is our belief that the perpetual future is the best asset class for retail traders to trade with. It has been our goal, and vision, to onboard the rest of the world - the futures traders, the CFD traders, the options traders and more - onto this form factor that we believe is ultimately better for them. We believe that funded accounts are the best way to learn and trade with this new form factor because it lowers the barrier to entry.

We have been extremely blessed beyond belief to achieve this mission. If you search up vestexchange on twitter, we have thousands of traders from traditional finance that have never traded perps, receiving payouts and expressing really positive feedback on our platform. Many of the feedback is that “we are too good to be true” because our rules are so trader friendly. I will continue to answer all feedback and hopefully continue to help explain anything people are uncertain about.

Like all other platforms and exchanges, affiliates receive a commission on referrals. Some partners also have content creation and partnership deals, but these are few and far between and we ask all of our affiliates to disclose when posting. Candidly, we also don’t really want to burden our balance sheet with 5 or 6 figure retainer deals because that value should be passed onto traders in any way we can.

For those who haven’t tried out Vest. I would love to onboard you! For those who are FUDDing Vest (mostly competitors), I would ALSO love to onboard you and for you to see why we’ve achieved such fast growth! It is our goal to build the best platform for retail traders, and I am glad that our product is putting pressure for innovation in this space.

text:
SK하이닉스 "솔리다임 IPO 결정된 사항 없어. 판단 기준은 장기 주주가치"

1. SK하이닉스가 10월 1일 뉴스룸 팩트 게시물을 통해 솔리다임 관련 최근 보도에 대한 입장을 밝혔다. 최근 언론에서는 솔리다임 자본 활용 방안을 '중복상장'과 연결해 기존 주주가치 훼손 우려를 제기해왔다.

2. 회사는 앞서 공시에서 밝힌 대로 솔리다임 경쟁력 강화 방안을 검토 중이나 확정된 사항은 없으며, 이는 지금도 마찬가지라고 설명했다.

3. 솔리다임은 인텔 NAND·SSD 사업 인수 과정에서 출범했으며, 업황 악화로 어려운 시기를 거쳐 현재는 AI 데이터센터용 고용량 eSSD 중심으로 사업을 전개하고 있다. 회사는 생산능력과 기술 경쟁력 확보를 위한 투자 필요성을 지속 검토 중이다.

4. 투자재원 마련 방안도 정해지지 않았다. 회사는 재무여력을 갖추고 있어 자체 자금 활용도 검토할 수 있지만, 자금이 있다는 것이 모든 투자를 자체 자금으로 하는 것이 최선이라는 뜻은 아니라고 강조했다. HBM, 서버용 DRAM, eSSD 등 전체 투자 수요를 고려해 자원을 배분해야 한다는 설명이다.

5. 다만 판단 기준은 분명히 했다. 외부 자본 활용 방안은 자체 자금 활용 대비 기존 주주의 경제적 가치에 미치는 영향을 충분히 따져 판단하겠다고 밝혔다.

6. 향후 구체적 방안을 검토할 경우 이사회 차원에서 재무적·사업적 영향을 면밀히 살피고, 기존 주주 영향과 주주보호 방안도 함께 검토해 충분히 설명하겠다고 덧붙였다.

如果六月初有人跟你說，接下來幾個月 30 年期美債殖利率會從 5% 左右一路衝到接近 5.6%，但 BTC 反而會從 71K 漲到 84K，你一定會覺得這個人瘋了。

因為照一般邏輯，長端殖利率越高，黃金、BTC 這類非生息資產面臨的壓力就越大。

但物極必反，長債殖利率持續往上，也代表市場對美債要求的風險溢價越來越高，背後反映的是對美國財政紀律越來越深的疑慮。

所以現在的長債殖利率，很像一根越拉越緊的橡皮筋。

在它斷掉以前，殖利率越高，對黃金跟 BTC 的壓制力就越強。近期黃金已經明顯承壓，BTC 相對卻強得多。

但如果市場最後開始交易「財政赤字持續惡化，龐大的債務終究需要更寬鬆的貨幣環境來消化」，那就等於這根橡皮筋被拉到極限後斷掉了。

原本壓制黃金跟 BTC 的高殖利率，反而會因為背後代表的財政問題，變成下一階段行情的燃料。

美債的信用與財政問題，Ray Dalio 已經喊很多年了。

只是這幾年 AI 帶來龐大的資本支出、生產力預期與企業獲利，讓全球資金持續流向美國，替這個問題爭取了更多時間。

目前的資產市場，其實同時跑著一條主線跟一條暗線。

主線是 AI 推動的成長與生產力革命，暗線是愈來愈龐大的赤字、利息支出與政府債務。

前者對應 AI 股、半導體股，後者對應黃金跟 BTC。

老實說，長債殖利率走到這裡已經開始出現一些失控的味道。

通膨預期在改善，長端殖利率卻還是一路往上。5% 以上的殖利率照理說已經很有吸引力，市場卻依然持續拋售長債、要求更高的風險補償。

如果連這種殖利率都吸引不到足夠的長期買盤，代表那條原本藏在水面下的財政暗線，正在慢慢浮上來。

而一旦市場真的開始全面交易這條暗線，黃金跟 BTC 的大牛行情，才剛要開始。

quoted_text:
Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

https://t.co/bZZU5oNlWp

A full investigation is underway, and further updates will be shared as they become available. For further details, please refer to the MetaMask Staking release linked below.
